heading: Burgwallen-Nieuwe Zijde
text: **AC-01. Rokin 72, De Gouden Bril and its Zacharias Jansen.** Pin 52.370420, 4.892281; Rokin 72 corner Wijde Kapelsteeg (the statue is on the steeg side). An optician's building of 1918 for "De Gouden Bril" (Schmidt Optiek, founded 1866, here since the 1870s per WinkelStories), with a standing figure by Dirk Polet of Zacharias Jansen, the Middelburg spectacle maker some credit with the first microscope and telescope, on the side wall; the gable stones show a pince-nez and monocle and the arms of Prince Bernhard. A shop front that advertises a claim to an invention. Local voice: vanderkrogt.net calls it the oldest optician's shop in the city (check). Lead: https://nl.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rokin_72 ; second https://www.vanderkrogt.net/standbeelden/object.php?record=NH03ad (record URL to confirm) and https://www.winkelstories.nl (Schmidt). Status: building and statue standing; shop still Schmidt per vanderkrogt (date not seen; check). Caveat: "inventor" is disputed (Lipperhey); say "claimed". Listed? check. Rank **Nice**. New place. The Mirakelkolom (dropped by DC) stands on the same address.
title: Rokin 72, De Gouden Bril and its Zacharias Jansen
rank_text: Rank **Nice**. New place. The Mirakelkolom (dropped by DC) stands on the same address.

heading: Burgwallen-Nieuwe Zijde
text: **AC-02. Nieuwendijk 89, the photographer's front with Daguerre and Niépce.** Pin 52.376774, 4.896645. A shop front designed by Gerrit van Arkel for the portrait photographer Albert Greiner (already twenty years at this address), with a frieze of putti taking photographs and medallions of the two inventors of photography, Daguerre and Niépce, between cheese and sweet shops. Local voice: Parool, "Niet lachen naar het vogeltje: chique fotograaf A. Greiner" (20 May 2023); VVAB Binnenstad piece "De oudste fotoateliers van Amsterdam" (Wilfred van Leeuwen). Lead: https://amsterdamopdekaart.nl (Nieuwendijk 89); gevelstenen.net (portraits, putti); Parool 2023. Status: front intact (Parool 2023). Caveat: date of the front to confirm (Van Arkel, c. 1890s?). Rank **Nice**. New place.
title: Nieuwendijk 89, the photographer's front with Daguerre and Niépce

heading: Burgwallen-Nieuwe Zijde
text: **AC-03. Sint Luciënsteeg, the gable stone wall.** Pin approx 52.369800, 4.890700 (north wall of the Amsterdam Museum in the Sint Luciënsteeg, by the little square after no. 25; fix on site). About 47 gable stones rescued from demolished houses are set in the outer wall and around the square: a milkmaid of 1603, "De Corendrager" 1626, three black moles, the town of Ulm (1672), a monk, an emperor and a peasant who say "I teach, I protect, I work for these two", a skater in a landscape. Most belong to the Koninklijk Oudheidkundig Genootschap's collection, lent to the museum. Local voice: nickname "Gevelsteenmuseum" (M for Amsterdam). Lead: https://kog.nu (Collectie gevelstenen); gevelstenen.net (47 stones listed, postcode 1012PM); https://mforamsterdam.com/sint-luciensteeg . Status: wall in place; the museum is being rebuilt (ONH, Nov 2026), so check access to the alley. Caveat: beside A-list Amsterdam Museum, pitched on the free street wall. Rank **Nice**. New place.
title: Sint Luciënsteeg, the gable stone wall

heading: Burgwallen-Nieuwe Zijde
text: **AC-04. The neon HELP in the Voetboogstraat (Joes Kloppenburg).** Pin 52.368269, 4.890682. On 17 August 1996 Joes Kloppenburg (26) was beaten to death here by four drunk young men while trying to stop them; his death made "zinloos geweld" a national cause. A plaque in the paving (text with Martin Reints) tells the night minute by minute, and the word HELP in neon hangs between two fronts above it, "om nooit te wennen aan geweld" (Volkskrant 1997, the first commemoration, 300 people). Makers: Vendel & De Wolf (vendelendewolf.nl) for the Amsterdams Fonds voor de Kunst; Kunstwacht credits Sandra de Wolf. Lead: https://nl.wikipedia.org/wiki/Monument_voor_Joes_Kloppenburg ; second https://feitjes.amsterdam (2022). Status: present 2022 (feitjes). Rank **Nice**. New place.
title: The neon HELP in the Voetboogstraat (Joes Kloppenburg)

heading: Burgwallen-Nieuwe Zijde
text: **AC-05. Een zeegezicht aan het IJ, the tiled cycle tunnel.** Pin 52.379235, 4.898193 (Cuyperspassage under Centraal Station). Irma Boom covered the floor-to-ceiling walls of the 2015 cyclists' and walkers' tunnel with about 70,000 hand-painted Tichelaar tiles after an 18th-century tableau by the Rotterdam painter Cornelis Boumeester of the herring fleet; the picture grows sketchier toward the IJ side, and Boom swapped the Rotterdam arms on the ship for three Amsterdam crosses. Lead: Kunstwacht (object 576); nl.wikipedia list of statues (2015). Status: in use. Caveat: BC dropped the Cuyperspassage as "part of Centraal Station"; I propose it on the artwork (and the Rotterdam joke), not the station. Rank **Nice**. New place.
title: Een zeegezicht aan het IJ, the tiled cycle tunnel

heading: Burgwallen-Nieuwe Zijde
text: **AC-06. Art under Centraal Station: tomorrow's weather and a mosaic seen through peepholes.** Pin 52.378257, 4.900489 (metro hall under CS). David Claerbout's "Weather Engine" (2018) is a computer-made landscape whose weather is tomorrow's forecast, fed live from the internet, with a figure going about his seasons; in the Kamperbrug metro entrance Joost van Roojen's granite mosaic (a gift from Dutch Railways when the east line opened in 1980) survives behind air vents put up for tunnel safety in 2013, with peepholes cut so it can still be seen (52.378077, 4.900375); Jennifer Tee's "Tulip Palepai" (2017) is made from scans of 100,000 tulip petals. Lead: Kunstwacht objects 1162, 1169, 1186. Status: in place (Kunstwacht). Rank **Okay**. New place (group of three).
title: Art under Centraal Station: tomorrow's weather and a mosaic seen through peepholes

heading: Burgwallen-Nieuwe Zijde
text: **AC-07. Canvas van Amsterdam on the Haringpakkersbrug.** Pin 52.379409, 4.895415. Since April 2026 a big steel panel on the side of the bridge by Centraal Station gets a new work by an Amsterdam artist twice a year; the first, FreelingWaters' "Vreemdeling welkom" in herring-cart style (Dutch flag, Gothic letters, gulls instead of crosses), faced a row of rough sleepers and the rolling suitcases. Lead: Kunstwacht object 7481. Status: first work up to end of August 2026; the current one not checked. Caveat: changing work, describe the frame. Rank **Okay**. New place or Look for in a Haringpakkerstoren/Singel-head place (BC-03).
title: Canvas van Amsterdam on the Haringpakkersbrug
rank_text: Rank **Okay**. New place or Look for in a Haringpakkerstoren/Singel-head place (BC-03).

heading: Burgwallen-Nieuwe Zijde
text: **AC-08. The UvA's word works on the Spui: Weiner's books in the paving.** Pin 52.368852, 4.890407. Lawrence Weiner's "Een vertaling van de ene taal naar de andere" (1996): three book shapes lying face down in the square, in Dutch with English, Arabic and Sranan; first cut in hard stone, too fragile, recast in iron. It belongs to the university's "Gevelproject" with Joseph Kosuth's "Located Text" (quotations on the fronts of the Oudemanhuispoort and other UvA buildings, see the Paul Scholten project PDF) and a Karel Appel painting. Lead: Kunstwacht object 520; https://straatpoezie.nl/gedicht/een-vertaling . Status: in place (OSM). Caveat: Kosuth's texts mostly sit on OZ buildings; DC-37 (Lieverdje) is on the same square. Rank **Okay**. New place or Look for in DC-37.
title: The UvA's word works on the Spui: Weiner's books in the paving
rank_text: Rank **Okay**. New place or Look for in DC-37.

heading: Burgwallen-Nieuwe Zijde
text: **AC-09. The White Cube in the Nieuwezijds Armsteeg.** Pin 52.377084, 4.895910. Residents tired of public urinating, vandalism and graffiti in this alley asked for art; housing association De Key commissioned Giny Vos, who clad a whole front in ribbed aluminium with an LED line drawing of a museum room in perspective, lit at night. Lead: Kunstwacht object 569. Status: not checked (check: Still there?). Caveat: BC-35 covers the Armsteeg's dike history; group there if preferred. Rank **Okay**. Group with BC-35.
title: The White Cube in the Nieuwezijds Armsteeg

heading: Burgwallen-Oude Zijde
text: **AC-10. The red window of the Oude Kerk ("Het Rode Raam").** Pin 52.374394, 4.897928 (seen from the alley off the Oudekerksplein). Giorgio Andreotta Calò's "Anastasis" (2018) turned one window of the Holy Sepulchre chapel permanently red, throwing red light into the church from the Red Light District; the VVAB and another heritage society went to court to keep the white glass, the judge let it go ahead in August 2018 and the court called it "een gepaste kunstuiting" in March 2020. Lead: Kunstwacht object 2764; https://www.parool.nl (11 Mar 2020) and https://www.nrc.nl/nieuws/2018/09/27/ . Status: in place (court 2020; Kunstwacht). Caveat: beside A-list Oude Kerk, pitched on the fight; visible from outside. Rank **Nice**. New place.
title: The red window of the Oude Kerk ("Het Rode Raam")

heading: Burgwallen-Oude Zijde
text: **AC-11. Rokin station: the archaeologists' wall and Manders' fountain.** Pin 52.369703, 4.892149 (Rokin station; the fountain is at 52.372188, 4.893052 on the Rokin). Between the escalators of Noord/Zuidlijn station Rokin a long vitrine shows thousands of finds from the metro dig, laid out by shape and colour rather than date by the artists Dewar & Gicquel with city archaeologist Jerzy Gawronski, facing their own mosaics of everyday things (a crocodile, a melodica, a high-heeled pump). Up on the street Mark Manders' Rokinfontein (2017) has two rough joined heads looking away from each other, made to look as if it had always been there (water off in winter). Lead: Kunstwacht objects 1167, 585; https://belowthesurface.amsterdam . Status: in place. Caveat: DC listed the fountain as a lead for theme A; the station itself is in NZ, the fountain in OZ. Rank **Nice**. New place.
title: Rokin station: the archaeologists' wall and Manders' fountain

heading: Burgwallen-Oude Zijde
text: **AC-12. Queen Wilhelmina on horseback, paid for by Amsterdam women.** Pin 52.369168, 4.892252; Rokin corner Langebrugsteeg. Theresia van der Pant's young Wilhelmina in a hat (1972) came about on the initiative of the city's women's organisations and was paid for by Amsterdammers; Queen Juliana advised the sculptor, who mostly made animals. Lead: Kunstwacht object 515. Rank **Okay**. New place, or Look for in AC-11.
title: Queen Wilhelmina on horseback, paid for by Amsterdam women
rank_text: Rank **Okay**. New place, or Look for in AC-11.

heading: Nieuwmarkt/Lastage
text: **AC-13. "De Lastage 1971", the gable stone of a boarded-up neighbourhood.** Pin 52.372226, 4.903083; Recht Boomssloot 42. A gable stone of 1971 shows houses with their windows nailed shut: the Lastage as it looked when the city was buying and closing houses for the metro and the planned motorway, the years of the Nieuwmarkt fight. Local voice: Parool/AD "Zoekplaatje" (November, year to fix) used it as a city quiz. Lead: gevelstenen.net (Recht Boomssloot 42, "dichtgespijkerde woonwijk, DE LASTAGE 1971"); https://www.ad.nl (Zoekplaatje). Second source for who made it needed. Rank **Nice**. New place (or Look for in DC-31, Auke Bijlsmabrug, which is a few steps away).
title: "De Lastage 1971", the gable stone of a boarded-up neighbourhood
rank_text: Rank **Nice**. New place (or Look for in DC-31, Auke Bijlsmabrug, which is a few steps away).

heading: Nieuwmarkt/Lastage
text: **AC-14. The Grenspaal: a turtle carrying the debris of Amsterdam.** Pin 52.369391, 4.901639; Sint Antoniesluis, head of the Jodenbreestraat. Hans 't Mannetje (1986) put together leftovers from the city's monument yard at the Uilenburg synagogue: his own green stone turtle carries a thick column from Berlage's insurance building "De Algemene" on the Damrak (where C&A now stands) and a block with a text by Jacob Israël de Haan showing it was meant to carry a bust of Rembrandt. Also called "Monument van Jacob Israël de Haan". Lead: https://nl.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grenspaal_(Hans_'t_Mannetje) ; https://stadscuratorium.nl (De zuildragende schildpad); VVAB "Gedenkteken de Grenspaal". Rank **Nice**. New place.
title: The Grenspaal: a turtle carrying the debris of Amsterdam

heading: Nieuwmarkt/Lastage
text: **AC-15. The Violist in the Stopera, by the Unknown Sculptor.** Pin 52.367222, 4.901667 (inside the Stopera's public passage). A bronze head with hat, a hand and a violin coming up out of (or sinking into) the floor appeared in 1991, placed at night; the city acquired the works on condition the maker stays unknown, and rumours named Queen Beatrix or Gene Holt. Same anonymous hand as the Borstplaat on the Oudekerksplein (DC-03) and the Boomzagertje elsewhere. Lead: Kunstwacht object 538; https://nl.wikipedia.org/wiki/De_Onbekende_Beeldhouwer . Visiting: in the passage, open by day. Rank **Nice**. New place. Look for: André Volten's pink granite ring outside (48 segments, half sunk), Marjolein Rothman's open silhouette of King Willem-Alexander on the plinth where Beatrix's bust stood (chosen by 2,500 voters), and the NAP display (theme C).
title: The Violist in the Stopera, by the Unknown Sculptor

heading: Nieuwmarkt/Lastage
text: **AC-16. Living by Numbers, the HIV/AIDS monument on the IJ.** Pin 52.378323, 4.906184; De Ruijterkade by the IJplein ferry landing. Jean-Michel Othoniel's red glass abacus in a steel frame, unveiled 1 December 2016 (World AIDS Day) by mayor Van der Laan from a cherry picker, called the first HIV/AIDS monument in Europe; its beads first showed 2030, the target year for no new infections. Removed for the new ferry quay, restored at a yard and put back at the end of 2021. Lead: https://nl.wikipedia.org/wiki/HIV/AIDSmonument ; Kunstwacht object 584; Parool 2019. Status: back since end 2021 (Kunstwacht, Flickr). Caveat: "first in Europe" is the makers' claim (quote it). Rank **Nice**. New place.
title: Living by Numbers, the HIV/AIDS monument on the IJ

heading: Nieuwmarkt/Lastage
text: **AC-17. Kalkmarkt 8, the seamen's doctor's pun stones.** Pin 52.372690, 4.906691. Three stones of 1990-91 on the house of the medical centre for seamen: a steamship over "I.C.CK.C.MEN" (I see sick seamen), and two emblems after Roemer Visscher's "Sinnepoppen" (1614), a turnstile "Principiis obsta" (prevention is better) and a sluice "Exonerat et arcet" (the doctor's name was Voorsluis). Local voice: Stadsherstel's friends' walk (2015) stops for it; NTvG interview (2022) with the port doctors of the Radio Medische Dienst. Lead: gevelstenen.net (Kalkmarkt 8); https://mforamsterdam.com/waalseiland . Status: in place (2023). Rank **Okay**. New place.
title: Kalkmarkt 8, the seamen's doctor's pun stones

heading: Nieuwmarkt/Lastage
text: **AC-18. "Time to re-tire", the Fisk tyre boy on the De Ruijterkade.** Pin 52.377483, 4.907986; De Ruijterkade 140-142. A 1933 stone on a former tyre company office shows the yawning boy in pyjamas with a candle and a tyre over his shoulder, the American Fisk mascot, with the slogan "Time to re-tire, get a Fisk". Lead: https://www.gevelstenenvanamsterdam.nl (De Ruijterkade 140-142, GET A FISK); gevelstenen.net. Status: in place (VVAG page 2026). Caveat: description of the figure to check against a photo. Rank **Okay**. New place or Look for in "De Ruijterkade's last shipping offices" (draft nieuwmarkt-1).
title: "Time to re-tire", the Fisk tyre boy on the De Ruijterkade
rank_text: Rank **Okay**. New place or Look for in "De Ruijterkade's last shipping offices" (draft nieuwmarkt-1).

heading: Nieuwmarkt/Lastage
text: **AC-28. The smoking skipper the city said no to.** Pin 52.371308, 4.911199; corner Prins Hendrikkade and Nieuwe Foeliestraat (Nieuwmarkt/Lastage side). A twenty-metre portrait of an old skipper with a pipe, painted on a blind wall in summer 2025 by the American-born Amsterdam muralist Nils Westergard, who asked permission, was refused (the city's welstand advice was negative) and carried on; look closely and the Oudezijds Kolk shows through the man's jumper. The model is a friend of the painter. Neighbours were pleased (AT5, 10 Jul 2025) and on 24 December 2025 the city let it stay "voorlopig". Lead: https://nl.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rokende_schipper ; AT5 24 Dec 2025; Parool 4 Jul 2025. Status: allowed to stay for now (Dec 2025). Rank **Nice**. New place.
title: The smoking skipper the city said no to

heading: Burgwallen-Nieuwe Zijde (continued)
text: **AC-29. Rokin 64, the Moor on the cornice.** Pin 52.370618, 4.892352; corner of the Mooresteegje. A black figure sits in the richly carved Louis XIV cornice (about 1725) of a house called "De Moriaan"; Mapping Slavery and a Parool walk on the colonial past (13 Jun 2023) use it to talk about how "moor" was used for Black people, and tie the sign to the merchant Bartholomeus de Moor, who put a Moor on every house he lived in. Lead: https://mappingslavery.nl/portfolio/amsterdam-2/ ; VVAG photo on Flickr ("Daklijst met moriaan, Rokin 64"). Caveat: De Moor died in 1633 and the cornice is a century later; the link of this house to him needs checking before writing it. Rank **Okay**. New place, or group with AC-01 (Rokin 72, a few doors on).
title: Rokin 64, the Moor on the cornice
rank_text: Rank **Okay**. New place, or group with AC-01 (Rokin 72, a few doors on).

heading: Burgwallen-Nieuwe Zijde
text: **AC-19. Annick van Hardeveld, the last courier.** Pin 52.377635, 4.895138; Hekelveld corner Nieuwezijds Voorburgwal. On the evening of 4 May 1945, with the radio already announcing the German surrender, the 21-year-old courier of the Binnenlandse Strijdkrachten cycled out for a last errand and was shot here at a German post; a bronze plaque on a stone base by Hans Bayens was unveiled on 4 May 1985 by Ed van Thijn, at the initiative of her brother Yann and her friends. Lead: https://www.4en5mei.nl/oorlogsmonumenten/zoeken/1617/amsterdam-monument-voor-annick-van-hardeveld ; Kunstwacht object 476. Rank **Nice**. New place.
title: Annick van Hardeveld, the last courier

heading: Burgwallen-Nieuwe Zijde
text: **AC-20. Centraal Station's two plaques: the cold welcome and the sergeant.** Pin approx 52.378800, 4.900200 (fix on the plaque in the station; check: Location). In the station's "catacombs" the Dutch state received the few survivors of the camps in 1945, coldly; a plaque unveiled on 30 August 2019 says so in plain words ("De overheid ... faalde in de uitvoering van haar taak"), based on the memories of architect Moshé Zwarts, who arrived here at almost eight after Bergen-Belsen. A second plaque (22 September 1984, broken tulip and dove) marks where BS sergeant W.H. Zeeman (22) was shot on 7 May 1945 when German Grüne Polizei tried to retake the station. Lead: https://www.4en5mei.nl/oorlogsmonumenten/zoeken/4962/amsterdam-herinnering ; NS news 30 Aug 2019 (https://nieuws.ns.nl); Parool 26 Aug 2019; 4en5mei record 1620 (Zeeman). Caveat: Centraal Station is A-list; pitched on the plaques. Rank **Amazing** (a state admitting its own failure, in a place millions pass). New place.
title: Centraal Station's two plaques: the cold welcome and the sergeant
rank_text: Rank **Amazing** (a state admitting its own failure, in a place millions pass). New place.

heading: Burgwallen-Nieuwe Zijde
text: **AC-21. Walk of Pride, the queer names from the Dam to the Homomonument.** Pin 52.373180, 4.891050 (first tiles at the Dam end of the Raadhuisstraat; fix the first tile on site). Since 8 July 2026 a line of bronze-inlaid tiles (52 or 53: sources differ) runs from the Dam through the Raadhuisstraat to the Homomonument, each with the name of a queer person, from unknown 19th-century Amsterdammers to international heroes, chosen by a committee from the community; an initiative of IHLIA LGBTI Heritage, the Homomonument foundation and Stichting GALA, laid for WorldPride 2026. Lead: https://walkofpride.amsterdam ; Volkskrant 9 Jul 2026; Gay Krant 20 Jun 2026. Caveat: the route runs on into Grachtengordel-West, so a single pin in NZ with the route in the text. Rank **Nice**. New place (DC-12/BC lead: Homomonument is West's).
title: Walk of Pride, the queer names from the Dam to the Homomonument
rank_text: Rank **Nice**. New place (DC-12/BC lead: Homomonument is West's).

heading: Burgwallen-Oude Zijde (continued; numbers kept as found)
text: **AC-30. The Prostitution Information Centre, a sex worker's own door.** Pin 52.374747, 4.897754; Enge Kerksteeg 3, by the Oude Kerk. Mariska Majoor, who had worked behind the window herself, opened the PIC in 1994 so that the talk about her trade would no longer happen without the people in it: a small information shop where anyone can ask anything, still there after thirty years (NH Nieuws, 31 Oct 2024). It belongs with the Belle statue (DC-03) that Majoor also initiated. Lead: https://nl.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prostitutie_Informatie_Centrum ; https://sekswerkerfgoed.nl (2014, "20 en 25 jaar PIC"). Status: open (NH Nieuws 2024; pic-amsterdam.com). Caveat: a shop with a souvenir side; pitch on the history. Rank **Okay**. Group with DC-03 or new place.
title: The Prostitution Information Centre, a sex worker's own door
rank_text: Rank **Okay**. Group with DC-03 or new place.

heading: Nieuwmarkt/Lastage (continued)
text: **AC-31. The Tak family's six stones, Sint Antoniesbreestraat 98.** Pin 52.370849, 4.900411. Six Stolpersteine in a row for Barend, Dora, Dora, Izak, Saartje (Tak-Bluhm) and Simon Tak, one household of the old Jewish quarter; the zone has others in clusters (Nieuwe Uilenburgerstraat 44, 70, 72, 74, 86; Zandstraat 11 with seven; Zwanenburgwal 92 with seven; Zeedijk 56 for Hartog Lek and Saartje Lek-Duveen). Lead: https://nl.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lijst_van_Stolpersteine_in_Amsterdam-Centrum ; https://www.joodsmonument.nl (per name). Caveat: stones are not places on their own; this is the one family group the user could take as a pin for the theme; the biographies are to be read on Joods Monument before writing. Rank **Okay**. New place, or Look for lines per street.
title: The Tak family's six stones, Sint Antoniesbreestraat 98

heading: Burgwallen-Oude Zijde
text: **AC-22. Beursplein 5: the banker of the resistance and the clock the Germans shot.** Pin 52.374389, 4.895967 (Effectenbeurs, inside). In the exchange hangs a plaque (17 February 1949) for Walraven "Wally" van Hall, the banker who financed much of the Dutch resistance through the Nationaal Steun Fonds with loans against worthless marked shares, shot in Haarlem in February 1945; near it Cephas Stauthamer's kneeling woman with a dove (1947, "Ex tenebris lux") for exchange members who died, and a clock face hit by a German bullet on 7 May 1945 with a 1949 text, "Op 7 mei 1945 hebben de moffen hun laatste kruit verschoten". Lead: 4en5mei records 2946 and 1622. Caveat: inside an office building (Euronext): access to check; the draft "Beursplein 5, the stock exchange that left Berlage" (oudezijde-1) covers the building, so this may be a merge of the war layer into it. Rank **Nice**. Merge into "Beursplein 5" or new place if access is real.
title: Beursplein 5: the banker of the resistance and the clock the Germans shot
rank_text: Rank **Nice**. Merge into "Beursplein 5" or new place if access is real.

heading: Nieuwmarkt/Lastage
text: **AC-23. Megadlé Jethomim, the orphanage drawn in the paving.** Pin 52.367189, 4.901640; Amstel 1 (beside the Stopera, Amstel side). A band of light granite setts outlines part of the boys' orphanage that stood here from 1865; the words in the paving say that in March 1943 the occupier took the almost hundred boys away, that three carers chose to go with them to Sobibor and that none came back. Design Otto Treumann, text Cor Jongens, unveiled 7 December 1989. Lead: https://www.4en5mei.nl/oorlogsmonumenten/zoeken/1625/amsterdam-gedenkteken-aan-de-amstel ; Kunstwacht object 453. Rank **Nice**. New place (DC-10, Vlooienburg plaque, is inside the Stopera: a user may want one "Jewish memorials around the Stopera" pin with AC-24).
title: Megadlé Jethomim, the orphanage drawn in the paving

heading: Nieuwmarkt/Lastage
text: **AC-24. Monument Joods Verzet, against a prejudice.** Pin 52.368184, 4.898687; Amstel 9 by the Zwanenburgwal. A black stone column with the tablets of the law (J.J. Glatt and Emmanuel Glatt, 1988) honours Jews who died fighting the occupier; Ed van Thijn argued at the time that the old idea that Jews did not resist was simply wrong. It is the place of the yearly Kristallnacht commemoration. Lead: 4en5mei record 1631; Kunstwacht object 455. Rank **Okay**. New place or group with AC-23.
title: Monument Joods Verzet, against a prejudice
rank_text: Rank **Okay**. New place or group with AC-23.

heading: Nieuwmarkt/Lastage
text: **AC-25. De Dokwerker and the February Strike.** Pin 52.366835, 4.904720; Jonas Daniël Meijerplein. Mari Andriessen's docker (1952) stands for the strike of 25 and 26 February 1941 against the deportation of Jews; the model was his friend Willem Termetz, from the resistance, and Andriessen himself hid Jews and refused the Kultuurkamer. He first faced the Waterlooplein and was turned toward the synagogue in 1970 for the metro works; the Rosj Pina school has adopted him; the yearly February Strike commemoration is held here. Look for: the ABVA/KABO plaque of 2006 on the Waterlooplein for the civil servants who struck, some executed for it (4en5mei 3611). Lead: 4en5mei record 1434; Kunstwacht object 498. Caveat: on the square of the Jewish Cultural Quarter (A-list buildings); the statue itself is not on the A-list. Rank **Nice**. New place.
title: De Dokwerker and the February Strike

heading: Nieuwmarkt/Lastage
text: **AC-26. Valkenburgerstraat, shot after the surrender (5 May 1945).** Pin 52.369783, 4.908957; corner Anne Frankstraat and Valkenburgerstraat. On the evening of 5 May 1945, after the capitulation, fifty German Grüne Polizei forced their way into building De Leeuw, where about 150 mostly unarmed men of the BS medical troops were gathered; four men who came to free them were killed: Flip Jernberg, Herman de Kok, Renée Pyck and Johannes van Reede. Cephas Stauthamer's relief of 1947 was lost from view in demolition and rebuilding and put back in the new building on the corner in 1998. Lead: 4en5mei record 1504; Kunstwacht object 523. Rank **Okay**. New place.
title: Valkenburgerstraat, shot after the surrender (5 May 1945)

heading: Nieuwmarkt/Lastage
text: **AC-27. The 8 December monument on the Mozes en Aäronkerk.** Pin 52.368346, 4.903503 (wall of the church, Waterlooplein side). A plaque with the names of the fifteen opponents of the military regime murdered in Fort Zeelandia, Paramaribo, on 8 and 9 December 1982, unveiled 8 December 1992 by Liesbeth Venetiaan-Vanenburg; Surinamese Amsterdam commemorates here every year (AT5 2014, Historiek 2012). Lead: https://nl.wikipedia.org/wiki/8_Decembermonument ; https://www.at5.nl (herdenking Decembermoorden, 10 Dec 2014). Caveat: the church is a draft (nieuwmarkt-3) and BC-26; the plaque could be a Look for line there instead. Rank **Okay**. New place or Look for.
title: The 8 December monument on the Mozes en Aäronkerk
rank_text: Rank **Okay**. New place or Look for.

heading: Sweep 3: war and memory / Weesperbuurt/Plantage
text: **AE-01. The population register attack, Plantage Kerklaan 36.** Pin 52.366743, 4.912312 (OSM memorial node, on the building), Plantage Kerklaan 36. On 27 March 1943 a resistance group of artists and students, Gerrit van der Veen's among them, set fire to the city's population register here, to make the forged identity papers of people in hiding hard to check. The plaque, designed by Willem Sandberg and unveiled on 4 August 1945, names the twelve executed on 1 July 1943: Arondeus, Bloemgarten, Groeger, Hartoch, Van Musschenbroek, Reitsma, Halberstadt, Brouwer, Limperg, Bakker, Barentsen, Roos ("zij streden en vielen voor de vrijheid"). Lead: https://www.4en5mei.nl/oorlogsmonumenten/zoeken/1602/amsterdam-monument-aan-de-plantage-kerklaan ; second: https://nl.wikipedia.org/wiki/Monument_voor_het_kunstenaarsverzet_1940-1945 (why the Kunstenaarsverzet monument stands nearby). Status: on the 4en5mei register and OSM, 2026. Caveat: the building belongs to the Artis complex (A-list); the plaque faces the street. Rank: **Amazing**. New place (pair with AE-02 in text; the Stolpersteine of the Prins family at Plantage Kerklaan 63, seven stones, are a Look for line here).
title: The population register attack, Plantage Kerklaan 36
rank_text: Rank: **Amazing**. New place (pair with AE-02 in text; the Stolpersteine of the Prins family at Plantage Kerklaan 63, seven stones, are a Look for line here).

heading: Sweep 3: war and memory / Weesperbuurt/Plantage
text: **AE-02. Monument for the artists' resistance, Westermanplantsoen.** Pin 52.365543, 4.914189, Plantage Middenlaan by the Westermanlaan. Carel Kneulman's monument stands on the strip left when the Panorama building was pulled down, chosen because Gerrit van der Veen led the register attack round the corner; plans for a memorial to him dated from the day he was shot, 10 June 1944, and took until the 1970s. Lead: https://nl.wikipedia.org/wiki/Monument_voor_het_kunstenaarsverzet_1940-1945 ; second: https://www.4en5mei.nl/oorlogsmonumenten/zoeken/1518 . Status: on Kunstwacht and 4en5mei, 2026. Caveat: unveiling year from my earlier note (1973), check the article before writing. Rank: Nice. New place.
title: Monument for the artists' resistance, Westermanplantsoen

heading: Sweep 3: war and memory / Weesperbuurt/Plantage
text: **AE-03. "Nooit meer Auschwitz", the broken-mirror monument, Wertheimpark.** Pin 52.367754, 4.909258, Wertheimpark. Jan Wolkers' mirrors lie broken so that the sky they reflect is never whole again ("De hemel blijft voorgoed geschonden"); beneath lies an urn of ashes collected at Auschwitz-Birkenau in January 1952. First at the Oosterbegraafplaats (1977), moved here larger in 1993; the national Holocaust remembrance is held here every last Sunday of January. Lead: https://nl.wikipedia.org/wiki/Auschwitzmonument_(Amsterdam) ; second: https://www.4en5mei.nl/oorlogsmonumenten/zoeken/1501 . Status: in use for the January ceremony. Caveat: fairly well known. Rank: Nice. New place (or group with "Wertheim fountain (Wertheimpark)").
title: "Nooit meer Auschwitz", the broken-mirror monument, Wertheimpark
rank_text: Rank: Nice. New place (or group with "Wertheim fountain (Wertheimpark)").

heading: Sweep 3: war and memory / Weesperbuurt/Plantage
text: **AE-04. The school plaques and the deaf memorial, Hortusplantsoen.** Pin 52.366428, 4.906203 (the deaf memorial), Hortusplantsoen 1-2. Three memorials in a row: Truus Menger-Oversteegen's monument for Jewish deaf war victims (17 October 2010, with sign-language drawings by Bart Koolen); a plaque for the Ammanschool for deaf children (1928-1976) at no. 2, whose Jewish pupils had to flee and hide; and plaques for the Van Det and Davidsschool, Jewish trade schools for girls and boys, from which "bijna alle bestuursleden, vele leerkrachten en de meeste leerlingen" were taken. Lead: https://www.4en5mei.nl/oorlogsmonumenten/zoeken/3545 ; second: https://www.4en5mei.nl/oorlogsmonumenten/zoeken/2943 and /4577 . Status: on the register 2026. Caveat: the Van Det plaque of 1948 hung inside the school hall; check what is visible outside. Rank: Nice. New place.
title: The school plaques and the deaf memorial, Hortusplantsoen

heading: Sweep 3: war and memory / Weesperbuurt/Plantage
text: **AE-05. The Kok family plaques, Nieuwe Keizersgracht 24.** Pin 52.365564, 4.906254, Nieuwe Keizersgracht 24. Two plaques of 2009: on the left Max, Julie, Samuel and Jacques Kok, taken from this house and killed in Auschwitz and Mauthausen; on the right Betty Kok, who at 17 went into hiding from here in 1942 through David and Jansje Gomes de Mesquita-Prins, the only one of the family to survive. Lead: https://www.4en5mei.nl/oorlogsmonumenten/zoeken/3642/amsterdam-monument-aan-de-nieuwe-keizersgracht ; second: Joods Monument (not read). Status: unveiled 13 December 2009, on register 2026. Caveat: private house front. Rank: Nice. New place.
title: The Kok family plaques, Nieuwe Keizersgracht 24

heading: Sweep 3: war and memory / Weesperbuurt/Plantage
text: **AE-06. The Brilleslijper house, Nieuwe Achtergracht 14.** Pin 52.361800, 4.905296, Nieuwe Achtergracht 14. Stolpersteine for Joseph, Fijtje and Jacob Brilleslijper and Gerrit Tak, all murdered in Auschwitz in 1944. Jannie and Lien Brilleslijper, resistance workers who were deported on the same train as the Frank family and survived, had lived at this address in 1939. Lead: https://joodsmonument.nl/en/page/89342/nieuwe-achtergracht-14-ii-amsterdam ; second: https://research.annefrank.org/en/personen/6bc77428-56e8-4712-a115-751a1d080c09/ and https://tracesofwar.com/sights/144118/Stolpersteine-Nieuwe-Achtergracht-14.htm . Status: stones on the wiki list 2026. Caveat: the wiki list counts six stones here, TracesOfWar three names; count on site. No stones for the sisters (they survived). Rank: Nice. New place.
title: The Brilleslijper house, Nieuwe Achtergracht 14

heading: Sweep 3: war and memory / Weesperbuurt/Plantage
text: **AE-07. The Stolpersteine of the Nieuwe Prinsengracht.** Pin 52.363059, 4.905532, Nieuwe Prinsengracht 18. Twelve stones in front of no. 18 and eight at no. 50, the densest clusters in the zone: whole households of the old Jewish Weesperbuurt in one doorstep. Lead: https://nl.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lijst_van_Stolpersteine_in_Amsterdam-Centrum ; second: Joods Monument per name (not read). Status: on the list 2026. Caveat: stories per family not yet read. Rank: Okay. New place (one pin for the street).
title: The Stolpersteine of the Nieuwe Prinsengracht
rank_text: Rank: Okay. New place (one pin for the street).

heading: Sweep 3: war and memory / Weesperbuurt/Plantage
text: **AE-08. The Stolpersteine of the Plantage Badlaan.** Pin 52.364236, 4.916589, Plantage Badlaan 15. Eleven stones at nos. 13, 15 and 24 of a short street of 1900s blocks. Lead: the wiki Stolpersteine list (above); second: Joods Monument (not read). Status: list 2026. Caveat: stories unread. Rank: Okay. New place.
title: The Stolpersteine of the Plantage Badlaan

heading: Sweep 3: war and memory / Weesperbuurt/Plantage
text: **AE-09. LIRO, the robbery bank, Sarphatistraat 47-55.** Pin 52.360951, 4.906645, Sarphatistraat 47-55. From 1941 this building held the "Lippmann, Rosenthal & Co." that the occupiers set up for "de stelselmatige beroving van de Joodse bevolking van al haar aardse bezittingen" (plaque text). The 2003 plaque ends with Isaiah: "tot beroving en er was niemand die zei: geef terug". Lead: https://www.4en5mei.nl/oorlogsmonumenten/zoeken/2969/amsterdam-plaquette-op-het-voormalige-liro-bankgebouw ; second: the gg-zuid draft "Lippmann, Rosenthal & Co., the bank whose name was stolen" (the real bank in the Nieuwe Spiegelstraat). Status: unveiled 26 May 2003, register 2026. Caveat: office building. Rank: Nice. New place (cross-reference the Lippmann Rosenthal draft).
title: LIRO, the robbery bank, Sarphatistraat 47-55
rank_text: Rank: Nice. New place (cross-reference the Lippmann Rosenthal draft).

heading: Sweep 3: war and memory / Weesperbuurt/Plantage
text: **AE-10. Walter Süskind's bridge plaque, Nieuwe Herengracht.** Pin 52.365831, 4.901969, Walter Süskindbrug. Süskind, born in Lüdenscheid in 1906 and dead after the Auschwitz evacuation in 1945, worked at the Hollandsche Schouwburg; the plaque (30 August 1972) says he "onttrok vele joodse medeburgers aan deportatie". Lead: https://www.4en5mei.nl/oorlogsmonumenten/zoeken/2947 ; second: OSM. Status: register 2026. Rank: Okay. Group with "Bridges with wartime names".
title: Walter Süskind's bridge plaque, Nieuwe Herengracht
rank_text: Rank: Okay. Group with "Bridges with wartime names".

heading: Sweep 3: war and memory / Weesperbuurt/Plantage
text: **AE-11. The health service plaque, Nieuwe Achtergracht 100.** Pin 52.362549, 4.908730, Nieuwe Achtergracht 100. Placed by the staff of the city health service (G.G. en G.D.) on 1 August 1947 for fifteen colleagues killed in the war. Lead: https://www.4en5mei.nl/oorlogsmonumenten/zoeken/1608 ; second: OSM. Status: register 2026. Rank: Okay. New place.
title: The health service plaque, Nieuwe Achtergracht 100

heading: Sweep 3: war and memory / Weesperbuurt/Plantage
text: **AE-12. Telefoon van de Wind, Hoftuin.** Pin 52.366064, 4.904488, Hoftuin by the Weesperstraat. A disconnected phone in a garden for calling the dead, run by Humanitas Amsterdam, after the Japanese wind phone of Otsuchi. Lead: OSM node 11944513513 (website humanitas.nl/afdeling/amsterdam_en_diemen); second: Humanitas page. Status: on OSM 2026. Caveat: check opening hours of the Hoftuin. Rank: Nice. New place.
title: Telefoon van de Wind, Hoftuin

heading: Sweep 3: war and memory / De Weteringschans
text: **AE-13. The wall in the middle of the school, Weteringschans 263.** Pin 52.359379, 4.897263, Weteringschans 263. During the war a wall suddenly went up in the middle of the Wilhelmina Catharinaschool: the Jewish half of the pupils was moved to the back. The 2005 plaque by Frits Nolte begins "Voor alle kinderen die van school naar huis gingen en daarna nooit meer werden gezien". Lead: https://www.4en5mei.nl/oorlogsmonumenten/zoeken/3385 ; second: OSM. Status: unveiled 25 February 2005, register 2026. Rank: **Amazing**. New place.
title: The wall in the middle of the school, Weteringschans 263

heading: Sweep 3: war and memory / De Weteringschans
text: **AE-14. Walraven van Hall's snapped tree, Frederiksplein.** Pin 52.359946, 4.899631, Frederiksplein. Fernando Sánchez Castillo's bronze tree, broken over a low wall, for the "banker of the resistance" shot in 1945; the fallen branches are a bench. A retired GP, Hans Weijers, started it after a 2005 documentary and raised €250,000 in the crisis years. Lead: https://nl.wikipedia.org/wiki/Monument_Walraven_van_Hall ; second: https://www.4en5mei.nl/oorlogsmonumenten/zoeken/3543 . Status: unveiled 3 September 2010. Rank: Nice. New place (listed as a lead in notes/wetering-1.md).
title: Walraven van Hall's snapped tree, Frederiksplein
rank_text: Rank: Nice. New place (listed as a lead in notes/wetering-1.md).

heading: Sweep 3: war and memory / De Weteringschans
text: **AE-15. The Navalny memorial, Frederiksplein.** Pin 52.359961, 4.899699, beside AE-14. A plaque for Aleksej Navalny ("Geef niet op en geloof in het beste") that moved here after the city would not let it stay at its first site; a Groningen student, Vladimir, travels down about once a month to clean it. Lead: https://www.nhnieuws.nl/nieuws/357218/vladimir-onderhoudt-al-twee-jaar-monument-ter-nagedachtenis-aan-aleksej-navalny ; second: OSM node 12994026750. Status: NH Nieuws, two years of upkeep (2026). Caveat: informal memorial; status may change. Rank: Nice. Group with AE-14.
title: The Navalny memorial, Frederiksplein

heading: Sweep 3: war and memory / De Weteringschans
text: **AE-16. Krop's monument for the Spieghelschool fire, Marnixstraat 404.** Pin 52.363956, 4.881643, by the DeLaMar theatre. On 5 January 1945 the resistance set fire to the Arbeitseinsatz office in the Spieghelschool; the occupiers shot five political prisoners and twenty officials in reprisal. Hildo Krop's bronze of 1947 was torn off its base and taken in September 1967 and recast. Lead: https://nl.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oorlogsmonument_Marnixstraat ; second: https://www.4en5mei.nl/oorlogsmonumenten/zoeken/1611 . Status: register 2026. Rank: Nice. New place.
title: Krop's monument for the Spieghelschool fire, Marnixstraat 404

heading: Sweep 3: war and memory / De Weteringschans
text: **AE-17. The WSBZ staff stone, Nieuwe Looiersdwarsstraat 15-17.** Pin 52.360728, 4.893644. A 1947 stone by Hans Krieks, placed by colleagues for twelve staff of the W.S.B.Z. "gevallen als slachtoffers van de Duitse terreur", most of them Jewish names (Pereira, Rodrigues, Nunes Vas). Lead: https://www.4en5mei.nl/oorlogsmonumenten/zoeken/1609 ; second: OSM. Status: unveiled 2 January 1947. Rank: Okay. New place.
title: The WSBZ staff stone, Nieuwe Looiersdwarsstraat 15-17

heading: Sweep 3: war and memory / De Weteringschans
text: **AE-18. "Tegen alle stromen in", Peter R. de Vries, Leidseplein.** Pin 52.363838, 4.882760, Leidseplein by the Lange Leidsedwarsstraat. Rini Hurkmans' two bronze hands gripping each other, with De Vries's own life rules in 41 languages, a few metres from where he was shot on 6 July 2021. Lead: https://nos.nl/l/2528991 ; second: https://www.nhnieuws.nl/nieuws/338489/monument-peter-r-de-vries-trekt-veel-bekijks-groot-maar-hij-verdient-het-echt . Status: unveiled 15 July 2024. Caveat: on an A-list square, but the monument is its own place. Rank: Nice. New place (lead in notes/wetering-1.md).
title: "Tegen alle stromen in", Peter R. de Vries, Leidseplein
rank_text: Rank: Nice. New place (lead in notes/wetering-1.md).

heading: Sweep 3: war and memory / De Weteringschans
text: **AE-19. Zeelandbank, Weteringcircuit.** Pin 52.359220, 4.891929. Nico Onkenhout's bench, Schouwen-Duiveland's thank-you for Amsterdam's help after the 1953 flood: a lion on waves, a fish tail, eighteen Zeeland town arms in the backrest. A plaster stand-in was put here in 1957; the real one was unveiled in July 1958 with four Zeelanders in costume. Lead: https://nl.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zeelandbank ; second: Kunstwacht record 532. Status: register 2026. Rank: Nice. New place (named in notes/wetering-3.md).
title: Zeelandbank, Weteringcircuit
rank_text: Rank: Nice. New place (named in notes/wetering-3.md).

heading: Sweep 3: war and memory / Grachtengordel-Zuid
text: **AE-20. Saint George and the dragon, Reguliersgracht 34.** Pin 52.363774, 4.895659, Reguliersgracht 34. Ben Guntenaar's white relief of 21 November 1945: the twelve faces are the twelve Jews hidden in this house by Ivo and Lydia Schöffer. The motto is a pun: "Submergo unica ut emergam", I dive under to come up. Lead: https://www.4en5mei.nl/oorlogsmonumenten/zoeken/1514/amsterdam-sint-joris-en-de-draak ; second: OSM. Status: register 2026. Caveat: private house; the forging story (Lydia Schöffer and false IDs) needs a second source before writing. Rank: **Amazing**. New place.
title: Saint George and the dragon, Reguliersgracht 34

heading: Sweep 3: war and memory / Grachtengordel-Zuid
text: **AE-21. Where Stichting 1940-1945 was founded, Keizersgracht 567.** Pin 52.364372, 4.890469. On 13 October 1944 representatives of the illegal groups met in deepest secrecy in this building and founded the Stichting 1940-1944, renamed 1940-1945 after the liberation, to carry the resistance's "verantwoordelijkheidsgevoel... voor elkanders moeilijkheden en noden". Plaque of 13 October 1994. Lead: https://www.4en5mei.nl/oorlogsmonumenten/zoeken/2944 ; second: OSM. Status: register 2026. Rank: Okay. New place.
title: Where Stichting 1940-1945 was founded, Keizersgracht 567

heading: Sweep 3: war and memory / Oostelijke Eilanden/Kadijken
text: **AE-22. The hunger winter relief, Oosterkerk.** Pin 52.369827, 4.919263, Wittenburgergracht front of the Oosterkerk. An interchurch committee had food bought from Groningen and Frisian farmers and shipped secretly to the islands in 1944-45; the neighbourhood's thanks is Hildo Krop's relief (a man with a sack on a ship, a woman with children before ruined houses) and a verse: "Dit monument vertoont de dank van heel de buurt". The weathered original is inside; a cast copy is on the street side. Lead: https://nl.wikipedia.org/wiki/De_hongerwinter ; second: https://www.buitenbeeldinbeeld.nl/Amsterdam_C/Hongerwinter.htm . Status: OSM 2026. Rank: Nice. Group with "Oosterkerk, the islands' church the city nearly demolished".
title: The hunger winter relief, Oosterkerk
rank_text: Rank: Nice. Group with "Oosterkerk, the islands' church the city nearly demolished".

heading: Sweep 3: war and memory / Oostelijke Eilanden/Kadijken
text: **AE-23. De Waarheid's stone, Windroosplein.** Pin 52.373079, 4.924318. For the staff of the communist underground paper De Waarheid "gevallen in de strijd tegen het fascisme"; by Rob Schotman and Wim Tap, 1983, moved here from the Hoogte Kadijk in 1993. Lead: https://www.4en5mei.nl/oorlogsmonumenten/zoeken/1495 ; second: Kunstwacht 586. Rank: Okay. New place.
title: De Waarheid's stone, Windroosplein

heading: Sweep 3: war and memory / Oostelijke Eilanden/Kadijken
text: **AE-24. Werkspoor's war memorial, Oostenburgergracht 77.** Pin 52.368022, 4.924538. A long stone of names, "Vrijheid, gerechtigheid, vrede", for the staff of the engineering works killed in the resistance, in bombings and in camps. Lead: https://www.4en5mei.nl/oorlogsmonumenten/zoeken/4707 ; second: Werkspoormuseum (photo 2025). Rank: Okay. Group with "Werkspoor's halls on Oostenburg".
title: Werkspoor's war memorial, Oostenburgergracht 77
rank_text: Rank: Okay. Group with "Werkspoor's halls on Oostenburg".

heading: Sweep 3: war and memory / Oostelijke Eilanden/Kadijken
text: **AE-25. The nautical college memorial, Marineterrein.** Pin 52.372376, 4.917126. Pieter Starreveld's plate for the former pupils of the Kweekschool voor de Zeevaart killed 1939-1945; 138 names at first, more added later. It stood in the school's courtyard on the Prins Hendrikkade until 2000. Lead: https://www.4en5mei.nl/oorlogsmonumenten/zoeken/3257 ; second: OSM. Caveat: Marineterrein access hours. Rank: Okay. Group with "Marineterrein, the navy yard behind the wall".
title: The nautical college memorial, Marineterrein
rank_text: Rank: Okay. Group with "Marineterrein, the navy yard behind the wall".

heading: Sweep 2: public art and walls / Oostelijke Eilanden/Kadijken
text: **AE-26. "Er ligt een roofstaat", the ship of the islands, Grote Wittenburgerstraat.** Pin 52.371708, 4.921704. A blue-stone ship on high waves (1983, Wim Tap, Marius van Beek, Hank Beelenkamp), commissioned to recall the islands' shipyard past, with a stout figurehead and frightened crew at the stern. The makers cut in Multatuli's line from Max Havelaar, "Er ligt een roofstaat tussen Oost-Friesland en de Westerschelde": the VOC yards' dark side, set in their own neighbourhood. Local voice: De Eilander, no. 7, 2008 (via Kunstwacht). Lead: https://www.buitenkunstamsterdam.nl (record 527, Plastisch teken) ; second: OSM. Status: register 2026. Rank: **Amazing**. New place.
title: "Er ligt een roofstaat", the ship of the islands, Grote Wittenburgerstraat

heading: Sweep 2: public art and walls / Oostelijke Eilanden/Kadijken
text: **AE-27. Kattenburger Triomfboog.** Pin 52.372737, 4.919126, Kattenburgerstraat underpass. David Smithson and Kristina Leko asked Kattenburgers to write their own history; 25 residents, mostly in their sixties, did: the fight to return after the 1960s demolition, the low-rent movement, the union men. Their handwriting is fired onto tiles on the six columns of the main underpass. Lead: Kunstwacht record 556 ; second: Kunstwacht cites the project; artists' site not read. Rank: Nice. New place.
title: Kattenburger Triomfboog

heading: Sweep 2: public art and walls / Oostelijke Eilanden/Kadijken
text: **AE-28. Mbulu Ngulu on the advertising column, Czaar Peterstraat.** Pin 52.367421, 4.925193, corner of the Oostenburgergracht. Since 1991 a West African reliquary guardian (orange head, red-and-white horns, purple rods) by Alexander Schabracq sits on top of a peperbus, diagonally across from De Gooyer. Lead: Kunstwacht record 504 ; second: OSM. Rank: Nice. New place.
title: Mbulu Ngulu on the advertising column, Czaar Peterstraat

heading: Sweep 2: public art and walls / Oostelijke Eilanden/Kadijken
text: **AE-29. Jakoba Mulder's lamp, Mulderplein.** Pin 52.366008, 4.924396. Gijs Bakker's 1997 memorial to one of the first women architects and planners: a tilted granito disc, a six-metre street lamp with leaf-shaped cuts, nine chairs, and 38 steel blocks spelling "Droombeeld. Visie. Werk. Inspanning. Verwachting. Wording." Lead: Kunstwacht 496 ; second: OSM. Rank: Nice. New place.
title: Jakoba Mulder's lamp, Mulderplein

heading: Sweep 2: public art and walls / Oostelijke Eilanden/Kadijken
text: **AE-30. Tussentijd, the shards of the Funenpark.** Pin 52.368708, 4.929850. Gabriel Lester's five giant "shards" with relief maps of the old bastion, after pottery and the 1663 wall found when the park was dug. Lead: Kunstwacht 557 ; second: gabriellester.com. Rank: Okay. New place.
title: Tussentijd, the shards of the Funenpark

heading: Sweep 2: public art and walls / Oostelijke Eilanden/Kadijken
text: **AE-31. Simon Erb's sgraffito school front, Tweede Leeghwaterstraat 7.** Pin 52.370064, 4.931299. A 1960 sgraffito on the De Ruiterschool, rated "Top" in the city's wall-art register. Lead: maps.amsterdam.nl WANDKUNST ; second: OSM not found. Caveat: not seen. Rank: Okay. New place.
title: Simon Erb's sgraffito school front, Tweede Leeghwaterstraat 7

heading: Sweep 2: public art and walls / Weesperbuurt/Plantage
text: **AE-32. The art of Weesperplein metro station.** Pin 52.361451, 4.907986. Three works from a 1976 open call with 198 entries: Charles Bergmans' Verplaatsing, ten blue-stone blocks polished by forty years of sitters; Matthijs van Dam's Luchtspiegelingen, the Weesperstraat and Sarphatistraat seen from below; Pieter Engels' Signatuur van de anonieme arbeider, three bronze beams forming an A for Amsterdam, aannemer, arbeider. Lead: Kunstwacht 1182-1184 ; second: OSM. Rank: Nice. New place.
title: The art of Weesperplein metro station

heading: Sweep 2: public art and walls / Weesperbuurt/Plantage
text: **AE-33. Krop's burghers, Weesperstraat.** Pin 52.360785, 4.908626. Hildo Krop's Poorter and Poortersvrouw (1940) on the Weesperstraat blocks, with Piet Kramer's year stones and locomotive relief. Lead: wiki statue list ; second: OSM nodes 4370446624 and 7084303792. Rank: Okay. New place.
title: Krop's burghers, Weesperstraat

heading: Sweep 2: public art and walls / Weesperbuurt/Plantage
text: **AE-34. The sphinxes of the Parktuin gate, Plantage Middenlaan.** Pin 52.367426, 4.909140. The empire gate is all that remains of the Parktuin and its concert hall; its lantern-bearing sphinxes vanished during or after the war. Hans 't Mannetje, once Krop's apprentice, carved marble copies from old prints, unveiled by mayor Polak on 16 January 1982 for the Plantage's 300 years. Lead: Kunstwacht 508 ; second: OSM 8272072528. Rank: Nice. New place.
title: The sphinxes of the Parktuin gate, Plantage Middenlaan

heading: Sweep 2: public art and walls / De Weteringschans

Zadkine's last big work, unveiled two days after his death in 1967, has hung on a console, stood on the Westeinde and gone to ArtZuid; in spring 2025 it returned to the green strip by the bank's new entrance. Jan Wolkers called it a pile of broken chocolate bars. Lead: https://nl.wikipedia.org/wiki/La_demeure_humaine ; second: Kunstwacht 545. Status: placed spring 2025. Rank: Nice. heading: Sweep 3: war and memory / Grachtengordel-West
text: **AW-01 The frog stone, Prinsengracht 535: hiders who gossiped like Ovid's frogs.** Pin 52.368743, 4.883000 (4en5mei; address pin 52.368753, 4.882961), Prinsengracht 535, stone beside the front door. A blue stone with a frog in relief and a line from Ovid's Metamorphoses, "QUAMQUAM SUNT SUB AQUA ...": the rest of the line, as the joke went, says that even under water they keep on slandering. From 1941 more than eight people hid in this house, among them the archaeologist and art historian Annie Zadoks-Josephus Jitta, and they gossiped so much that they compared themselves with the Lycian peasants whom Latona turned into frogs and who went on cursing under water. She escaped when the hiding place was cleared in 1942/1943, bought the house after the war, and her son gave the stone. Local voice: the hiders' own joke, as she told it to NRC ("Een huis vol kikkers", 30 November 1990, cited by 4en5mei). Lead: 4en5mei 4785. Second: https://nl.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prinsengracht_535 ; Jona Lendering, "Ovidius in Amsterdam", Mainzer Beobachter blog, 23 June 2012 (cited by 4en5mei). Status: in the 4en5mei register, read 2026-11-24 ("bevindt zich naast de voordeur"). Caveats: private house, stone only; a short walk from the A-list Anne Frank House, which makes a good contrast but must not be the pitch. Rank **Amazing**. New place.
title: The frog stone, Prinsengracht 535: hiders who gossiped like Ovid's frogs

heading: Sweep 3: war and memory / Grachtengordel-West
text: **AW-02 Homomonument: three triangles that point somewhere.** Pin 52.374466, 4.884725 (OSM), Westermarkt, on the Keizersgracht. Karin Daan's pink granite triangles (unveiled 5 September 1987), the first free-standing monument in the world to persecuted gay men and lesbians. Pitch on what most people stand on without seeing: the three corners form one big triangle; the step into the water ("present") points at the National Monument on the Dam, the one in the pavement ("past") with Jacob Israël de Haan's line "Naar vriendschap zulk een mateloos verlangen" points at the Anne Frank House, and the raised one ("future") pointed at the COC's office then in the Rozenstraat. The idea began on 4 May 1970, when two young activists were arrested for laying a wreath on the Dam for gay victims; a day later thirty wore pink triangles in protest. Local voice: flowers on the water step all year, for war victims and for AIDS victims (nl.wikipedia); the tram stop was renamed "Homomonument" in 2017. Lead: KW 529 (gemeentelijk monument). Second: 4en5mei 1499; https://nl.wikipedia.org/wiki/Homomonument_(Amsterdam) (after Karin Daan's own explanation). Status: in KW and 4en5mei 2026; OSM inscription. Caveats: second tier per A-LIST.md, allowed; directly beside the A-list Westerkerk, so pitch on the pointing. Rank **Nice**. New place (possibly a monument merge: KW calls it a gemeentelijk monument).
title: Homomonument: three triangles that point somewhere
rank_text: Rank **Nice**. New place (possibly a monument merge: KW calls it a gemeentelijk monument).

heading: Sweep 3: war and memory / Grachtengordel-West
text: **AW-03 Reestraat 6: Anton de Kom's Amsterdam house.** Pin 52.372411, 4.884141 (Mapping Slavery marker), Reestraat 6. The anti-colonial writer of "Wij slaven van Suriname" (1934) lived here in 1935, after the colonial government arrested him in 1933 for "communist propaganda" and sent him away; he died in a concentration camp in 1945 for his part in the resistance. His house in Paramaribo collapsed a few years ago; this one survives because Stadsherstel bought the near-ruined shop-house in 1968 (only the ground floor stood) and rebuilt it, timber frame and all, by 1970; it was a milk shop for half a century. Local voice: Stadsherstel, "Zijn huis in Paramaribo is helaas enkele jaren geleden ingestort, maar gelukkig bestaat dit pand in Amsterdam nog". Lead: https://mappingslavery.nl/kaarten-2/kaarten-nederland/amsterdam/ . Second: https://stadsherstel.nl/monumenten/reestraat-6/ ; https://www.hekjesenslootjes.nl/node/771 . Status: Stadsherstel page current 2026 (now part of the Pulitzer hotel). Caveats: whether a plaque marks the house is not stated anywhere I read (check on site); nl.wikipedia (Reestraat) dates his stay to the 1920s, Mapping Slavery and Stadsherstel to 1935: use 1935. De Kom's 4en5mei stone (4544) is in the Nieuwe Kerk (Core zone, A-list). Rank **Nice**. New place.
title: Reestraat 6: Anton de Kom's Amsterdam house

heading: Sweep 3: war and memory / Jordaan
text: **AW-04 The old gym, Nieuwe Passeerdersstraat 1: "Aan onze gevallen makkers".** Pin 52.366563, 4.879384 (4en5mei; address pin 52.366431, 4.879105). A white stone figure raising his arms to the sky, by Hendrik Dannenburg, on the front of a late-19th-century gymnasium, for the Jewish sportsmen killed in the war. From 1 November 1941 Jews were barred from sports clubs; in January 1945 the occupier turned this same turnhal into the registration office of the Arbeitseinsatz, and on 8 January 1945 the resistance tried to blow it up and failed. Unveiled on Saturday afternoon 3 May 1952 by alderman F. van Wijck. Lead: 4en5mei 1601. Second: to find (nl.wikipedia list of war memorials in Amsterdam-Centrum not yet checked). Status: register 2026. Caveat: the building's present use is not in the source. Rank **Nice**. New place.
title: The old gym, Nieuwe Passeerdersstraat 1: "Aan onze gevallen makkers"

heading: Sweep 3: war and memory / Jordaan
text: **AW-05 Jordaanoproer, Noordermarkt: the woman on the table.** Pin 52.379398, 4.886411 (KW), Noordermarkt by the Noorderkerk. Sofie Hupkens's 1987 group of two women and a man bound by one broad hand, for the riot in the week of 4 July 1934 against cuts in the dole: five dead and dozens wounded. The front woman is modelled on the woman who that evening climbed on a table and said "Ik krijg nu zeven gulden minder". Text on the base: "Eenheid sterkste keten Jordaanoproer 1934". Beside it the 1950 relief by E.J. Hoek for the Jordaan residents killed in the war (unveiled 3 May 1950, 4en5mei 1604). Local voice: the quoted woman. Lead: KW 494. Second: https://nl.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lijst_van_beelden_in_Amsterdam-Centrum (row 1987); for the Hoek relief 4en5mei 1604 and KW 503. Status: KW 2026; OSM. Caveats: DW-05 covers what locals point at on the square (and names the oproer row only as a source); keep separate or fold in. The Berta de Vries bridge (DW Look for) belongs to the same story. Rank **Nice**. Group with DW-05, or new place.
title: Jordaanoproer, Noordermarkt: the woman on the table

heading: Sweep 2: public art and walls / Jordaan
text: **AW-06 The London Police corner, Prinsengracht at the Tuinstraat.** Pin 52.377833, 4.885574 (SAC 896), Prinsengracht 64, side wall on the Tuinstraat. The Amsterdam-based duo's round-eyed "lads" cover a wall that was a dumping spot for bulky rubbish, whose owner spent time and money every year on removing graffiti; the mural stopped it. Around the corner the Tuinstraat and Egelantiersstraat carry the zone's densest patch of small street art (SAC lists 12 active pieces within 100 m, among them "Wednesday Addams"). Local voice: the Jordaan murals initiative, "Bewoners van de Jordaan kunnen zich vast nog wel herinneren dat dit vroeger een plek was waar mensen hun grofvuil deponeerden" (WJGR 2012, 00000044). Lead: WJGR 2012, 00000044. Second: SAC 896 (marked "seen" 15 times; last seen 19 October 2026); OSM mural. Status: October 2026. Caveat: street art changes; the small pieces around it come and go. Rank **Nice**. New place.
title: The London Police corner, Prinsengracht at the Tuinstraat

heading: Sweep 2: public art and walls / Jordaan
text: **AW-07 Vaste klant, Looiersgracht 40B: a statue paid for a bar tab.** Pin 52.368656, 4.881400 (OSM; address pin 52.368675, 4.881391), on the bench of café Festina Lente. Albert Zweep, a regular here as a young artist, drank on credit until the bill could not be paid, and settled it with a statue: a sad old regular stroking the café cat, modelled on the characters of Carmiggelt's "Kronkels" (1997). Vandals kept knocking the head off; he repaired it again and again until Heineken paid for a bronze version; since 2020 he has worn a face mask. Local voice: the artist (2021), the work he is proudest of. Lead: https://nl.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vaste_klant . Second: NRC, "De Vaste Klant", 1 May 2020 (https://www.nrc.nl/nieuws/2020/05/01/de-vaste-klant-a3998202); OSM. Status: May 2020; mask photos (Wikipedia). Caveats: on a café terrace (borderline food and drink, but the statue is the point); the café was called Café Looiers when it was placed. Rank **Nice**. New place.
title: Vaste klant, Looiersgracht 40B: a statue paid for a bar tab

heading: Sweep 2: public art and walls / Jordaan
text: **AW-08 Volksvrouw, Marnixplein: a communist sculptor's wife in bronze.** Pin 52.377843, 4.879064 (OSM, Marnixplein). Half-length woman with folded arms, for the women of the crisis years who kept their heads above water; Henk Henriët (1903 to 1945), a communist artist who knew poverty himself, used his wife Tonia as model. The plaster stood in the Stedelijk after his memorial exhibition of 1946 and was cast in bronze only in 1967. Lead: KW 490. Second: https://nl.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lijst_van_beelden_in_Amsterdam-Centrum (Marnixplein row). Status: KW 2026. Caveat: KW's pin (52.374473, 4.876642) is on the Tweede Marnixplantsoen while its text says Marnixplein; OSM has it on the Marnixplein: check. Rank **Okay**. New place (or group with AW-09).
title: Volksvrouw, Marnixplein: a communist sculptor's wife in bronze

heading: Sweep 2: public art and walls / Jordaan
text: **AW-09 De Baadster: Krop's bather who got lost and came back.** Pin 52.378178, 4.878224 (KW), Marnixbad, Marnixplein 1. Hildo Krop's limestone nude whose long hair turns into a wave (1954 to 1956) decorated the 1955 public baths. When the pool was demolished in 2004 the city promised to put her back on the new building; the drawings showed her, nobody prepared it, the then director was said to be against it, and the stone went missing "door een miscommunicatie". Krop's grandson fought for years with Heemschut's monumental-art group; at seven in the morning of 13 February 2019 a crane put her back. Beside the pool, René Nyssen's little bronze "Diploma A" of two children treading water, with "Alle eendjes zwemmen in het water" and a slow film of water running over them (KW 493). Local voice: the grandson in De Volkskrant (18 February 2016), "Maar van die terugplaatsing kwam tot dusver niets terecht". Lead: Hildo Krop Museum, Nieuwsbrief 20, March 2019 (https://hildokropmuseum.nl/wp-content/uploads/pdfs/20-nieuwsbrief-mrt-2019.pdf). Second: KW 589; Wandkunst (Marnixbad entry, written before the return). Status: replaced February 2019. Rank **Nice**. New place.
title: De Baadster: Krop's bather who got lost and came back

heading: Sweep 2: public art and walls / Jordaan
text: **AW-10 Tweede Marnixplantsoen: Naatje who came home and a poem down a stair.** Pin 52.374417, 4.876083 (KW 590, De trap). A small statue strip on the Singelgracht side: Hanna Mobach's "Nieuwe Naatje" (model Marja Meijer; base "Op 15 mei 1975 ter ere van Amsterdam 700 weer thuisgebracht"), which stood on the Rokin until the metro works of 2003, then on the Bullebaksluis (2005), and here "temporarily" since 2008; Steffen Maas's stone stair "De trap" with a poem by K. Schippers about the plantsoen running down its treads ("Heb je de treden net vluchtig bekeken ..."). The anonymous sculptor's running man with a violin case (KW 548) stands at the corner: he went missing and came back painted blue (group with DW-02). Lead: KW 509, 590, 548. Second: OSM (Naatje, Man met vioolkist); https://nl.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lijst_van_beelden_in_Amsterdam-Centrum . Status: KW 2026. Caveat: Pjotr Müller's "Steen in drieën gespleten" in the same plantsoen is to be removed (damaged, KW 489). Rank **Okay**. New place (the running man to DW-02).
title: Tweede Marnixplantsoen: Naatje who came home and a poem down a stair

heading: Sweep 2: public art and walls / Jordaan
text: **AW-11 Energie en tijd: Verhulst on the substation.** Pin 52.370340, 4.875734 (Wandkunst), Marnixstraat 212 at the Lauriergracht. A concrete and steel wall sculpture of 1962 by Hans Verhulst on the city's biggest electricity substation of its day (11.5 million guilders, opened June 1962), on the site where the English gasworks "de Engelsman" stood: energy on the same spot for over a century. The register rates it "Top"; best seen from the Lauriergracht and the Nassaukade. Lead: Wandkunst register. Second: https://nl.wikipedia.org/wiki/Energie_en_tijd ; OSM. Status: Wikipedia photo 2022. Rank **Nice**. New place.

heading: Sweep 2: public art and walls / Jordaan
text: **AW-12 Spelen in de Stad: a pupil's line on the school wall.** Pin 52.376883, 4.881215 (KW), Tuinstraat 172G, Theo Thijssenschool. Piet Parra's giant lettering of one pupil's one-line poem, chosen from the class's entries on "playing in the city": "Ik speel in de stad, met alles wat er bestaat" (Lisa van de Schouw). Commissioned by Ymere. Local voice: the murals initiative cites it as the newest good example (WJGR 2012, 00000044). Lead: KW 567. Second: WJGR 2012, 00000044. Status: KW 2026. Rank **Okay**. heading: Sweep 2: public art and walls / Haarlemmerbuurt with the Western Islands
text: **AW-13 Mono no aware II: graffiti's grandmother under a bridge that will go.** Pin 52.381855, 4.890108 (KW), underpass of the car bridge at the Korte Prinsengracht. Mick La Rock, one of the first women graffiti writers in Europe, covered the bridge walls (2023) with black geometric lines that abstract the outlines of her old graffiti pieces and the sunlight on the canal; the Japanese title means the awareness that everything passes, and the bridge will probably be demolished. Commissioned by the city with Mokumse Muurtjes; residents had a say in the choice of artist. The same tunnel is "Filmset aan het IJ" (KW 579), a light-art frame for changing temporary installations. Local voice: La Rock, "Als iemand mij 25 jaar geleden had gezegd dat ik in 2023 de opdracht zou krijgen van de gemeente om een gigantische brugmuur te bekleden, dan had ik keihard gelachen van ongeloof." Lead: KW 2771. Second: SAC "Mono No Aware II" (active). Status: active 2026. Rank **Nice**. New place.
title: Mono no aware II: graffiti's grandmother under a bridge that will go

heading: Sweep 2: public art and walls / Haarlemmerbuurt with the Western Islands
text: **AW-14 De Aardige Amsterdammer, Droogbak: a hand for the volunteers.** Pin 52.380316, 4.894451 (OSM), Droogbak 1A. An outstretched hand for the volunteers who help homeless and lonely people, by Klaas Hartzema, who works with the homeless, with the Regenboog Groep; each year the volunteer of the year is announced here. The first one (2012, unveiled with mayor Van der Laan) was made of a kind of foam and was stolen on King's Day 2015; he and Laszlo Gèleng made a new one that October; it was badly damaged again in 2024. Local voice: Hartzema, "Het beeld was niet hufterproof, het was van een soort schuim gemaakt." Lead: Het Parool, 18 October 2015 (https://www.parool.nl/kunst-media/nieuw-beeld-voor-aardige-amsterdammer-na-diefstal~b127fc7a/). Second: KW 554; Wikimedia Commons "De Aardige Amsterdammer 2.jpg". Status: damaged May 2024 (artist's LinkedIn post title); repaired state unknown. Rank **Nice**. New place.
title: De Aardige Amsterdammer, Droogbak: a hand for the volunteers

heading: Sweep 2: public art and walls / Haarlemmerbuurt with the Western Islands
text: **AW-15 Vinkenstraat: a wall that makes you see suns.** Pin 52.382613, 4.886316 (KW 566), Vinkenstraat 83. Roland Schimmel's "1000 zonnen" (2009, for De Key): stare at the black circles and coloured after-images appear, the halo effect he works with. A few steps on, Cyril Lixenberg's folded-steel "Getrapt vierkant" and the little square he designed (1981; he worked from folded and cut paper). At Vinkenstraat 164, the gable stone 't Nachtglas, a ship's four-hour sandglass for the night watch, found in 1987 when the house was demolished and named in no deed (VVAG). Lead: KW 566, 526. Second: OSM (Getrapt vierkant, 1981); VVAG vinkenstraat-164-amsterdam-nachtglas. Status: KW 2026. Rank **Okay**. New place.
title: Vinkenstraat: a wall that makes you see suns

text: **AW-16 Nelson Mandela's vegetable garden, Prinseneiland.** Pin 52.385643, 4.887646 (address pin Prinseneiland 1, corner of the Galgenstraat; approximate). A mural on the corner house, "Nelson Mandela's moestuin te Pollsmoor": the garden he fought to grow on the prison roof in oil drums between 1982 and 1988. heading: Sweep 2: public art and walls / Haarlemmerbuurt with the Western Islands
text: **AW-17 Wubboboom, Haarlemmerplein: an elm for an astronaut.** Pin 52.384217, 4.884151 (address pin Haarlemmerplein 1; approximate, the tree stands "in een hoek" of the square). A living memorial for Wubbo Ockels (died 18 May 2014), announced at his memorial service in the Westerkerk and unveiled in November 2014 before some 200 people with his widow: an elm of a variety said to live 500 years, chosen for its odd leaf colour, with benches carrying his lines "Optimisme is een verantwoordelijkheid" and "We zijn allemaal astronaut van Ruimteschip Aarde". Lead: https://nl.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wubboboom . Second: AT5, https://www.at5.nl/artikelen/136914/wubbo-boom-op-haarlemmerplein-onthuld ; NOS 8 November 2014. Status: Wikipedia photo 2015. heading: Sweep 2: public art and walls / Grachtengordel-West
text: **AW-20 The cat on Herengracht 395.** Pin 52.368232, 4.887093 (address pin Herengracht 395). A metal cat crawls along the front above the round window; amsterdamopdekaart's caption for the 1882 building is simply "Let op de kat!". One source says resident Fred Fraay put up a cat and a mouse on either side, years ago. Lead: https://nl.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lijst_van_beelden_in_Amsterdam-Centrum (row "Kat tegen gevel boven het ronde raam", maker unknown, 1980 to 2000). Second: https://amsterdamopdekaart.nl/1850-1940/Herengracht/395 . Status: unknown date. Caveats: the Fraay and mouse claim comes from an app's fun-facts page only; find the mouse on site or drop the claim. Rank **Okay**. New place (DW listed it as a lead).
title: The cat on Herengracht 395

heading: Sweep 2: gable stones by street
text: **AW-21 Bloemgracht: the townsman, the farmer and the sailor.** Pin 52.374285, 4.879668 (address pin Bloemgracht 89), Jordaan. The street with the Jordaan's best stones. At 87, 89 and 91, three identical step gables of the 1640s carry DE STEEMAN, DE LANDMAN and DE SEEMAN, owned by Hendrick de Keyser since 1927 and 1929 ("De Drie Hendricken", "de parels van de Jordaan"). They do not show the residents' trades: they show three ways of living in the Golden Age, the townsman, the farmer and the sailor; a resident linked them to a 1642 poem by Cornelis Biens. At 77 and 81 DE SAAYER and DE JONGE SAAYER, a sower on a ploughed field, marked two neighbouring sugar refineries working sugar from Suriname and Brazil. Also on the street: De Son and De Maen (1648), Jakobs droom (168) and De Doos (10), the last two already DW Look for lines. Local voice: VVAG quoting the resident-author, "tot lering en vermaak". Lead: VVAG bloemgracht-87-89-91-amsterdam-steeman-landman-seeman and bloemgracht-77-81-amsterdam-saayer. Second: GS.net (Bloemgracht rows); Maandblad Amstelodamum 95 pp. 3 to 15 (cited by VVAG). Status: VVAG 2026. Caveat: 87 to 91 are listed buildings: likely merge with their monument records. Rank **Amazing**. New place or monument merge.
title: Bloemgracht: the townsman, the farmer and the sailor
rank_text: Rank **Amazing**. New place or monument merge.

heading: Sweep 2: gable stones by street
text: **AW-22 Palmgracht: the cauliflower next to the cabbage.** Pin 52.381821, 4.882871 (address pin Palmgracht 63), Jordaan. GS.net counts 17 stones on this short canal-that-is-a-street. DE BLOMKOOL (63, named in 1679) was a pun: the neighbour on both sides was Willem Harmensz Cool, and number 61 had "de Kool". IN DE BATAVIER (64) copies a musketeer from De Gheyn's 1607 drill manual. DE RAKSASA VAN MALANG (68, 2009) is a new stone: the VVAG chairman Jos Otten, born in Malang, had Hans 't Mannetje carve a Javanese temple guardian from Singosari, on the spot where the old stone De Doos had sat. Also the Suyker Ried fronton, moved here in 2008. Lead: VVAG palmgracht-63-amsterdam-blomkool, palmgracht-64-amsterdam-batavier, palmgracht-68-amsterdam-raksasa. Second: GS.net. Status: VVAG 2026. Rank **Nice**. Group with BW-02 (Raepenhofje, on the same street) or BW-26, or new place.
title: Palmgracht: the cauliflower next to the cabbage
rank_text: Rank **Nice**. Group with BW-02 (Raepenhofje, on the same street) or BW-26, or new place.

heading: Sweep 2: gable stones by street
text: **AW-23 Lindengracht 206 to 220: the builders' row.** Pin 52.380141, 4.883096 (address pin Lindengracht 212), Jordaan. A philanthropic housing block whose eight stones honour the building trades in turn: in den metselaer, timmerman, schilder, smid, stucadoor, loodgieter, grondwerker, steenhouwer. Lead: https://www.amsterdam-monumentenstad.nl/database/grachtenboek_objecten.php?id=6789 . Second: https://amsterdamopdekaart.nl/1850-1940/Lindengracht/206-220 (rijksmonument 518316). Status: listed. Caveat: date and builder not read. Rank **Okay**. Monument merge (518316).
title: Lindengracht 206 to 220: the builders' row

heading: Sweep 2: gable stones by street
text: **AW-24 Brouwersgracht: a bag of coins and a cowherd who stayed home.** Pin 52.380093, 4.888648 (address pin Brouwersgracht 97), Grachtengordel-West (the row runs into the Haarlemmerbuurt at 94). EEN SAK SESTHALVE (97): a tied money bag with "VRIENDEN SIET / EEN SAK SESTHALVE / GEEF IK NIET", dated 18 September 1772, brought from the back wall of Reestraat 19 by Stadsherstel; what it meant is unknown. 't SMACK ZEYL (101), on the corner café, bought by Stadsherstel at an auction in 1955. DE KOE W8CHTER BLIJFT THUIS (94), a modern stone: the arms of the owner's Zeeland birth village Koewacht with the Amsterdam arms hidden in the middle tree, for the Amsterdam-born wife; "W8" reads "wacht". Lead: VVAG brouwersgracht-97-amsterdam-sak-sesthalve, brouwersgracht-94-amsterdam-koewachter. Second: GS.net. Status: VVAG 2026. Rank **Nice**. New place.
title: Brouwersgracht: a bag of coins and a cowherd who stayed home

heading: Sweep 2: gable stones by street
text: **AW-25 Haarlemmerdijk: the widow called Sluys and the shepherd behind the cash machine.** Pin 52.383177, 4.886093 (address pin Haarlemmerdijk 109), Haarlemmerbuurt. SLUYS (109) shows a little town by the water that everyone took for Sluis in Zeeland; house research found it was the name of Vrouwtje Sluijs, widow of Eymert van Veen, who bought the house on 16 March 1730. The early-18th-century shepherd with his flock went from number 101 into the post office hall around 1910, vanished behind a cash machine in 1989, and was saved in 1995 when the VVAG chairman told his story loudly in the builders' cabin; it now sits over the gateway of 98 to 100 (already a DW Look for line). Also IN LANGEN DYCK and LANACDICK at 79 and 81, two spellings of the same place. Lead: VVAG haarlemmerdijk-109-amsterdam-sluys, haarlemmerdijk-98-100-amsterdam-herder. Second: WJGR 2018 (shepherd, per DW). Status: VVAG 2026. Rank **Nice**. New place.
title: Haarlemmerdijk: the widow called Sluys and the shepherd behind the cash machine

heading: Sweep 2: gable stones by street
text: **AW-26 Nine Streets: stones saved from demolitions.** Pin 52.370409, 4.885108 (address pin Wolvenstraat 32), Grachtengordel-West. Wolvenstraat 32 carries DIE OUWE WILDEWOLF and DE VERLOOREN ARBEYD, saved when their houses were pulled down in 1950; Berenstraat 7 has a stone for the street itself; Huidenstraat 2 the Oranjeappel orphanage gate. Lead: VVAG Wolvenstraat 32, Berenstraat 7 and Huidenstraat 2 pages. Second: GS.net. Status: VVAG 2026. Caveat: weaker stories; may serve better as a Look for line in a Nine Streets text. Rank **Okay**. New place or Look for.

heading: Sweep 4: hidden history / Burgwallen-Nieuwe Zijde
text: **BC-01. The two houses the Victoria Hotel could not buy.** Pin 52.377144, 4.898038; Damrak 1 corner Prins Hendrikkade (the two small dark gables built into the hotel front, old nos. 46-47). Hook: in 1889 the hotel company bought and demolished the whole corner except two early 17th-century houses whose owners, tailor Pieter August Carstens and spirits dealer Johannes Frederik Verburgt, asked too much; the hotel was built around them. No. 46 was a knife shop from 1602 to 1742. The story inspired Thomas Rozenboom's novel "Publieke Werken" (Libris Prize 2000, filmed 2015). Local voice: Amsterdamsche Courant, 10 June 1889: "De perceelen van den kleermaker Karsten en den slijter Verburgt werden wegens te hooge eischen niet gekocht en zullen vermoedelijk worden ingebouwd." Lead: https://www.onh.nl/verhalen/de-huisjes-van-het-victoria-hotel-amsterdam ; second https://nl.wikipedia.org/wiki/Victoria_Hotel . Status: standing, a souvenir shop inside (ONH, undated, checked 2026-11-24 from text only). Caveats: monument status of the two houses not checked. Rank: **Amazing**. New place.
title: The two houses the Victoria Hotel could not buy

heading: Sweep 4: hidden history / Burgwallen-Nieuwe Zijde
text: **BC-02. Nieuwezijds Kolk: the castle under the street and the corn measurers' house.** Pin 52.376110, 4.895000; Nieuwezijds Kolk (Korenmetershuisje). Hook: in 1994 digging for new building at the Nieuwezijds Kolk found foundations of a brick castle (built c. 1280-1290, probably by Floris V, gone by 1304), counted as the oldest structure of Amsterdam; possible castle remains also lie under Dirk van Hasseltssteeg 2-6. Beside it stands the Korenmetershuisje (1620), the guild house of the corn measurers with measure, barrel and strickle carved over the door, one of the few guild houses left and one of the few free-standing buildings in the old centre. Local voice: "Kasteel aan de Amstel". Lead: https://nl.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kasteel_van_Amsterdam ; second https://nl.wikipedia.org/wiki/Korenmetershuisje_(Amsterdam) . Status: guild house standing (rijksmonument); the castle is underground, no marker found in the sources read. Caveats: check on site for any paving marker. Rank: Nice. New place.
title: Nieuwezijds Kolk: the castle under the street and the corn measurers' house

heading: Sweep 4: hidden history / Burgwallen-Nieuwe Zijde
text: **BC-03. Torensluis: the footprint of the Jan Roodenpoort tower.** Pin 52.374440, 4.889720; Singel at the Torensteeg. Hook: the widest bridge of its day was built beside the Jan Roodenpoortstoren, a medieval wall tower given a 55 m spire in 1616-17 (probably Hendrick de Keyser) that served as public clock tower and prison; the provost lived below. The tower went in 1829 because the poor city could not maintain it, as did the Haringpakkerstoren at the Singel's IJ end. The vaulted cellars in the bridgehead survive; Stadsherstel shows a photo of the tower's footprint on the Torensluis. Both towers were measured before demolition so they could be rebuilt; Stadsherstel offered to rebuild the Haringpakkerstoren for its 50th birthday and backed off on 12 April 2010 for fear of the UNESCO nomination. Local voice: neighbours on the Singel lived "bij de Toren" (Stadsherstel, from the archives). Lead: https://nl.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jan_Roodenpoortstoren ; second https://stadsherstel.nl/monumenten/singel-157/ . Status: cellars said to be open to the public after restoration (nl.wiki), current use not verified 2026-11-24. Caveats: Multatuli statue sits on the same bridge (not this theme). Rank: Nice. Group with: Haringpakkerstoren (gone, corner Singel/Prins Hendrikkade, pin 52.379170, 4.895280 NZ).
title: Torensluis: the footprint of the Jan Roodenpoort tower
rank_text: Rank: Nice. Group with: Haringpakkerstoren (gone, corner Singel/Prins Hendrikkade, pin 52.379170, 4.895280 NZ).

heading: Sweep 4: hidden history / Burgwallen-Nieuwe Zijde
text: **BC-04. The Heilige Stede site: the miracle chapel's replacement.** Pin 52.370220, 4.891870; Rokin between Wijde and Enge Kapelsteeg. Hook: the chapel built in 1346-47 where the Miracle of Amsterdam (1345) happened became a Protestant chapel, then a horse stable after 1578; Catholics revived the procession as the silent Stille Omgang in 1881 from a 1651 route document, and the Reformed church demolished the chapel in 1908 despite protests. The 1912 replacement (church plus shops) saw Princess Beatrix confirmed in 1956, was a Turkish mosque 1972-1980 and a conference centre after.
