Local voice: "Nieuwezijds Kapel"; the procession "Stille Omgang". Lead: https://nl.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nieuwezijds_Kapel_(1912) ; second https://nl.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heilige_Stede . Status: building standing (rijksmonument since 2001), a tourist attraction inside since 2005. Caveats: DC dropped the Mirakelkolom as thin; this is the building, not the column. Rank: Okay. New place.
title: The Heilige Stede site: the miracle chapel's replacement

heading: Sweep 4: hidden history / Burgwallen-Nieuwe Zijde
text: **BC-05. Hotel Polen fire, 1977.** Pin 52.372197, 4.892578; Papenbroekssteeg through Rokin Plaza, Rokin/Kalverstraat. Hook: on 9 May 1977 Hotel Polen burned down: 33 dead, the deadliest fire in the Netherlands since the Second World War; the wooden-framed building had no smoke detectors and had failed a fire inspection. Rokin Plaza (1981-83) replaced it, with the Papenbroekssteeg running through. Part of the hotel's De Distel tile tableau survives in the Keramisch Museum Goedewagen. Local voice: the name came from the "Poolsche Koffiehuis" in the Kalverstraat. Lead: https://nl.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brand_in_Hotel_Polen . Status: gone, exact spot known. Caveats: no on-site memorial found in sources read; single source. Rank: Okay. New place.
title: Hotel Polen fire, 1977

heading: Sweep 4: hidden history / Burgwallen-Nieuwe Zijde
text: **BC-06. De Papegaai, the Kalverstraat hidden church.** Pin 52.371236, 4.891831; Kalverstraat 58. Hook: a Catholic station church from 1672 in a rented house on the shopping street; the house had a compass on its gable (owner Willem Compas), yet the church was nicknamed the Parrot. The present church (1848-49) was the first neo-Gothic church in Amsterdam. Local voice: "De Papegaai". Lead: https://nl.wikipedia.org/wiki/De_Papegaai_(Amsterdam) . Status: open church. Caveats: single source; check opening hours. Rank: Nice. New place.
title: De Papegaai, the Kalverstraat hidden church

heading: Sweep 4: hidden history / Burgwallen-Nieuwe Zijde
text: **BC-07. Kromelleboogsteeg and the Roode Leeuw stones.** Pin 52.372504, 4.892140; Kalverstraat 1 (behind Dam 20). Hook: Kalverstraat 1-5 run back to the closed Kromelleboogsteeg, the alley once called "Roode Leeuwsteeg" after the inn De Roode Leeuw (from 1454) on its corner with the Dam. Gable stones on the Peek & Cloppenburg building still show a lion with "Roode Leeuw". Kalverstraat 1 is an early Wijdeveld design (1915-17, jeweller Citroen). Local voice: "Rooleeuwsteegje". Lead: https://nl.wikipedia.org/wiki/De_Roode_Leeuw_(Amsterdam) ; second https://nl.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kalverstraat_1 . Status: alley closed; stones visible. Rank: Okay. New place.
title: Kromelleboogsteeg and the Roode Leeuw stones

heading: Sweep 4: hidden history / Burgwallen-Nieuwe Zijde
text: **BC-08. The Singel doelen and the 1606 armoury.** Pin 52.367981, 4.889342; Singel 421-425. Hook: Singel 421 is the Handboogdoelen (c. 1509), the archers' guild house, nicknamed "Garnalendoelen"; next to it the Militiegebouw (1606), the city armoury with tall doors for the cannon, later a silk-winding workhouse for girls (1682), the French conscription hall, the city council chamber in 1926-28, and the room where Max Euwe played part of his 1935 world title match against Alekhine. The crossbowmen's Voetboogdoelen beside it became the West India Company headquarters in 1674; its site and that of the Sint-Catharinakerk (demolished 1939) became the University Library. Lead: https://nl.wikipedia.org/wiki/Militiegebouw ; second https://nl.wikipedia.org/wiki/Handboogdoelen_(Amsterdam) . Status: standing; the University Library left the complex in autumn 2025 (nl.wiki), new use unknown. Caveats: check access. Rank: Nice. New place.
title: The Singel doelen and the 1606 armoury

heading: Sweep 4: hidden history / Burgwallen-Nieuwe Zijde
text: **BC-09. Oude Lutherse Kerk: Lutherans in a warehouse.** Pin 52.368330, 4.889148; Singel 411 corner Spui. Hook: from 1600 Lutherans worshipped in a warehouse called De Vergulden Pot on this spot; the church followed in 1632-33. Lead: https://nl.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oude_Lutherse_Kerk . Status: standing, used by the University of Amsterdam for ceremonies (to verify). Rank: Okay. New place.
title: Oude Lutherse Kerk: Lutherans in a warehouse

heading: Sweep 4: hidden history / Burgwallen-Nieuwe Zijde
text: **BC-10. Die Port van Cleve: where Heineken began.** Pin 52.374125, 4.890771; Nieuwezijds Voorburgwal 176-180. Hook: brewery De Hooiberg stood here from 1592 (the widow Weyntgen Elberts); Gerard Adriaan Heineken bought it in 1863 and moved the brewing to the Stadhouderskade once the Nieuwezijds Achterburgwal was filled in; the builders converting it to a beer house found the gable stone "Die Port van Cleve" that gave the name (1870). Spuistraat 129-131 (gable cartouche 1662) belonged to the complex. Lead: https://nl.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hotel_Die_Port_van_Cleve ; second https://nl.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spuistraat_129-131_(Amsterdam) . Status: hotel. Caveats: commercial hotel; the hook is the brewery site. Rank: Okay. New place.
title: Die Port van Cleve: where Heineken began

heading: Sweep 4: hidden history / Burgwallen-Nieuwe Zijde
text: **BC-11. Olieslagerssteeg: leper house, oil pressers and Maison de Bonneterie.** Pin 52.368060, 4.891940; Olieslagerssteeg, Kalverstraat/Rokin. Hook: Amsterdam's first leper house, the Sint Jorishof, stood on the Kalverstraat here; its chapel became the carpenters' guild house (the "Kistenmakerspand"); oil pressers worked in the alley and sold Haarlemmerolie as a cure-all; in 1901 Maison de Bonneterie replaced the chapel (rijksmonument since 1974; ONH describes its 1909 interior). Lead: https://nl.wikipedia.org/wiki/Olieslagerssteeg_(Amsterdam) ; second https://nl.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sint_Jorishof_(Amsterdam) and https://www.onh.nl/verhalen/modepaleizen-in-amsterdam . Status: steeg open; store status not verified 2026-11-24. Rank: Okay. New place.
title: Olieslagerssteeg: leper house, oil pressers and Maison de Bonneterie

heading: Sweep 4: hidden history / Burgwallen-Oude Zijde
text: **BC-12. Sint Olofspoort: houses on the gate and the chapel wall.** Pin 52.376284, 4.899940; Sint Olofspoort 1, Nieuwebrugsteeg 13, Sint Olofssteeg 8. Hook: the Sint Olofspoort, a city gate beside the 15th-century Sint-Olofskapel, was demolished in 1618 and houses were built on its site. Sint Olofspoort 1 (c. 1605) uses the chapel's west wall as its back wall; nos. 9-15 were sold in 1618 on condition of not using the old gate wall. Nieuwebrugsteeg 13 was the very first house bought by Vereniging Hendrick de Keyser (1918), with a gable stone of a hat maker's workshop ("hoede kramer"). Round the corner Het Jopenvat (1659) fills a triangular plot between two alleys under a beer-barrel stone. Local voice: the gate name survives as the street name "Sint Olofspoort". Lead: https://www.hendrickdekeyser.nl/de-huizen/nieuwebrugsteeg-13 ; second https://www.hendrickdekeyser.nl/de-huizen/sint-olofspoort-1 and https://www.hendrickdekeyser.nl/de-huizen/het-jopenvat , https://nl.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sint-Olofskapel . Status: standing, private (HdK rents them). Rank: **Amazing**. New place.
title: Sint Olofspoort: houses on the gate and the chapel wall

heading: Sweep 4: hidden history / Burgwallen-Oude Zijde
text: **BC-13. Het Aepgen, the wooden house on the Zeedijk.** Pin 52.376486, 4.899364; Zeedijk 1. Hook: c. 1550, one of only two wooden house fronts left in the city; the legend says sailors paid their lodging with monkeys. Local voice: "in de aap gelogeerd" (to be had, from the monkey lodging story). Lead: https://www.hendrickdekeyser.nl/de-huizen/het-aepgen ; second https://www.hendrickdekeyser.nl/nieuws/huis-uitgelicht-het-aepgen . Status: standing, café In 't Aepjen downstairs. Caveats: the monkey payment is legend; well known locally. Rank: Nice. New place.
title: Het Aepgen, the wooden house on the Zeedijk

heading: Sweep 4: hidden history / Burgwallen-Oude Zijde
text: **BC-14. Spooksteeg: the ghost of the Zeedijk.** Pin 52.375144, 4.900899; Spooksteeg, between Zeedijk and Oudezijds Achterburgwal. Hook: in July 1753 and again in 1853 wailing was heard here that searches could not trace; the 1853 scare drew crowds every night and the alley was renamed from Waterpoortsteeg to Spooksteeg in 1855. The legend blames Helena, who killed her sister Dina over a sailor. Local voice: Algemeen Handelsblad 1853: "sedert een tiental dagen, duizenden elke avond naar de Zeedijk, waar, zo heet het, een spook door akelige geluiden de rust van eenige huizen stoort." Lead: https://www.onh.nl/verhalen/het-spook-van-de-zeedijk . Status: alley open. Caveats: DC dropped this for blogs only; ONH now gives the 1853 newspaper quote; the sisters' tale is legend. Rank: Okay. New place.
title: Spooksteeg: the ghost of the Zeedijk

heading: Sweep 4: hidden history / Burgwallen-Oude Zijde
text: **BC-15. Mata Hari and the Determeyer skybridge.** Pin 52.374666, 4.899855; Korte Niezel, Oudezijds Voorburgwal 27-33. Hook: uniform maker Determeyer bought one house after another and in 1929 built a covered bridge over the Korte Niezel to join the upper floors; it still carries the departed firm's name. From the early 1970s the complex was a notorious illegal gambling palace, "Mata Hari"; the city had housing corporation Ymere buy it in 2007 to stop it coming back. Lead: https://nl.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mata_Hari_(rijksmonument) . Status: standing (rijksmonument); bridge visible from the alley. Caveats: single source. Rank: Nice. New place.
title: Mata Hari and the Determeyer skybridge

heading: Sweep 4: hidden history / Burgwallen-Oude Zijde
text: **BC-16. Oudezijds Voorburgwal 61: four hundred years without piles.** Pin 52.374131, 4.899070. Hook: a late-16th-century merchant's house (roof timbers dated 1592-1596) with an osendrop on both sides; Stadsherstel's foundation survey found no piles at all: the walls stand straight on the ground ("op staal"). Later a doll factory "Hollandia" (1908) and a bicycle store in the cellar. Local voice: Stadsherstel, "Vierhonderd jaar zonder palen maar met bijzonder marmer". Lead: https://stadsherstel.nl/monumenten/oudezijds-voorburgwal-61/ . Status: standing, homes, restored 2018. Caveats: DC dropped this as single source; Stadsherstel is the owner and did the survey, which makes it the primary source. Rank: Okay. New place.
title: Oudezijds Voorburgwal 61: four hundred years without piles

heading: Sweep 4: hidden history / Burgwallen-Oude Zijde
text: **BC-17. Ship Chandlers Warehouse: all its 17th-century glass.** Pin 52.376176, 4.901939; Geldersekade 8. Hook: built 1623 as a tobacco shop, then a ship's chandler (Jan Vinke, 1804) whose grandson founded the shipbrokers Vinke & Co. here in 1860; it is said to be the only house in Amsterdam with original 17th-century leaded windows on every floor, and claims to be the city's oldest shop. Rococo tobacco ornament over the door (1775). Lead: https://nl.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ship_Chandlers_Warehouse . Status: standing. Caveats: "oldest shop" is a claim; ONH gives the pharmacy (BC-18) the same title. Rank: Nice. New place.
title: Ship Chandlers Warehouse: all its 17th-century glass

heading: Sweep 4: hidden history / Burgwallen-Oude Zijde
text: **BC-18. Apotheek Van der Meulen, a pharmacy since 1696.** Pin 52.374337, 4.900623 (approx); corner Geldersekade/Stormsteeg. Hook: apothecaries have worked on this corner without a break since 1696; the interior of about 1880 is painted in its original Berlin blue, Bentheim grey and ochre. Lead: https://www.onh.nl/verhalen/de-geldersekade-en-de-oudste-apotheek-van-amsterdam . Status: not verified 2026-11-24 (is it still a pharmacy?). Caveats: exact door not pinned. Rank: Nice. New place.
title: Apotheek Van der Meulen, a pharmacy since 1696

heading: Sweep 4: hidden history / Burgwallen-Oude Zijde
text: **BC-19. Geldersekade 78: the swindler Barmat.** Pin 52.374536, 4.901017. Hook: in the 1920s the "master swindler" Barmat ran a business here; his scandal became, against his will, a centrepiece of Hitler's antisemitic propaganda. Earlier a perfume factory and a tobacco trade. Local voice: Stadsherstel, "Hitler gebruikte deze meesteroplichter als schrikbeeld in zijn propaganda". Lead: https://stadsherstel.nl/monumenten/geldersekade-78/ . Status: standing, homes. Rank: Okay. New place.
title: Geldersekade 78: the swindler Barmat

heading: Sweep 4: hidden history / Burgwallen-Oude Zijde
text: **BC-20. The Bethaniën quarter: convent crypt, cows and Krishna.** Pin 52.372222, 4.898333; Barndesteeg/Bethaniënstraat. Hook: the north wing of the 15th-century Bethaniënklooster survives in the Barndesteeg with a vaulted crypt from about 1450; the nuns fattened cows for the civic guards' dinners, hence the Koestraat. In 1970 the first Hare Krishna temple in the Netherlands opened at Bethaniënstraat 37-39 ("500 years after the convent there were monks here again"). Local voice: Stadsherstel, "500 Jaar na het Bethaniënklooster waren hier weer monniken". Lead: https://nl.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bethani%C3%ABnklooster ; second https://stadsherstel.nl/monumenten/bethanienstraat-37-39/ . Status: standing (rijksmonument 1970), student rooms in the roof. Caveats: group with the existing draft "Barndesteeg" (places/oudezijde-1.yaml) and DC-18 (Koestraat). Rank: Nice. Group with: draft Barndesteeg.
title: The Bethaniën quarter: convent crypt, cows and Krishna
rank_text: Rank: Nice. Group with: draft Barndesteeg.

heading: Sweep 4: hidden history / Burgwallen-Oude Zijde
text: **BC-21. De Star: the wall of a vanished church, and the Spinhuis gate.** Pin 52.370670, 4.896360; Spinhuissteeg. Hook: the Augustinians' hidden church De Star (in a warehouse from 1698, rebuilt as a big hall church 1848-49) closed in 1929 as the centre emptied and was almost entirely demolished in 1955; only a long high wall with Ionic pilasters still stands in the Spinhuissteeg. Opposite, the Spinhuis gate recalls the women's house of correction of 1597 where inmates spun and sewed. Lead: https://nl.wikipedia.org/wiki/De_Star_(Amsterdam) ; second https://nl.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spinhuis_(Amsterdam) . Status: wall standing. Rank: Okay. New place.
title: De Star: the wall of a vanished church, and the Spinhuis gate

heading: Sweep 4: hidden history / Burgwallen-Oude Zijde
text: **BC-22. Pijlsteeg: an alley through a hotel.** Pin 52.372320, 4.895300; Dam to Oudezijds Voorburgwal. Hook: once the Apostolensteeg, renamed after mayor Dirk Pijl (late 14th century); a keurboek of 1413, one of the first Amsterdam documents on prostitution, names it one of the two streets where it was allowed. Now Hotel Krasnapolsky has built over and around it, but it stays public; three gable stones from demolished houses sit in the wall at the Wintertuin entrance, one a wooden chair "Anno 1728" from a chair maker's house. Lead: https://nl.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pijlsteeg_(Amsterdam) . Status: open. Caveats: Wynand Fockink is listed under Food and drink. Rank: Nice. New place.
title: Pijlsteeg: an alley through a hotel

heading: Sweep 4: hidden history / Burgwallen-Oude Zijde
text: **BC-23. The murder of Magere Josje, 1957.** Pin 52.373690, 4.898530; Oudezijds Voorburgwal 83. Hook: sex worker Johanna Scheide-Oudes, "Magere Josje", was found dead in her room on 11 August 1957; Appie Baantjer, then in the murder squad, led the case and never solved it. Local voice: "Magere Josje". Lead: https://nl.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moord_op_Magere_Josje . Status: house standing; nothing marks it. Caveats: single source; handle with care. Rank: Okay. New place.
title: The murder of Magere Josje, 1957

heading: Sweep 4: hidden history / Nieuwmarkt/Lastage
text: **BC-24. The Nieuwmarkt scaffold: Sjako and the only guillotine.** Pin 52.372573, 4.900503; Nieuwmarkt square. Hook: the master thief Sjako was broken on the wheel and beheaded here after his capture in 1717; on 15 June 1812 the French guillotine was used in Amsterdam for the first and only time, here, on poisoner Hester Rebekka Nepping, her lover and her maid. Local voice: Sjako, "de Robin Hood van Amsterdam". Lead: https://www.onh.nl/verhalen/de-guillotine-in-amsterdam ; second https://www.onh.nl/verhalen/sjako-robin-hood-amsterdam . Status: nothing marks it. Caveats: the Waag is A-list; this is the square's story, not the building. Rank: Okay. New place.
title: The Nieuwmarkt scaffold: Sjako and the only guillotine

heading: Sweep 4: hidden history / Nieuwmarkt/Lastage
text: **BC-25. Zuiderkerk: mortuary, oldest bell, the architect's grave.** Pin 52.370000, 4.899722. Hook: the first church built for Protestant worship in Amsterdam (1603-11, Hendrick de Keyser, the tower's niches left empty); in the Hunger Winter of 1944-45 it was a mortuary where the dead waited for burial. The tower still rings the "Salvator" (1511), the oldest bell in the city, taken from the Oude Kerk. De Keyser's gravestone can be seen through a glass plate in the floor. Tower visits with a guide in summer. Local voice: the bell's motto "Salvator vocor". Lead: https://www.onh.nl/verhalen/de-zuiderkerk-kerk-mortuarium-en-museum ; second https://nl.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zuiderkerkstoren_(Amsterdam) . Status: open (exhibition space). Caveats: DC parked two Zuiderkerk lines for "a Zuiderkerk place": fold them in. Rank: Nice. New place.
title: Zuiderkerk: mortuary, oldest bell, the architect's grave

heading: Sweep 4: hidden history / Nieuwmarkt/Lastage
text: **BC-26. Mozes en Aäronkerk: the Moroccans' church asylum, 1975.** Pin 52.368279, 4.902911; Waterlooplein 205. Hook: from 7 to 15 November 1975 about a hundred undocumented Moroccan workers went on hunger strike in the church; on 17 October 1978 these "kerkmarokkanen" got residence permits. Local voice: "kerkmarokkanen". Lead: https://www.onh.nl/verhalen/wereldplek-in-amsterdam-mozes-en-aaronkerk-verleende-kerkasiel . Status: church standing. Caveats: single source. Rank: Nice. New place.
title: Mozes en Aäronkerk: the Moroccans' church asylum, 1975

heading: Sweep 4: hidden history / Nieuwmarkt/Lastage
text: **BC-27. Cold War shelters under the metro.** Pin 52.366958, 4.903261; Waterlooplein metro station (Nieuwmarkt station 52.371944, 4.901111). Hook: in the 1960s the city folded atom shelters into the new east line: Nieuwmarkt station was built to hold 3,000 people behind steel doors, and a bunker for the mayor and council was added at Waterlooplein with a link to the city hall. Waterlooplein station also has a permanent display of finds from its digging. Lead: https://www.onh.nl/verhalen/bijna-vergeten-veertig-verborgen-bunkers-in-amsterdam ; second https://nl.wikipedia.org/wiki/Waterlooplein_(metrostation) . Status: stations open; shelters opened only on Open Monumentendag. Caveats: DC-30 is the Nieuwmarkt metro art; group or keep apart. Rank: Okay. Group with: DC-30.
title: Cold War shelters under the metro

heading: Sweep 4: hidden history / Nieuwmarkt/Lastage
text: **BC-28. Goslerhuisje, last house of the Joden Houttuinen.** Pin 52.369856, 4.901685; Jodenbreestraat 1. Hook: a low, slightly skewed lock-keeper's house, the only building left of the Joden Houttuinen, cleared in the late 1960s for the Maupoleum (itself demolished in the 1990s); named after A. Gosler and Sons, iron dealers and demolition contractors. A few doors on, the Jewish cinema Tip Top (Jodenbreestraat 25-27) was demolished in 1953; the theatre school on the site named its small hall Tip Top. Local voice: "Maupoleum", called one of the ugliest buildings in the city. Lead: https://nl.wikipedia.org/wiki/Goslerhuisje ; second https://nl.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tip_Top_Theater . Status: standing (rijksmonument 1973). Rank: Nice. New place.
title: Goslerhuisje, last house of the Joden Houttuinen

heading: Sweep 4: hidden history / Nieuwmarkt/Lastage
text: **BC-29. Schottenburch, the oldest warehouse.** Pin 52.371960, 4.902290; Kromboomssloot 18-20. Hook: a double warehouse with a 1636 stone, already on Pieter Bast's map of 1597; its plot runs askew to its neighbours, possibly from before the Lastage came inside the walls (c. 1585). From 1979 to 1988 an artists' initiative held shows and performances here. Local voice: "oudste nog bestaande pakhuis van Amsterdam". Lead: https://nl.wikipedia.org/wiki/Schottenburch . Status: standing. Caveats: the "oldest" title is contested (nl.wiki says "one of the oldest"). Rank: Nice. New place.
title: Schottenburch, the oldest warehouse

heading: Sweep 4: hidden history / Nieuwmarkt/Lastage
text: **BC-30. Saaihal, the Staalmeesters' hall.** Pin 52.368345, 4.897091; Staalstraat 7. Hook: built 1641 by Pieter de Keyser as part of the Staalhof, the cloth-control centre known from Rembrandt's "De Staalmeesters". Lead: https://nl.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saaihal_(Amsterdam) . Status: standing. Rank: Okay. New place.
title: Saaihal, the Staalmeesters' hall

heading: Sweep 4: hidden history / Nieuwmarkt/Lastage
text: **BC-31. Christ Church on Hendrick de Keyser's workshop.** Pin 52.368582, 4.897734; Groenburgwal 42. Hook: the English church stands on the site of Hendrick de Keyser's stonemason's yard. Lead: https://stadsherstel.nl/monumenten/groenburgwal-42-christchurch/ . Status: standing. Caveats: check what Stadsherstel shows of the yard. Rank: Okay. New place.
title: Christ Church on Hendrick de Keyser's workshop

heading: Sweep 4: hidden history / Nieuwmarkt/Lastage
text: **BC-32. Diamantslijperij Boas.** Pin 52.369587, 4.904066; Nieuwe Uilenburgerstraat 173-175. Hook: diamond-cutting factory of 1879 with a free-standing boiler house, a survivor of Uilenburg's Jewish diamond industry. Lead: https://nl.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diamantslijperij_Boas . Status: standing. Rank: Okay. New place.
title: Diamantslijperij Boas

heading: Sweep 5: behind the gate / Burgwallen-Nieuwe Zijde
text: **BC-33. Rasphuispoort and the swimming pool behind it.** Pin 52.367729, 4.891063; Heiligeweg, opposite the Voetboogstraat. Hook: Hendrick de Keyser's gate (c. 1603) to the Rasphuis, where young men rasped Brazil wood into dye powder; the relief shows a cart of logs drawn by lions, bears, boars and tigers, under a woman with a whip labelled "Castigatio". Behind it, invisible from the street, the Heiligewegbad (1896-1987), at its opening the biggest indoor pool in Europe and subject of one of the first Dutch films (1896); its steam bath was a discreet meeting place for gay men in the 1940s and 1950s. Now a side entrance of the Kalvertoren mall. Local voice: "Heiligebad". Lead: https://nl.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rasphuispoortje ; second https://nl.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heiligewegbad . Status: gate standing. Rank: **Amazing**. New place.
title: Rasphuispoort and the swimming pool behind it

heading: Sweep 5: behind the gate / Burgwallen-Nieuwe Zijde
text: **BC-34. Makelaers Comptoir.** Pin 52.375346, 4.892667; Nieuwezijds Voorburgwal 75. Hook: the brokers' guild house of 1633 on a triangular plot, with the best-preserved 17th-century front hall in the city; Vereniging Hendrick de Keyser lets it for small events, the only way in. Lead: https://nl.wikipedia.org/wiki/Makelaers_Comptoir ; second: the Hendrick de Keyser house page (read, URL not kept). Status: standing. Rank: Okay. New place.
title: Makelaers Comptoir

heading: Sweep 5: behind the gate / Burgwallen-Nieuwe Zijde
text: **BC-35. Oude Braak and Nieuwezijds Armsteeg: the dike-arm lanes.** Pin 52.376800, 4.895400; Oude Braak. Hook: the Oude Braak, once "De Break" after a dike breach, was a web of alleys between Nieuwezijds Voorburgwal and Nieuwendijk; only part of it is public now, the rest is for residents, with old warehouses. The curving Nieuwezijds Armsteeg next to it began as a dike arm; digging in 1984 found the 2 m clay wall of 1342 with its palisade. Local voice: part was called "Kromme Elleboogsteeg" until the council dropped the name. Lead: https://nl.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oude_Braak ; second https://nl.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nieuwezijds_Armsteeg . Status: partly closed. Rank: Okay. New place.
title: Oude Braak and Nieuwezijds Armsteeg: the dike-arm lanes

heading: Sweep 5: behind the gate / Burgwallen-Oude Zijde
text: **BC-36. Het Veilinghuisje: the house everyone thought was demolished.** Pin 52.375410, 4.899230; Oudezijds Voorburgwal 28 (on the inner court). Hook: a small auction house of a known bookselling family (Bom, from 1882) on an inner court boxed in by Warmoesstraat, Oudezijds Armsteeg, Oudezijds Voorburgwal and Heintje Hoekssteeg, invisible from the street. It was due to be demolished in 1989 and everyone thought it had been, so the city left it off its monument survey; Stadsherstel found it standing, had it listed and restored it. The court also held one of the first sugar bakeries (dug up), and next door at no. 30 the Anthony Theater's floor collapsed in 1991. Local voice: Stadsherstel, "werd in 1989 gesloopt. Althans dat was de bedoeling en iedereen dacht ook dat dat gebeurd was." Lead: https://stadsherstel.nl/monumenten/oudezijds-voorburgwal-28/ ; second https://stadsherstel.nl/monumenten/oudezijds-voorburgwal-28-brouwerij-de-prael/ . Status: standing; glimpses from the De Prael brewery premises (brewery status not verified 2026-11-24). Rank: **Amazing**. New place.
title: Het Veilinghuisje: the house everyone thought was demolished

heading: Sweep 5: behind the gate / Burgwallen-Oude Zijde
text: **BC-37. Gebed zonder end.** Pin 52.369761, 4.893771; alley from the Kuiperssteeg to the Grimburgwal, entered under a gate. Hook: the name, "Prayer without end", probably recalls the convents of the "Stille Zijde"; the alley runs over the grounds of the Sint Claraconvent (c. 1397). The name is painted on the wall because the sign kept being stolen. Local voice: "Gebed zonder end". Lead: https://nl.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gebed_zonder_end . Status: open, pedestrian. Rank: Nice. New place.
title: Gebed zonder end

heading: Sweep 5: behind the gate / Nieuwmarkt/Lastage
text: **BC-38. Uilenburger Synagoge, reached only by alleys.** Pin 52.370212, 4.905264; Nieuwe Uilenburgerstraat 91. Hook: an Ashkenazi synagogue of 1766 built behind the street houses, closer to the water than the road, for centuries reachable only through passages; it survived the slum clearances and was looted in the war. The screened yard was later the city's monument yard, which left a bridge stone, a city arms tableau from the Oude Haarlemmersluis (set 1957) and a stone for the restoration workshop (closed 1974). Lead: https://nl.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uilenburger_Synagoge . Status: used by Beit Ha'Chidush and for concerts. Caveats: check public access. Rank: Nice. New place.
title: Uilenburger Synagoge, reached only by alleys

heading: Sweep 5: behind the gate / Nieuwmarkt/Lastage
text: **BC-39. Oudezijds Huiszittenhuis: the poor-relief courtyard.** Pin 52.368849, 4.901637; Waterlooplein 69 (gate on the Nieuwe Amstelstraat). Hook: built 1655 (Willem de Keyser) to hand out bread and peat to the poor; behind it a courtyard with arcaded galleries, and a regents' room with a painted ceiling and a Van der Helst; the Academie van Bouwkunst has used it since 1946. Lead: https://nl.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oudezijds_Huiszittenhuis . Status: school; courtyard access not verified. Rank: Nice. New place.
title: Oudezijds Huiszittenhuis: the poor-relief courtyard

heading: Sweep 5: behind the gate / Nieuwmarkt/Lastage
text: **BC-40. A.S. Onderwijzerhof, a hofje from the 1980s.** Pin 52.367095, 4.903389. Hook: a small square-cum-hofje made during the 1980s renewal of this part of the Jewish quarter. Lead: https://nl.wikipedia.org/wiki/A.S._Onderwijzerhof . Status: open. Rank: Okay. New place.
title: A.S. Onderwijzerhof, a hofje from the 1980s

heading: Sweep 4: hidden history / Grachtengordel-Zuid
text: **BE-01 Poentunnel: the bankers' tunnel under the Keizersgracht.** Pin 52.363869, 4.892125 (the tunnel line under the Keizersgracht between De Bazel and the Vijzelbank), Vijzelstraat 32 / Keizersgracht. The only tunnel under an Amsterdam canal: 50 m long, 3.5 m wide, dug in 1974-75 together with a new main sewer so the ABN directors could walk dry from one building to the other. It was never meant for money, but the nickname "Poentunnel" (poen: dough, rhyming on the Coentunnel) stuck. After 1999 the north side was bricked up; on Open Monumentendag 2024 it opened for two days and people queued more than three and a half hours, and the city told visitors to stop coming. Local voice: the "Keizerssnede", the cut through the Keizersgracht. Lead https://nl.wikipedia.org/wiki/Poentunnel ; second https://www.nhnieuws.nl/nieuws/340608/extreme-belangstelling-bezoekers-wachten-ruim-35-uur-voor-amsterdamse-poentunnel and https://onh.nl/verhaal/de-amsterdamse-poentunnel-ging-voor-heel-even-open . Status: closed, opened only on special days (latest: Open Monumentendag 14-15 Sept 2024). Caveats: nothing to see from the street; the pin is the tunnel line, not an entrance. Rank: **Amazing**. New place.
title: Poentunnel: the bankers' tunnel under the Keizersgracht

heading: Sweep 4: hidden history / Grachtengordel-Zuid
text: **BE-02 The Vijzelbank and its gate over the Kerkstraat.** Pin 52.363039, 4.891865, Vijzelstraat 66 (where the building bridges the Kerkstraat). On 23 March 1955 the Vijzelflat that Van der Mey had built over the Kerkstraat (1926-28) collapsed; Duintjer's bank of 1969-73 that replaced it set off "a storm of unprecedented ferocity" in the council, which broke party discipline and changed how the city thought about its centre. It still spans the Kerkstraat like a gate. Local voice: VVAB Binnenstad chose its "dull" facade as a cover to tell that story. Lead https://nl.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kerkstraat_(Amsterdam) ; second Binnenstad 178, "De Vijzelbank" (Geurt Brinkgreve), https://web.archive.org/web/2021/https://amsterdamsebinnenstad.nl/binnenstad/178/vijzelbank.php . Status: standing (wiki, read Nov 2026); current use not checked. Caveats: the building is plain; the story is the point. Rank: Okay. Group with BE-01.
title: The Vijzelbank and its gate over the Kerkstraat

heading: Sweep 4: hidden history / Grachtengordel-Zuid
text: **BE-03 Amstelkerk: the "temporary" church that stayed.** Pin 52.362321, 4.896482, Amstelveld 10. Built in wood in 1668-70 by Stalpaert as a stopgap, placed off-centre so a stone church could rise beside it; the stone church never came, and that empty half became the Amstelveld. Because it was temporary there were no burials. In 1982 the bell fell askew during a service; in 1986 Stadsherstel bought the church for one guilder. Van Gogh sat here in 1877-78 listening to his uncle Stricker. Lead https://nl.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amstelkerk ; second https://stadsherstel.nl/monumenten/de-amstelkerk/ and theobakker.net amstelkerk.pdf. Status: in use, services again since 2006 (wiki, read Nov 2026). Caveats: listed; DE-41 covers the Amstelveld square. Rank: Nice. Group with DE-41.
title: Amstelkerk: the "temporary" church that stayed

heading: Sweep 4: hidden history / Grachtengordel-Zuid
text: **BE-04 Het Vrededuifje to De Duif: a clandestine church that was squatted by its own parish.** Pin 52.361450, 4.896697, Prinsengracht 756 (Kerkstraat 169 was the hidden church). The Catholic congregation first met in the clandestine "Het Vrededuifje" in the Kerkstraat; in 1796 it moved to the Prinsengracht, and the present church by Molkenboer followed in 1857. When the bishop closed it in 1974 the parishioners occupied their own church and kept it open as an ecumenical community. Lead https://nl.wikipedia.org/wiki/De_Duif_(Amsterdam) ; second https://nl.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kerkstraat_(Amsterdam) . Status: in use (Stadsherstel restoration 2006). Caveats: locate puts the Prinsengracht church in De Weteringschans (outer side of the canal); listed. Rank: Nice. New place.
title: Het Vrededuifje to De Duif: a clandestine church that was squatted by its own parish

heading: Sweep 4: hidden history / Grachtengordel-Zuid
text: **BE-05 Reguliersgracht: the canal that started Amsterdam's conservation movement.** Pin 52.364456, 4.895592, Reguliersgracht 6. In 1900-01 the city wanted to fill it for an electric tram; the brochure "Stedenschennis" (talks by D.C. Meijer and Jan Veth, 1901) and the young Amstelodamum society saved it, the start of systematic care for the cityscape. Even earlier, in 1866, the Chamber of Commerce had drawn a railway line from a station south of town straight over this canal. Number 6 also keeps rare "linksdekkende" (left-lapping) roof tiles. Local voice: Meijer mocked the hurry for electric trams: would it be such a disaster to keep the horses on the Utrechtsestraat line? Lead Binnenstad 202 "De Reguliersgracht: boter, kaas en eieren", https://web.archive.org/web/2021/https://amsterdamsebinnenstad.nl/binnenstad/202/reguliersgracht.html ; second https://nl.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reguliersgracht . Status: canal open; checked Nov 2026. Caveats: the canal itself is well known (the seven bridges view); the hook is the near-filling. Rank: Nice. New place.
title: Reguliersgracht: the canal that started Amsterdam's conservation movement

heading: Sweep 4: hidden history / Grachtengordel-Zuid
text: **BE-06 Huis met de Kolommen: the mayor's house given on one condition.** Pin 52.364861, 4.893444, Herengracht 502. Built 1672 for a West India Company director; in 1927 banker Van Aalst gave it to the city on condition that it become the mayor's official residence. The wartime NSB mayor Voûte lived here; Samkalden made the top floor a private flat; the first reception was 2 Sept 1927. The money and portraits of the last Bors van Waveren daughter went to the Deutzenhofje (BE-27). Lead https://nl.wikipedia.org/wiki/Huis_met_de_Kolommen ; second slice gg-zuid-1 (Ambtswoning van de burgemeester). Status: in use as official residence (wiki, Nov 2026). Caveats: closed; seen from the street only; on the monument slice. Rank: Okay. New place.
title: Huis met de Kolommen: the mayor's house given on one condition

heading: Sweep 4: hidden history / Grachtengordel-Zuid
text: **BE-07 Herengracht 524: Jurriaan Andriessen's painted landscape room.** Pin 52.364634, 4.895091, Herengracht 524. One of two identical merchants' houses of 1697-98 in the Golden Bend; behind the neck gable hides a room painted in 1771 by Jurriaan Andriessen, the leading Dutch wall painter of his day, with a wide landscape of trees, water and figures. Its coach house stood on the Keizersgracht behind. Lead https://www.hendrickdekeyser.nl/de-huizen/herengracht-524 . Status: owned by Hendrick de Keyser since 1995, let; no regular opening found (Nov 2026). Caveats: private; mention only if a visiting day exists. Rank: Okay. New place.
title: Herengracht 524: Jurriaan Andriessen's painted landscape room

heading: Sweep 4: hidden history / De Weteringschans
text: **BE-08 Max Euweplein: the prison where Anne Frank was held.** Pin 52.362283, 4.883161, Max Euweplein. The square stands on the site of the Huis van Bewaring (1850, on bastion De Schinkel); after the arrest of 4 August 1944 Anne Frank and the others were held here before Westerbork. During the war "any day could be your last" there. The prison closed in 1979; the 1991 square kept a round shape against the city's wish for a rectangle, and the colonnade carries "Homo sapiens non urinat in ventum". Memorial stone 1992, "Tranen voor het verzet" (1993). Lead https://nl.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Euweplein ; second https://www.nhnieuws.nl/nieuws/348203/in-het-amsterdamse-huis-van-bewaring-kon-tijdens-de-oorlog-iedere-dag-de-laatste-zijn (4 May 2025) and https://research.annefrank.org/en/locaties/51209a6b-cf00-4fe8-8533-828555d56401/ . Status: public square (2025). Caveats: the chess board and casino are what people know; the prison is the hidden layer. Rank: Nice. New place.
title: Max Euweplein: the prison where Anne Frank was held

heading: Sweep 4: hidden history / De Weteringschans
text: **BE-09 Walenweeshuis: Dortsman's orphanage waiting behind closed doors.** Pin 52.362063, 4.890745, Vijzelgracht 2A. The Walloon orphanage of 1669-71 by Adriaan Dortsman, with wings of 1679, 1683 and 1728 and a school of 1866 in the courtyard; from 1971 to 2016 the French consulate and Maison Descartes, empty since. In 2025 new owners announced a restoration and new use. Lead https://nl.wikipedia.org/wiki/Walenweeshuis ; second https://www.rodi.nl/amsterdam-nieuw-west/nieuws/436615/walenweeshuis-aan-vijzelgracht-krijgt-nieuwe-bestemming (16 Mar 2025) and https://www.nhnieuws.nl/nieuws/341809/zorgen-om-walenweeshuis-vijzelgracht-amsterdam . Status: empty, restoration planned (March 2025). Outlook: major change ahead. Caveats: listed; courtyard not accessible now. Rank: Nice. New place.
title: Walenweeshuis: Dortsman's orphanage waiting behind closed doors

heading: Sweep 4: hidden history / De Weteringschans
text: **BE-10 Noortsche Bos: Vingboons' weavers' houses.** Pin 52.361762, 4.887327, Spiegelgracht 27 (corner Tweede Weteringdwarsstraat). In 1670-71 Philips Vingboons, architect of grand canal houses, also designed 211 weavers' homes in the Weteringbuurt, an early piece of social housing; many still stand. The corner house is the first monument you meet coming from the Rijksmuseum. The neighbourhood was weavers' and dyers' country: Prinsengracht 997-999 began as two dye works (1671). Local voice: VVAB counted on the corner house "13 awnings, 7 flags and a man-sized cook" in 2002. Lead Binnenstad 193, https://web.archive.org/web/2021/https://amsterdamsebinnenstad.nl/binnenstad/193/spiegelgr27.php ; second https://www.hendrickdekeyser.nl/de-huizen/prinsengracht-997 . Status: standing; signage not re-checked (2002 evidence). Caveats: hook is the ensemble, the corner house is only the entry point. Rank: Okay. New place.
title: Noortsche Bos: Vingboons' weavers' houses

heading: Sweep 4: hidden history / De Weteringschans
text: **BE-11 Frederiksplein 10: an admiralty captain's house that lost its canal.** Pin 52.360982, 4.898787, Frederiksplein 10. Rebuilt around 1730, probably for admiralty captain Adam van Ingen: his arms crown the sandstone facade, with Neptune and Mercury, ship's cannon and navigation instruments. It stood on the Achtergracht, filled in 1870 to make the Frederiksplein. Hendrick de Keyser was offered it in 1918 but only bought it in 1975 because of the price. Lead https://www.hendrickdekeyser.nl/de-huizen/frederiksplein-10 . Status: HdK house (Nov 2026). Caveats: interior private. Rank: Okay. Look-for type; group with DE-44 (same square).
title: Frederiksplein 10: an admiralty captain's house that lost its canal
rank_text: Rank: Okay. Look-for type; group with DE-44 (same square).

heading: Sweep 4: hidden history / De Weteringschans
text: **BE-12 Paleis voor Volksvlijt: the glass palace under the Nederlandsche Bank.** Pin 52.360600, 4.899300 (approximate, axis of the Sarphatistraat on the Frederiksplein). Amsterdam's Crystal Palace (Outshoorn, 1859-64) burnt on the night of 17-18 April 1929; the surviving gallery wings stood until 1961, demolished for the Nederlandsche Bank. Rudy Kousbroek called that "the most extreme act of vandalism in Amsterdam after the war"; Wim T. Schippers proposed knocking down the bank and rebuilding the palace. Lead https://nl.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paleis_voor_Volksvlijt ; second Binnenstad 194 (Geurt Brinkgreve), https://web.archive.org/web/2021/https://amsterdamsebinnenstad.nl/binnenstad/194/volksvlijt.php . Status: gone. Caveats: gone thing, high bar; pin approximate. Rank: Okay. Group with DE-44.
title: Paleis voor Volksvlijt: the glass palace under the Nederlandsche Bank

heading: Sweep 4: hidden history / De Weteringschans
text: **BE-13 Amstelsluizen: Hudde's sluices that flush the canals.** Pin 52.362231, 4.903047, Amstel by the Sarphatistraat. Built 1673 under Johannes Hudde, the sluices are still closed to let fresh water push through the canals; a sluice keeper's house and two small customs houses stand on them. In 1675-87 a horse-driven mill by the city timber yard pumped water, with an underground conduit under the Weesperplein. Lead https://nl.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amstelsluizen ; second theobakker.net raadsels.pdf. Status: in use (wiki, Nov 2026). Caveats: listed (rijksmonument 518510). Rank: Okay. Group with Hogesluis (drafted).
title: Amstelsluizen: Hudde's sluices that flush the canals

heading: Sweep 4: hidden history / Weesperbuurt/Plantage
text: **BE-14 Weesperplein station: the Cold War shelter for 12,000.** Pin 52.361111, 4.907778, Weesperplein metro station. Built 1979 as a public nuclear shelter (Project 102), the largest in Amsterdam: the ceiling panels fold down to be tables, sliding steel doors and a decontamination sluice are still visible before the gates at the Rhijnspoorplein/Sarphatistraat entrance, and the tunnel gates double as flood barriers, still tested. Under the station lies an unused tunnel stub for an east-west line that never came. Maintenance stopped in 1999. Lead https://arcam.nl/wp-content/uploads/2022/10/Fietsroute-langs-de-Openbare-Schuilplaatsen-van-Amsterdam-1.2.pdf ; second https://nl.wikipedia.org/wiki/Weesperplein_(metrostation) and https://onh.nl/verhaal/bijna-vergeten-veertig-verborgen-bunkers-in-amsterdam . Status: station in use (2022-26). Caveats: sources disagree on capacity (12,000 Arcam and wiki, 3,000 ONH); the shelter rooms are closed. Rank: **Amazing**. New place.
title: Weesperplein station: the Cold War shelter for 12,000

heading: Sweep 4: hidden history / Weesperbuurt/Plantage
text: **BE-15 Hortusbrug shelter: room for 100 under a bridge.** Pin 52.364167, 4.908333 (approximate, Hortusbrug, Nieuwe Herengracht / Plantage Middenlaan). The 1960 bridge by Sterenberg hides a public shelter (Project 11, 1962) for 100 people; the stairs down are on both banks. Lead https://arcam.nl/wp-content/uploads/2022/10/Fietsroute-langs-de-Openbare-Schuilplaatsen-van-Amsterdam-1.2.pdf ; second https://nl.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hortusbrug . Status: closed shelter (2022). Caveats: pin approximate; the stair hatches are the only thing to see. Rank: Nice. Group with BE-14.
title: Hortusbrug shelter: room for 100 under a bridge

heading: Sweep 4: hidden history / Weesperbuurt/Plantage
text: **BE-16 Diamantbeurs: the exchange that never lost a stone.** Pin 52.361933, 4.906969, Weesperplein 4. Built 1911 (Van Arkel) for the Beursvereniging voor den Diamanthandel, which left the Casino on the Waterlooplein (where a rival club was nicknamed the "kinnesinnebeursie"); housed Belgian refugees in WWI; burnt on 12 Feb 1956 without a single diamond lost thanks to the vaults; its first woman member was admitted in 1952. Lead https://nl.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diamantbeurs_(Amsterdam) ; second theobakker.net casino.pdf. Status: now Capital C (creative hub; wiki). Caveats: listed. Rank: Nice. New place.
title: Diamantbeurs: the exchange that never lost a stone

heading: Sweep 4: hidden history / Weesperbuurt/Plantage
text: **BE-17 Muiderpoort: the gate that sank.** Pin 52.363726, 4.919355, Sarphatistraat 500 / Alexanderplein. The only surviving gate of the 17th and 18th-century walls is the second one: on the night of 29-30 January 1769 the first gate slid off its foundation. Rauws' replacement went up in 1770; on 9 October 1811 Napoleon rode through it in a coach drawn by eight white horses. Lead https://nl.wikipedia.org/wiki/Muiderpoort_(Amsterdam) ; second theobakker.net poorten.pdf. Status: standing (office use). Caveats: listed, well visible; the hook is the sinking. Rank: Nice. New place.
title: Muiderpoort: the gate that sank

heading: Sweep 4: hidden history / Weesperbuurt/Plantage
text: **BE-18 Nieuwe Kerkstraat hidden synagogues and hofjes.** Pin 52.363781, 4.903895, Nieuwe Kerkstraat 16. The Fernandes Nuneshuis at no. 16 was a hofje for poor Portuguese-Jewish women; further east, no. 149 housed the "Russensjoel", the prayer house of Russian Jews; the street also keeps the 1782 wall remnant of the Sarphatihuis workhouse. Lead https://nl.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nieuwe_Kerkstraat_(Amsterdam) ; second theobakker.net synagogen.pdf. Status: buildings standing (wiki read Nov 2026). Caveats: the street article is thin and the Russensjoel and Fernandes Nunes pages do not exist; needs a gable check before drafting. Rank: Okay. New place.
title: Nieuwe Kerkstraat hidden synagogues and hofjes

heading: Sweep 4: hidden history / Weesperbuurt/Plantage
text: **BE-19 Joodsche Invalide: the home that became the health service.** Pin 52.362525, 4.909003, Nieuwe Achtergracht 100. Built 1925 for the Jewish home for invalids, now the GGD headquarters. Lead theobakker.net weesperstraat.pdf ; second slice plantage-2 (De Joodsche Invalide). Status: GGD offices. Caveats: thin from my sources; theme A scout may hold the war story. Rank: Okay. New place.
title: Joodsche Invalide: the home that became the health service

heading: Sweep 4: hidden history / Weesperbuurt/Plantage
text: **BE-20 Plantage Muidergracht 1-23: a row restored by its own residents.** Pin 52.366149, 4.909390, Plantage Muidergracht 19. After the war the row was shabby and threatened by university plans to clear the Plantage, Hortus included. Eleven owners restored their houses one by one from 1993; the last square metres of no. 19 were painted on Easter Monday 2003. Local voice: Ine Vermaas, "stadsherstel in eigen beheer", with neighbours pushing each other over shared party walls. Lead Binnenstad 201, https://web.archive.org/web/2021/https://amsterdamsebinnenstad.nl/binnenstad/201/plantage.html . Status: standing (2003 evidence). Caveats: ordinary to look at. Rank: Okay. New place.
title: Plantage Muidergracht 1-23: a row restored by its own residents

heading: Sweep 4: hidden history / Oostelijke Eilanden/Kadijken
text: **BE-21 Oranje-Nassau Kazerne: Napoleon's barracks, saved by the neighbours.** Pin 52.364749, 4.921370, Sarphatistraat 600. Built 1810-13 as Napoleon's Quartier Saint-Charles, 278 m long, paid for by a 5% levy on rents or by having soldiers billeted; his arms were later swapped for Orange. In 1839-40 Artis kept its elephants and tigers here; from 1892 the army's carrier pigeons. Slated for demolition after 1987, it was saved by residents' protest and became 150 social homes (1990). Lead https://nl.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oranje-Nassau_Kazerne ; second slice eilanden-1. Status: housing (wiki, Nov 2026). Caveats: listed; courtyard private. Rank: Nice. New place.
title: Oranje-Nassau Kazerne: Napoleon's barracks, saved by the neighbours

heading: Sweep 4: hidden history / Oostelijke Eilanden/Kadijken
text: **BE-22 Marineterrein commandant's house with its Cold War bunker.** Pin 52.372419, 4.915313, Marineterrein, Kattenburgerstraat 5-7. Under the commandant's house is a communications bunker from the Cold War; in 2025 the house and three other navy buildings became municipal monuments, and a second protected shelter under building 029 is in procedure. The 17th-century gatehouse (Stalpaert) at Kattenburgerstraat 7 is the way in. Lead https://nl.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marineterrein_(Amsterdam) ; second slice eilanden-1 (Gebouw 001, Beschermd Onderkomen Kazerne V.B.S.). Status: listed 2025; bunker not open. Caveats: navy site partly public; bunker access unknown. Rank: Nice. Group with DE-08 (the wall).
title: Marineterrein commandant's house with its Cold War bunker
rank_text: Rank: Nice. Group with DE-08 (the wall).

heading: Sweep 4: hidden history / Oostelijke Eilanden/Kadijken
text: **BE-23 Kattenburg's fake old facades.** Pin 52.370900, 4.917200, Kattenburgerplein. The whole island was demolished in 1962-68; the gabled row on the Kattenburgerplein is a reconstruction by Theo Rouwhorst of the city's monuments office, inspired by what had stood there, criticised by historians as a falsification. The Kattenburgers were Orangists: on 29 May 1787 they raised the double drawbridge and plundered patriots' houses ("the battle of the Kattenburgerbrug"). Lead https://nl.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kattenburg ; second theobakker.net kattenburg.pdf. Status: standing. Caveats: pin approximate (the row); Scheepvaartmuseum next door is A-list, this is not. Rank: Nice. New place.
title: Kattenburg's fake old facades

heading: Sweep 4: hidden history / Oostelijke Eilanden/Kadijken
text: **BE-24 Marie Altelaar and the rent strike of Kattenburg.** Pin 52.372346, 4.919470 (approximate, Kattenburgerkruisstraat). When the new homes turned out dearer than promised, residents led by Marie Altelaar held back part of the rent every month for more than fifteen years; a court ruled for them on 19 Sept 1986. A square on Wittenburg carries her name. Lead https://nl.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kattenburg ; second https://nl.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wittenburg_(Amsterdam) . Status: history; the Marie Altelaarplein exists. Caveats: pin approximate; a gate arch on the Kattenburgerkruisstraat is mentioned but not confirmed. Rank: Okay. Group with BE-23.
title: Marie Altelaar and the rent strike of Kattenburg

heading: Sweep 4: hidden history / Oostelijke Eilanden/Kadijken
text: **BE-25 The VOC and Admiralty ropewalks.** Pin 52.368043, 4.924566, Oostenburgergracht 77 (ropewalk front buildings, nos. 75-81). In 1661 the VOC opened a 500 m ropewalk and a vast sawmill on fresh Oostenburg, the start of what became the largest industrial firm in the world. The front building of the VOC ropewalk (1660s) and the Admiraliteitslijnbaan are among the last 17th-century buildings on the island; Tsar Peter the Great trained four months at the VOC yard here in 1697. Lead https://nl.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oostenburg_(Amsterdam) ; second https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Admiraliteitslijnbaan,_Amsterdam . Status: standing (wiki 2026). Caveats: house numbers differ between sources (75-77 VOC, 79-81 Admiralty); DE-18 covers the Touwbaanpark and 400-year fence, nearby. Rank: Nice. Group with DE-18.
title: The VOC and Admiralty ropewalks

heading: Sweep 4: hidden history / Oostelijke Eilanden/Kadijken
text: **BE-26 Kadijksplein: dockers' coffee house and sailors' home.** Pin 52.370033, 4.911917, Kadijksplein 4. The Koffiehuis van den Volksbond (no. 4) sits at an angle facing the gate of the former Entrepotdok (no. 1); the Zeemanshuis for sailors is at nos. 17-18. Lead slice eilanden-1 (Koffiehuis van den Volksbond, Zeemanshuis, both municipal monuments 2004) ; second https://nl.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kadijksplein . Status: buildings standing; Zeemanshuis used by YWAM (2026). Caveats: the coffee house is no longer one. Rank: Okay. New place.
title: Kadijksplein: dockers' coffee house and sailors' home

heading: Sweep 5: behind the gate / Grachtengordel-Zuid
text: **BE-27 Deutzenhofje: a mother's will in brick.** Pin 52.362653, 4.889931, Prinsengracht 855-899. Agneta Deutz (d. 1692) left her only son Jan Meerman just the legal third and gave the rest to a hofje for poor women, built 1694-95; the regents' room still has her portraits and silver, and the gable stone carries a verse. Van Eeghen called her last fifteen years a tragedy. Extended in 1964 with houses on the Kerkstraat; older women still live here. Lead theobakker.net deutzenhofje.pdf (I.H. van Eeghen, Amstelodamum 1960) ; second https://nl.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deutzenhofje . Status: inhabited, normally closed; sometimes open on Open Tuinen Dagen. Caveats: listed; private courtyard, respect residents. Rank: **Amazing**. New place.
title: Deutzenhofje: a mother's will in brick

heading: Sweep 5: behind the gate / Grachtengordel-Zuid
text: **BE-28 Collectie Six: Rembrandt's friend still at home.** Pin 52.365053, 4.900680, Amstel 218. The Six family has lived here since 1915 with Rembrandt's portrait of Jan Six; since 1957 the state helps on condition of limited access by introduction, so visits are by request. Guestbook since 1809 (25 volumes); the collection includes a planetarium of 1754. Lead https://www.collectiesix.nl/bezoek ; second https://nl.wikipedia.org/wiki/Collectie_Six . Status: visits by request (site live, Nov 2026). Caveats: private home; no walk-in. Rank: **Amazing**. New place.
title: Collectie Six: Rembrandt's friend still at home

heading: Sweep 5: behind the gate / Grachtengordel-Zuid
text: **BE-29 Coach house of Keizersgracht 524 on the Kerkstraat.** Pin 52.365064, 4.886189, Kerkstraat 61. The Kerkstraat was the canal belt's service lane, lined with coach houses (about 45 were counted); this one, painted by Hendrik Keun in 1772 (Rijksmuseum), has Hercules and a goddess in its niches and a garden house with Hope, Faith and Charity. Lead Binnenstad 187 "Open Tuinen" (Juliet Oldenburger), https://web.archive.org/web/2021/https://amsterdamsebinnenstad.nl/binnenstad/187/opentuinen.php ; second https://nl.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kerkstraat_(Amsterdam) . Status: private garden, opened on Open Tuinen Dagen (2001 evidence). Caveats: needs a current opening check. Rank: Nice. New place.
title: Coach house of Keizersgracht 524 on the Kerkstraat

heading: Sweep 5: behind the gate / Grachtengordel-Zuid
text: **BE-30 Museum Van Loon's coach house and its fake windows.** Pin 52.362865, 4.893158, Kerkstraat 259 (garden side of Keizersgracht 672). The garden front of the coach house (1775) carries Apollo, Flora and Silenus, but its first-floor windows are fake: the family did not want servants looking into the garden. The car replaced the horses in 1920; the museum bought it in 2009 and reopened it as a coach house in 2011. Lead https://nl.wikipedia.org/wiki/Museum_Van_Loon ; second slice gg-zuid-2 (Koetshuis Museum Van Loon). Status: open with the museum (2026). Caveats: inside a paid museum; the Kerkstraat side is visible free. Rank: Nice. New place.
title: Museum Van Loon's coach house and its fake windows

heading: Sweep 5: behind the gate / Grachtengordel-Zuid
text: **BE-31 Kerkstraat craftsmen's houses: 1673 shop with a date ribbon.** Pin 52.362389, 4.895527, Kerkstraat 324. Built as a "winkelhuis" for maltster Gillis Moyaert, with a date ribbon reading 1673 in the facade; split from the start into rented upper and lower homes. Nos. 288-292 were built together around 1691 by master carpenter Adriaen Sessincks, 288 with its 17th-century layout intact. Lead https://www.hendrickdekeyser.nl/de-huizen/kerkstraat-324 ; second https://www.hendrickdekeyser.nl/de-huizen/kerkstraat-288 . Status: HdK rental houses (Nov 2026). Caveats: private; seen from the street. Rank: Okay. Look-for type.
title: Kerkstraat craftsmen's houses: 1673 shop with a date ribbon

heading: Sweep 5: behind the gate / Grachtengordel-Zuid
text: **BE-32 Herengracht 412: perhaps the oldest garden house in Amsterdam.** Pin 52.367060, 4.887194, Herengracht 412. Philips Vingboons published the plan of this 1667 house with its garden, and it is the only garden house plan of his known: a room, a chicken coop ("Hoenderhock") and a wash house. In 1734 Paulus Loot van Schooten crowned it with a sandstone dome-like top and his alliance arms, but brickwork and layout suggest the core is still 17th-century. The garden is now a lawn. Local voice: Juliet Oldenburger imagined the prosaic chicken coop turned into a "speelhuys". Lead Binnenstad 186 "Het oudste tuinhuis van Amsterdam?", https://web.archive.org/web/2021/https://amsterdamsebinnenstad.nl/binnenstad/186/tuinhuis.php . Status: garden house standing (article undated, around 2000); access only on Open Tuinen Dagen if at all, not checked. Caveats: private; the dating is the author's hypothesis. Rank: Nice. New place.
title: Herengracht 412: perhaps the oldest garden house in Amsterdam

heading: Sweep 5: behind the gate / De Weteringschans
text: **BE-33 Commiezenhuisje: the toll house that became a pumping station.** Pin 52.360282, 4.888122, Weteringschans 30 (by the Weteringpoortbrug). A small toll collectors' house of 1848 at the old Weteringpoort; today it serves as a pumping station. Lead https://nl.wikipedia.org/wiki/Weteringschans ; second slice wetering-3 (Commiezenhuisje). Status: standing (wiki 2026). Caveats: tiny; one-fact item. Rank: Okay. Look-for type.
title: Commiezenhuisje: the toll house that became a pumping station

heading: Sweep 5: behind the gate / De Weteringschans
text: **BE-34 Lange Leidsedwarsstraat 144: next door to the inn "Het Land der Belofte".** Pin 52.363353, 4.885401, Lange Leidsedwarsstraat 144. Part of a row of six intact 18th-century houses (144-146 around 1725, the rest 1770) in a quarter laid out for working people. Next to no. 144 Gijsbert van Dorpen ran the inn "Het Land der Belofte" (the Promised Land) with a kolf course; his daughter and her husband took it over in 1734 and lived in no. 144. Lead https://www.hendrickdekeyser.nl/de-huizen/lange-leidsedwarsstraat-144 . Status: HdK rental house (Nov 2026). Caveats: the inn is gone; private. Rank: Okay. New place.
title: Lange Leidsedwarsstraat 144: next door to the inn "Het Land der Belofte"

heading: Sweep 5: behind the gate / Oostelijke Eilanden/Kadijken
text: **BE-35 Marineterrein gatehouse.** Pin 52.371839, 4.916391, Kattenburgerstraat 7. Stalpaert's 17th-century gatehouse of the Admiralty yard, listed since 1970. Lead https://nl.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marineterrein_(Amsterdam) . Status: open gate (2026). Caveats: thin alone. Rank: Okay. Group with BE-22 and DE-08.
title: Marineterrein gatehouse
rank_text: Rank: Okay. Group with BE-22 and DE-08.

heading: Jordaan
text: **BW-01 Karthuizerhof: 104 widows' homes on a Carthusian monastery.** Pin 52.378526, 4.881514 (pin approximate, middle of the court), Karthuizersstraat 89 to 171. Built 1650 by city architect Daniël Stalpaert for the Huiszittenmeesters as the Huiszittenweduwenhof, 104 homes (76 for the Nieuwezijds, 28 for the Oudezijds), on the ground of the Carthusian monastery Sint Andries ter Zaliger Haven (1394, wrecked by the geuzen in 1566), whose prior Willebord is a character in Vondel's Gijsbrecht; the monastery court was a plague graveyard from 1602. Inside: two 17th-century pumps (fish-head and mascaron spouts), a cog ship over the gate on the inside and the city arms on the outside, the names of the first regents over the entrance. The elderly left in 1973, it was squatted the same year with the city's consent, renovated 1986 to 65 homes; Ymere owns it. Local voice: the street is the "Droogstokkenstraatje" after the white drying racks (JW). Lead: Jordaanweb hofjes page; second: nl.wikipedia "Huiszittenweduwenhof" and Theo Bakker jordaan.pdf. Status: open daily 10:00 to 20:00, no groups (AOS, read 2026-11-24). Caveats: residents' court, keep quiet; listed; the graveyard part is DW-25 (Noorderspeeltuin). Rank: **Amazing**. Merge with monument 2194 (jordaan-2); group with DW-25.
title: Karthuizerhof: 104 widows' homes on a Carthusian monastery
rank_text: Rank: **Amazing**. Merge with monument 2194 (jordaan-2); group with DW-25.

heading: Jordaan
text: **BW-02 Raepenhofje and Bossche Hofje: one court, two hofjes, a hedge between.** Pin 52.382400, 4.883687, Palmgracht 28 to 38 (Raepenhofje) and 20 to 26 (Bossche Hofje, 52.382302, 4.883909). Both plots were bought on the same day in 1648 and today only a low hedge divides them (TB). The Raepenhofje has a turnip ("raap") keystone with "P.A." (Pieter Adriaensz. Raep), a Vondel verse and the text "Salig syn de vreedsamen"; female students live there now. The Bossche Hofje (1648) housed eight elderly Mennonite women. Lead: Theo Bakker driehoekstraat.pdf; second: Jordaanweb hofjes page and AOS. Status: open by day, the gate is locked at night (AOS read 2026-11-24; GC 2009). Caveats: listed; residents. Rank: Nice. Merge with monuments 4073 and 4072 (jordaan-3).
title: Raepenhofje and Bossche Hofje: one court, two hofjes, a hedge between
rank_text: Rank: Nice. Merge with monuments 4073 and 4072 (jordaan-3).

heading: Jordaan
text: **BW-03 Suykerhofje: only for women of a peaceful temper.** Pin 52.379738, 4.883394, Lindengracht 149 to 163. Founded 1667, court from 1670; admission asked for a "vreedzaam humeur". Lead: Jordaanweb hofjes page; second: walk 2023. Status: open weekdays, shut Saturday and Sunday (walk 2023). Caveats: listed; hours unconfirmed after 2023. Rank: Nice. Merge with monument 3549 (jordaan-3).
title: Suykerhofje: only for women of a peaceful temper

heading: Jordaan
text: **BW-04 Hofje De Zeven Keurvorsten: a gunpowder maker's Catholic hofje with its history in a chronogram.** Pin 52.376325, 4.879688, Tuinstraat 197 to 225. Founded about 1645 by gunpowder maker Cornelis Martensz. Pronck for poor Catholic women "van onbesproken gedrag"; seven houses added 1724, a prayer room over the gate 1778, the St Barbara chapel next door used from 1862 until after the war. The history is told in a chronogram in the court; a gable stone says "Alidaeshofje", a name that never caught on, and "Zeven Keurvorsten" may be a mocking name from Protestant neighbours. Renovated 2012, now 12 homes; monograph by Marijke Bruggeman (2009). Lead: nl.wikipedia "Hofje De Zeven Keurvorsten"; second: AOS. Status: usually open by day (AOS read 2026-11-24, walk 2023). Caveats: the mocking-name origin is "may be" in the source. Rank: Nice. Merge with monument 5769 (jordaan-5).
title: Hofje De Zeven Keurvorsten: a gunpowder maker's Catholic hofje with its history in a chronogram

heading: Jordaan
text: **BW-05 Constantiahofje: free homes for loyal old workmen.** Pin 52.380766, 4.881987, Willemsstraat 149 to 165. Built 1863 by P.J. Hamer for the Stichting voor den Ambachtsstand: rent-free homes for workmen over 60 who had served one employer at least 12 years; named after Constantia van Loon. The extra houses at 143 to 147 (1868/1873) carry the lettering "Constantia woningen"; Jordaanweb lists them as a "naamloos hofje". Lead: nl.wikipedia "Constantiahofje"; second: walk 2023. Status: gate open (walk 2023); Ymere owns it. Caveats: listed. Rank: Nice. Merge with monument 518324 (jordaan-6).
title: Constantiahofje: free homes for loyal old workmen

heading: Jordaan
text: **BW-06 Concordiahof: bleaching courts behind the Westerstraat.** Pin 52.377255, 4.880632 (pin approximate, Anjeliersstraat side of the block), entrances Westerstraat 221 to 289 and 327 to 405, Anjeliersstraat 308 to 394. Late-19th-century back-to-back workers' blocks of Bouwmaatschappij Concordia around two inner bleaching courts, reached through gates; summer hofjes concerts. Lead: Jordaanweb hofjes and Westerstraat pages; second: Jordaanweb hofjesconcerten map. Status: concerts listed on Jordaanweb (undated); day access not confirmed. Caveats: may be shut; pin approximate. Rank: Okay. New place.
title: Concordiahof: bleaching courts behind the Westerstraat

heading: Jordaan
text: **BW-07 Platanenhof: the Catholic boys' orphanage and the passages under it.** Pin 52.370704, 4.878710 (gate on the Lauriergracht; the slice point is 52.370039, 4.878850), Lauriergracht 99 to 105 / Elandsstraat 152 to 156. Catholic boys' orphanage from 1686 by Steven Vennecool, an orphanage until 1954, then De Triangel 1971 to 1992; now 22 homes, a youth theatre and a nursery; named in 1971 after its ten plane trees. Under the complex runs a system of passages, said to link to the old monasteries; in the war weapons for the resistance were hidden there; others think they are water cellars. Lead: Jordaanweb platanenhof page; second: nl.wikipedia "Platanenhof". Status: concert venue (Jordaanweb, undated); day access not confirmed. Caveats: the passages are not open and their purpose is disputed: tell it as a story with both versions. Rank: Nice. Merge with monument 1038 (jordaan-2).
title: Platanenhof: the Catholic boys' orphanage and the passages under it

heading: Jordaan
text: **BW-08 Rozenhofje: on the site of Lingelbach's maze.** Pin 52.372552, 4.878057, Rozengracht 147 to 181. Stands where Lingelbach's 17th-century doolhof (maze, a pleasure garden) was; five houses of 1743/1744 founded from Jan de Jager's estate for single Mennonite women; rebuilt 1884 by G.B. and A. Salm; a clock of 1790. Lead: nl.wikipedia "Rozengracht 147-181"; second: Jordaanweb hofjes page. Status: shut; open only on Open Monumentendag (JW). Caveats: the maze left no trace; listed. Rank: Nice. Merge with monument 5070 (jordaan-5).
title: Rozenhofje: on the site of Lingelbach's maze

heading: Jordaan
text: **BW-09 Hamers- en Bouwershofje, the "Verdriethuisjes".** Pin 52.374677, 4.876888, Marnixstraat 281 (back on Westerkade 21, the two fronts are the same). Two old hofjes merged here in 1877: De Hamer's little houses at Herengracht 373 to 387, sunk half below the street when the quay was raised and so called the "verdriethuisjes", and Marretje Arend Bouwersdochter's four houses in the Wijde Steeg (1634). The old residents paid almost no rent and would not move until the city let the old houses decay; the last came in 1885 and brought the old gable stone, a shield with swans (Syvert P. Sem) and leaves (Maria Bouwers). By J.H. Coelewij: 24 one-room homes off one corridor for widows and single women over 50; Vrouwen van Bethanië from 1925; now staff housing of Hotel Okura. Local voice: "verdriethuisjes". Lead: nl.wikipedia "Hamer en Bouwershofje"; second: Jordaanweb hofjes page. Status: building in use (Wikipedia, 2017 photos); no access. Caveats: see it from the street, both fronts; listed. Rank: Nice. Merge with monument 204043 (jordaan-3).
title: Hamers- en Bouwershofje, the "Verdriethuisjes"

heading: Jordaan
text: **BW-10 Hofje van de Weduwe Roosen: a hofje without a court.** Pin 52.367282, 4.881392, Eerste Passeerdersdwarsstraat 124 to 130. Four houses from the second half of the 18th century for eight single women who lived free; named after the widow Roosen in 1820, on a plaque "Het Hofjen van de Weduwe Roosen"; no garden, so the women made front gardens; a fully blind wall to the canal; it survived the 1990 clearance of the street. Lead: nl.wikipedia "Eerste Passeerdersdwarsstraat 124-130"; second: Jordaanweb hofjes page. Status: standing, owned by the Diaconie (Wikipedia). Caveats: private homes; listed. Rank: Okay. Merge with monument 4079 (jordaan-1).
title: Hofje van de Weduwe Roosen: a hofje without a court

heading: Jordaan
text: **BW-11 The Bleijskapel: a church nobody can see from the quay.** Pin 52.371307, 4.881111 (pin approximate: the front house; the chapel is behind it), Lauriergracht 39. An 1881/1882 neo-Gothic chapel by A.C. Bleijs for the RK Gesticht De Voorzienigheid, built entirely in an inner court with cast-iron columns, pointed arches and painted-over murals; the only chapel by Bleijs. Listed only in 1992, after neighbours objected to a developer's plan for 108 flats and a CDA council member took it up; the city had not seen the point. A host bakery was at number 37. Lead: nl.wikipedia "Lauriergracht achter 39"; second: RCE register 422548 (https://monumentenregister.cultureelerfgoed.nl/monumenten/pdf/422548). Status: offered on Funda as office space with "monumentale kapel" (search result, date not shown). Caveats: private, no access; nothing to see from the street but the church-like windows of number 39. Rank: Nice. Merge with monument 422548 (jordaan-2).
title: The Bleijskapel: a church nobody can see from the quay

heading: Jordaan
text: **BW-12 Lauriergracht 12: the last tile bakery, through a covered passage.** Pin 52.372020, 4.881896. Tile bakery De Twee Laurierbomen from 1808 to about 1854, the only one in Amsterdam after 1816; before it a steenkoperij (building-materials yard) for some two and a half centuries. A covered passage with a hardstone gutter for wheelbarrows leads to storage buildings and a mid-19th-century neo-Gothic wooden loggia (now a bike shed). Lead: https://stadsherstel.nl/monumenten/lauriergracht-12/; second: https://stadsherstel.nl/monumenten/achterhuis-lauriergracht-12/ and opslaghuisje-lauriergracht-12. Status: architects' office Rappange (Stadsherstel, read 2026-11-24). Caveats: not open: only the front and the passage door can be seen. Rank: Okay. Merge with monument 3221 (jordaan-2).
title: Lauriergracht 12: the last tile bakery, through a covered passage

heading: Jordaan
text: **BW-13 Lindenhofje.** Pin 52.380475, 4.885339, Lindengracht 94 to 112. One of the Lindengracht hofjes, listed. Lead: Jordaanweb hofjes page; second: Theo Bakker jordaangangen.pdf. Status: shut, "niet meer te bezoeken" (TB). Caveats: thin hook; keep as a line in a hofjes text unless more turns up. Rank: Okay. Merge with monument 204037 (jordaan-3).
title: Lindenhofje

heading: Jordaan
text: **BW-14 Broenshofje: six rooms off a corridor.** Pin 52.379222, 4.884561, Boomstraat 52. Founded 1851 by Mrs A.C. Broen: six rooms off a corridor for Protestant single women, f1 a week, fuel, and a party parcel at Easter, Christmas and Sinterklaas. Lead: Jordaanweb Boomstraat page; second: walk 2023. Status: shut (walk 2023). Caveats: not listed; front only. Rank: Okay. New place.
title: Broenshofje: six rooms off a corridor

heading: Jordaan
text: **BW-15 Regenboogs Liefdehofje.** Pin 52.377220, 4.882894, Tuinstraat 100 to 102. Lead: Jordaanweb hofjes page; second: walk 2023. Status: shut, "unfortunately cannot enter" (walk 2023). Caveats: thin hook. Rank: Okay. Merge with monument 215024 (jordaan-5).
title: Regenboogs Liefdehofje

heading: Jordaan
text: **BW-16 Rijpenhofje.** Pin 52.373168, 4.879108, Rozengracht 116 to 138. Lead: Jordaanweb Rozengracht page: a dull gatehouse replaced three houses in 1912. Second: Jordaanweb hofjes page. Status: unknown access. Caveats: thin. Rank: Okay. Merge with monument 215008 (jordaan-5).
title: Rijpenhofje

heading: Grachtengordel-West
text: **BW-17 Van Brienenhofje "De Star": the blind wall on the Prinsengracht.** Pin 52.378676, 4.887269, Prinsengracht 85 to 133. Built 1804 to 1806 by city architect Abraham van der Hart on the site of the De Star brewery, for poor Catholics, founded by Aernout (Arnoud) Jan van Brienen; the canal front is completely blind. Owned by housing association Het Oosten since 1995 (search result summary of the HMDB marker). Lead: walk 2023; second: https://www.hmdb.org/m.asp?m=253756. Status: open Mon to Fri 6:00 to 18:00, Sat 6:00 to 14:00 (walk 2023). Caveats: the often-told legend that Van Brienen founded it after being locked in his strongroom found no source in this scout's search: do not use it unless another scout sources it; the founder's first name varies. Rank: Nice. Merge with monument 4268 (gg-west-4).
title: Van Brienenhofje "De Star": the blind wall on the Prinsengracht

heading: Grachtengordel-West
text: **BW-18 Nieuwe Suykerhofje.** Pin 52.371524, 4.883444, Prinsengracht 385 to 395. Lead: Jordaanweb hofjes page; second: nl.wikipedia category Hofje in Amsterdam. Status: access unknown. Caveats: thin hook; check at the door. Rank: Okay. Merge with monument 4328 (gg-west-4).
title: Nieuwe Suykerhofje

heading: Grachtengordel-West
text: **BW-19 De Rode Hoed: the hidden church in the middle of the block.** Pin 52.377355, 4.887269, Keizersgracht 102. A hat-maker's until 1629; in 1630 the Remonstrants built their schuilkerk Vrijburg here, in the middle of the block with houses on all four sides and no access from any street; galleries, arched windows and a small rose window; in use as a church until 1957. Its great hall is the largest and oldest surviving hidden church in the country. To keep it hidden the congregation bought or rented nearly all the houses around. Huub Oosterhuis found it empty in 1989 and opened a debate centre on 14 September 1990 (Sonja Barend, Het Lagerhuis, the 2022 Wie is de Mol? finale). Lead: nl.wikipedia "Rode Hoed"; second: Catharijneconvent Rapport Schuilkerken. Status: debate centre, events (Wikipedia mentions 2024). Caveats: open only for events; listed. Rank: **Amazing**. Merge with monument 2485 (gg-west-3).
title: De Rode Hoed: the hidden church in the middle of the block

heading: Grachtengordel-West
text: **BW-20 The garden house that travelled: behind Keizersgracht 62 to 64.** Pin 52.378212, 4.888097 (pin approximate: the front house). Built 1699 behind Keizersgracht 587 to 589; dismantled in 1917 for De Bazel's building and the widening of the Vijzelstraat; the overgrown parts turned up in 1966 in the garden of Herengracht 466 and were rebuilt here 1971 to 1973 as the music room of the Amsterdams Muzieklyceum, where Johan Cruijff signed a lottery contract. Lead: https://stadsherstel.nl/monumenten/keizersgracht-62-64-tuinhuis/; second: https://stadsherstel.nl/monumenten/keizersgracht-62/ (the sugar plantation and ice factory of number 64). Status: Euro Business Center (Stadsherstel, read 2026-11-24). Caveats: not public, not visible from the street. Rank: Okay. New place.
title: The garden house that travelled: behind Keizersgracht 62 to 64

heading: Grachtengordel-West
text: **BW-21 Onze-Lieve-Vrouwekerk: a church built in on three sides.** Pin 52.373119, 4.884542, Keizersgracht 220. Built 1852 to 1854 by Theo Molkenboer for the Redemptorists next to their monastery at 218, inside the block, with only the canal front visible; the first neo-Gothic church north of Brabant and Limburg. The Redemptorists left in 1985 and the Syriac Orthodox bought it (Moeder Godskerk); Catholics also use it. Lead: nl.wikipedia "Onze-Lieve-Vrouwekerk (Amsterdam)"; second: RCE 2535 in slice. Status: in use (Wikipedia, read 2026-11-24). Caveats: open at services; check visiting. Rank: Okay. Merge with monument 2535 (gg-west-3).
title: Onze-Lieve-Vrouwekerk: a church built in on three sides

heading: Haarlemmerbuurt
text: **BW-22 West-Indisch Huis: the meat hall where the WIC met.** Pin 52.380161, 4.892040, Herenmarkt 99 / Haarlemmerstraat 75. Opened 1617 as a meat hall and guard room; WIC directors from 1623 to 1647; hotel from 1660, old people's home from 1825; the courtyard lies behind. In 1835 the wooden soup kitchen on the Herenmarkt burnt in the Soeploodsoproer. Lead: nl.wikipedia "Herenmarkt"; second: slice record 1372. Status: offices, congresses, weddings, John Adams Institute (Wikipedia). Caveats: the courtyard's public access and a statue in it were not confirmed: check before claiming; listed. Rank: Nice. Merge with monument 1372 (haarlemmer-1).
title: West-Indisch Huis: the meat hall where the WIC met

heading: Jordaan
text: **BW-23 Marnixstraat 291 to 293: houses on the old bastion, below the street.** Pin 52.374353, 4.876715, Marnixstraat 291 to 293 / Westerkade 23 to 25. Three houses stand behind the street line and lower than it, probably older than the levelling of the rampart De Schans (dug away after 1877); a group of buildings already shows here on the 1625 Berckenrode map. Stone blocks of the old bastion survive along the sunken lane in front of 291 and 293. In 1917 the spot was already "Verdwijnend Amsterdam". Lead: https://stadsherstel.nl/monumenten/marnixstraat-291/; second: Stadsherstel Vriendenwandeling 2025 PDF. Status: Stadsherstel homes (page read 2026-11-24). Caveats: not in the monument slices; private homes, seen from the street. Rank: **Amazing**. New place (group with DW-24 for the bastion line).
title: Marnixstraat 291 to 293: houses on the old bastion, below the street
rank_text: Rank: **Amazing**. New place (group with DW-24 for the bastion line).

heading: Jordaan
text: **BW-24 Westerkade 1 to 9: the first homes on the levelled rampart.** Pin 52.376922, 4.878360 (Westerkade 5), Westerkade 1 to 9 / Marnixstraat 215 to 231. Block A of 1876 to 1877 by Bastiaan de Greef for the Amsterdamsche Vereeniging tot het bouwen van Arbeiderswoningen: back-to-back one-room homes to relieve the overcrowded Jordaan, on land between the Raam- and Zaagbarrière; the Westerkade got its name only after (16 November 1876). Lead: nl.wikipedia "Westerkade 1-9"; second: none. Status: apartments (Wikipedia). Caveats: modest to look at; story-led. Rank: Okay. New place.
title: Westerkade 1 to 9: the first homes on the levelled rampart

heading: Jordaan
text: **BW-25 Westerstraat 202: a 1770 soap boiler's stone in a 1980s wall.** Pin 52.378128, 4.881063. A double anachronism: a 20th-century building carrying a 1770 gable stone. Herman Lelijman's soap works stood here on the Anjeliersgracht and paid for a country house in Geuzenveld; later a school of Sint Aloysius, demolished; new-build 1986. Lead: nl.wikipedia "Westerstraat 202 (Amsterdam)"; second: Jordaanweb Westerstraat page. Status: standing (Wikipedia). Caveats: small. Rank: Okay. New place.
title: Westerstraat 202: a 1770 soap boiler's stone in a 1980s wall

heading: Jordaan
text: **BW-26 Palmgracht 74: a cake-slice school that stood on two canals.** Pin 52.382080, 4.882457, Palmgracht 74 / Lijnbaansgracht 15A to C. The 21st public paupers' school (early 1870s, Publieke Werken under Bastiaan de Greef) in the triangle of Lijnbaansgracht, Palmgracht and Brouwersgracht, built with a high bridge at the door; the Palmgracht was filled in 1895 for hygiene; the school closed in 1976; now a business centre, municipal monument 2007. Lead: nl.wikipedia "Palmgracht 74"; second: none. Status: business centre (Wikipedia). Rank: Okay. New place.
title: Palmgracht 74: a cake-slice school that stood on two canals

heading: Jordaan
text: **BW-27 Blijvend Applaus: Wim Sonneveld's houses for old artists.** Pin 52.376318, 4.882244 (pin approximate), Egelantiersgracht 72 to 74. Houses of the Stichting Blijvend Applaus, founded by Wim Sonneveld to give (retired) artists cheap homes; over the entrance the gable stone Sonneveld had put up. Lead: Stadsherstel Vriendenwandeling 2025 PDF. Second: none found. Status: per the 2025 walk. Caveats: the house numbers need checking against the walk text (a search summary placed a stop at Egelantiersgracht 51); one source only. Rank: Okay. New place.
title: Blijvend Applaus: Wim Sonneveld's houses for old artists

heading: Jordaan
text: **BW-28 Bloemgracht 76: Blaeu's printing house.** Pin 52.374937, 4.881159. Joan Blaeu set up a printing house here about 1637 (Stadsherstel walk 2025). Lead: Stadsherstel Vriendenwandeling 2025 PDF. Second: none yet. Caveats: check against a Blaeu source before use. Rank: Okay. New place.
title: Bloemgracht 76: Blaeu's printing house

heading: Haarlemmerbuurt
text: **BW-29 De Kruiwagen, Singel 2: a timber house in brick clothes.** Pin 52.379524, 4.894368, Singel 2 to 2a. Built 1606 by herring buyer Jan Loots as a medieval-style self-supporting timber frame clad in brick, 11 by 11.6 m; Hendrick Jansz. Cruywagen added the wheelbarrow gable stone about 1660; the Buiksloter ferry house until 1661, and half of it a café ever since (photographed by Olie and Breitner); a hoisting installation with a huge wheel survives inside. Lead: Theo Bakker haarlemmerbuurt.pdf; second: slice record 5249. Status: café (TB). Caveats: the wheel is inside; listed. Rank: Nice. Merge with monument 5249 (haarlemmer-2).
title: De Kruiwagen, Singel 2: a timber house in brick clothes

heading: Haarlemmerbuurt
text: **BW-30 Haarlemmerplein: the last real wagon square, and Drees's stone.** Pin 52.384259, 4.883358 (Haarlemmerplein 23). Theo Bakker: the only wagenplein of the city that stayed a working wagon square into the 20th century. At number 23 a gable stone for Willem Drees, placed 1986 with a counter-demonstration. Haarlemmerplein 2 collapsed in 1919. Lead: Theo Bakker haarlemmerbuurt.pdf; second: slice record 1356. Caveats: the square is rebuilt; the stone is the object. Rank: Okay. Merge with monument 1356 (haarlemmer-1); DW-31 and DW-33 are on the same square.
title: Haarlemmerplein: the last real wagon square, and Drees's stone
rank_text: Rank: Okay. Merge with monument 1356 (haarlemmer-1); DW-31 and DW-33 are on the same square.

heading: Haarlemmerbuurt
text: **BW-31 Vinkenstraat 39: the crèche the queens visited.** Pin 52.381760, 4.887572. In 1872 the Vereeniging tot verbetering der kleine kinderbewaarplaatsen opened its first branch here, open 7:00 to 21:30; Queen Emma visited in 1873 (92 children), Wilhelmina came by coach in 1926. Rebuilt 1904 by Coenraad Wiegand from two houses, with yellow frames and a large tile panel recalling the crèche. Lead: nl.wikipedia "Vinkenstraat 39"; second: none. Status: standing (Wikipedia). Rank: Okay. New place.
