title: Vinkenstraat 39: the crèche the queens visited

heading: Haarlemmerbuurt
text: **BW-32 De Keijser, Zandhoek 13: Stadsherstel's first restoration, Jacob Olie's grandfather's house.** Pin 52.388062, 4.889984. Built 1645 by Reinier Reael, after whom the island is named; later owned by Jacob Olie's grandfather, and Olie photographed his Orange-minded neighbours here when Queen Wilhelmina drove by. Stadsherstel's first restoration (owned 1957, restored 1959). Lead: https://stadsherstel.nl/monumenten/de-keijser-zandhoek-13/ (path from the sitemap); second: Stadsherstel page In Den Gouden Reael (Zandhoek 14). Status: homes (Stadsherstel). Caveats: private. Rank: Okay. New place.
title: De Keijser, Zandhoek 13: Stadsherstel's first restoration, Jacob Olie's grandfather's house

heading: Haarlemmerbuurt
text: **BW-33 De Oude Amsterdammer, Korte Prinsengracht 5.** Pin 52.381861, 4.890082. 1652, for the timber merchants Van Marcken, who stacked Norwegian wood on the quay; a tapperij from 1879 into the 1950s (Café Spoorzicht in 1932); the corner shopfront with two doors still shows the bar. Lead: Stadsherstel page "De oude Amsterdammer" (korte-prinsengracht-5-haarlemmer-houttuinen-65a); second: none. Status: home (Stadsherstel). Rank: Okay. New place.
title: De Oude Amsterdammer, Korte Prinsengracht 5

heading: Grachtengordel-West
text: **BW-34 De Posthoorn: a hidden church in a post-coach house.** Pin 52.379956, 4.888076, Prinsengracht 7. About 1687 the Augustinian hidden church moved into the former post-coach house "de Posthoorn"; a posthorn is still in the facade above the original entrance; the Posthoorngang gate was at Brouwersgracht 81 to 89. Its successor is Cuypers' Posthoornkerk, Haarlemmerstraat 124 (1860), his first of six Amsterdam churches, now a Stadsherstel event venue. Lead: Theo Bakker papeneiland.pdf; second: https://stadsherstel.nl/monumenten/de-posthoornkerk/. Status: Prinsengracht 7 a house; the church an event venue (Stadsherstel, read 2026-11-24). Caveats: private house; look for the horn. Rank: Nice. New place; group with monument 1289 (haarlemmer-1).
title: De Posthoorn: a hidden church in a post-coach house
rank_text: Rank: Nice. New place; group with monument 1289 (haarlemmer-1).

heading: Grachtengordel-West
text: **BW-35 Pottenbakkersgang: a path older than the canal belt.** Pin 52.375177, 4.888718 (pin approximate), Herengracht between 151 and 155. A pre-1612 path (Pottenbakkerspad on the Pottenbakkersweer) that was absorbed into the canal belt and can still be traced (TB). Lead: Theo Bakker jordaangangen.pdf; second: none (a search found only the Westerstraat alley). Caveats: not the slum alley of the same name at Westerstraat 216 to 226, whose houses went to the Openluchtmuseum Arnhem in 2002; pin approximate; nothing marked. Rank: Okay. New place.
title: Pottenbakkersgang: a path older than the canal belt

heading: Grachtengordel-West
text: **BW-36 Lekkeresluis: the rattle watch's room in the arch.** Pin 52.380374, 4.888292. The first arch was bricked up as the guard room of the ratelwacht; until about 1916 a wooden walkway ran from the stone steps (still there) to a door in the arch. The bridge is of 1754 ("Anno 1754" stones). Lead: Theo Bakker papeneiland.pdf; second: nl.wikipedia "Lekkeresluis". Status: municipal monument 1995. Rank: Okay. Group with DW-23.
title: Lekkeresluis: the rattle watch's room in the arch

heading: Grachtengordel-West
text: **BW-37 Langestraat 80: the Tsar in the gable and the Hollandsche Mediaeval.** Pin 52.377200, 4.890987. A very tall house of 1664; in 1713 "the house with the Tsaar van Moscovieen in the gable" (why is unclear); studio of S.H. de Roos, who designed the Hollandsche Mediaeval typeface (1912); Stadsherstel's second restoration (1957). Lead: https://stadsherstel.nl/monumenten/langestraat-80/; second: none. Rank: Okay. New place.
title: Langestraat 80: the Tsar in the gable and the Hollandsche Mediaeval

heading: Grachtengordel-West
text: **BW-38 Blauwburgwal, 10 May 1940: the corner the bombs took.** Pin 52.376621, 4.890038 (Herengracht 107). The bombing of May 1940 destroyed Herengracht 105 to 107 and Blauwburgwal 17 to 25 with deaths; the corner was a parking lot for six years; in 1951 coffee firm Matagalpa (before the war Cohen Bendiks, renamed on the occupier's order) built the office by Theo Lammers and Karel Sijmons. Across the water Blauwburgwal 22 (bakery of Prior's Papbeschuit, 52.376900, 4.890300) was shored up, and Van Gendt's auction house at Blauwburgwal 15 survives cut down. Lead: nl.wikipedia "Herengracht 107"; second: nl.wikipedia "Blauwburgwal 22" and "Blauwburgwal 15". Status: standing (Wikipedia). Caveats: the Wikipedia articles give 10 and 11 May: check the date; look for a memorial plaque on site before claiming one. Rank: Nice. New place.
title: Blauwburgwal, 10 May 1940: the corner the bombs took

heading: Grachtengordel-West
text: **BW-39 De Dolphijn, Singel 140 to 142: the Night Watch captain's house.** Pin 52.375641, 4.890079. Built 1599 to 1602 for the poet Hendrik Laurensz. Spiegel to a pared-down Hendrick de Keyser design; one of three early-17th-century houses with a side house (with Bartolotti and the Huis met de Hoofden); Frans Banninck Cocq lived here while Rembrandt painted his company, the Night Watch (1640 to 1642). Lead: nl.wikipedia "De Dolphijn"; second: none read. Status: private (Wikipedia). Rank: Nice. New place.
title: De Dolphijn, Singel 140 to 142: the Night Watch captain's house

heading: Grachtengordel-West
text: **BW-40 Huis Van Brienen, Herengracht 284: a top-100 interior.** Pin 52.370674, 4.886552. On the site of "In de Stadt Praegh" (about 1620); rebuilt 1728 to 1733 for the Mennonite merchant David Rutgers and his sisters with a garden house and back house; bought 1781 by Arnold Johan van Brienen as a wedding gift for his son Willem Joseph, mayor under Lodewijk Napoleon; one of the top 100 interiors in the Netherlands. Lead: nl.wikipedia "Huis Van Brienen"; second: slice record 1795. Status: owner and visiting not confirmed (Hendrick de Keyser pages not readable). Caveats: the interior is the point; private unless a tour is found. Rank: Okay. Merge with monument 1795 (gg-west-2).
title: Huis Van Brienen, Herengracht 284: a top-100 interior

heading: Sweep 6: modern and contested / Burgwallen-Nieuwe Zijde
text: **CC-01. The bicycle garage under the water at Stationsplein.** Pin 52.379300, 4.901000 (approximate, the entrance on the Stationsplein, reverse-geocodes to Stationsplein 35M). Under the Open Havenfront, nine metres below the water, about 7,000 bikes park in a garage built from 2018 and opened around 2023; its sister garage at the IJboulevard (4,000 places) opened on 22 February 2023. Hidden inside: two sgraffito wall pieces of 1965 by Lex Horn, each about 3 by 7 metres, saved from the demolished Jan Swammerdam Instituut and moved here in one piece. The pair replaced the Fietsflat of 2001. Local voice: none found yet. Lead https://nl.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fietsenstalling_Stationsplein_(Amsterdam) ; second source needed (gemeente or Wurck project page). Status: in use (wiki, read 24 Nov 2026). Caveats: exact pin of the Horn panels inside not known; check that they are visible to the public. Rank **Nice**. New place.
title: The bicycle garage under the water at Stationsplein

heading: Sweep 6: modern and contested / Burgwallen-Oude Zijde
text: **CC-02. Blaauwlakenblok: the block the Bijenkorf wanted, the squatters held and the residents rebuilt (with W139 and the Condomerie).** Pin 52.373215, 4.896842 (gate of the Blaauwlakensteeg; W139 at Warmoesstraat 139, 52.373751, 4.895988; Condomerie at Warmoesstraat 141, 52.373679, 4.895872). The diamond-shaped block between Warmoesstraat, Sint Annenstraat, OZ Voorburgwal and Sint Jansstraat was earmarked in the 1960s for large-scale "city" building: De Bijenkorf owned much of it for offices and a garage (the garage went to the Beursplein instead). Squatters took it in the late 1970s, the city bought the houses in 1983, and after years of residents' participation about sixty monumental houses were restored with over a hundred homes and dozens of workspaces (finished early this century). Four gated alleys cut through it; the Zwartlakensteeg leaves by the Oliphantsgang, 70 cm wide. W139, squatted in 1979 by young artists in a former cinema used as Bijenkorf storage, was a home of the Nieuwe Wilden (Rob Birza, Peter Klashorst) and still runs free shows; the Condomerie next door opened on 1 May 1987 as probably the world's first condom shop. Local voice: on W139's reopening after the renovation (19 January 2007) the board said the building should be "as public as a post office, only with longer opening hours" (d'Oude Binnenstad, April 2007); in 2009 the district showed residents a Project 1012 film while discussing the renovated block (OpNieuw 2009-2). Lead https://nl.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blaauwlakenblok ; second https://nl.wikipedia.org/wiki/W139 and d'Oude Binnenstad 2007-1 (DC's `ob/OB2007.1.6.w.one`). Status: W139 and Condomerie open (Condomerie advert in d'Oude Binnenstad April 2020; W139 in OpNieuw 2021-4 as partner of "Ongekend Zeedijk"). Caveats: alleys gated, residents and visitors only, so the pitch is the gates, the open front of W139 and the shop; BC lists "Torpedo Theater, W139" as a theme C lead. Rank **Amazing**. New place.
title: Blaauwlakenblok: the block the Bijenkorf wanted, the squatters held and the residents rebuilt (with W139 and the Condomerie)

heading: Sweep 6: modern and contested / Burgwallen-Oude Zijde
text: **CC-03. Oudezijds Armsteeg "street gallery".** Pin to set on site (Oudezijds Armsteeg, OZ; not point-checked as no exact spot is known). In August 2013 residents turned a dumping corner of the steeg into an open-air gallery of small street vitrines, after geveltuinen had already reclaimed it (d'Oude Binnenstad 2013-3). Local voice: it is a residents' own project against litter on the Wallen edge. Lead: d'Oude Binnenstad 2013-3 (DC's `ob/`); second source needed. Status: unverified since 2013. Caveats: may be gone; check on site before anything. Rank **Okay** (conditional). New place, or a Look for for AC-09 (White Cube, Nieuwezijds Armsteeg is the other Armsteeg, so do not merge by name).
title: Oudezijds Armsteeg "street gallery"
rank_text: Rank **Okay** (conditional). New place, or a Look for for AC-09 (White Cube, Nieuwezijds Armsteeg is the other Armsteeg, so do not merge by name).

heading: Sweep 6: modern and contested / Nieuwmarkt/Lastage
text: **CC-04. The Stopera and the NAP under it.** Pin 52.367726, 4.902017 (the NAP display in the passage between Amstel and Waterlooplein). Town hall and opera house in one, by Wilhelm Holzbauer and Cees Dam (opera opened 23 September 1986, town hall in use from 1988), chosen from 803 competition entries in 1968. The fight: "Het stadhuis staat op de Dam" campaigners, the name read as "Stop de opera", and on the first pile day (5 July 1982) protesters wrecked and set fire to machines, after which the site was fenced. It ran more than 100 million guilders over budget. In the passage: the NAP monument by Louis van Gasteren and Kees van der Veer (1988), with a bolt at 0 m NAP and water columns (what each column shows: check on site). In autumn 2026 Stichting NAP opened an info point here and runs a "Boutfunding" campaign until 31 December 2026 for a new NAP museum (target 100,000 euros). Local voice: nickname "Het Kunstgebit" (the dentures, seen from the Blauwbrug); OpNieuw calls it "deze kille kolos" whose sight still gives "painful stabs in the warm Amsterdam heart" (Haije Bouwman, OpNieuw 2003-4), "nog steeds een steen des aanstoots" (OpNieuw 2007-4) and "dat spuuglelijke gebouw dat Stopera heet" (market traders' piece, OpNieuw 2017-1). Lead https://nl.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stopera ; second https://nl.wikipedia.org/wiki/Normaal_Amsterdams_Peil and https://www.architectuur.org/bouwwerk/197/Stadhuis_Muziektheater.html ; NAP campaign: rodi.nl (15 Oct 2026); nickname and Schippers detail from feitjes.amsterdam and architectuur.org (read earlier today; recheck the exact page). Status: open; info point open since 16 Oct 2026. Caveats: AC lists the NAP display as theme C and AC-15 (Violist) sits in the same building: group AC-15 and the wedding room by Wim T. Schippers under this item. The Stopera is not on A-LIST.md. Rank **Amazing**. New place.
title: The Stopera and the NAP under it

heading: Sweep 6: modern and contested / Nieuwmarkt/Lastage
text: **CC-05. Where the Maupoleum stood: the "Colosseum" and the green glass box.** Pin 52.369605, 4.901658 (Theaterschool, Jodenbreestraat 3); second pin 52.368389, 4.905577 (Filmacademie, Markenplein 1). The Maupoleum (1971 to 1994), Maup Caransa's brutalist block, was long called the ugliest building in Amsterdam. Its replacement was nicknamed before it was even finished: "Het wordt nu al in de volksmond het Colosseum genoemd" (OpNieuw 1996-1); it houses the Academie voor Theater en Dans and a city office. Across the square the Filmacademie (Koen van Velzen, 1999, a tight front of green glass) promptly inherited the "ugliest building" title. Local voice: OpNieuw ran a street poll in 1998 ("Een ouderwetse zwarte doos", Haije Bouwman): "Vreselijk, vreselijk", "op een weiland waar niemand het ziet, zo lelijk vind ik het", and "it goes well with that ugly Stopera"; the client replied in OpNieuw 1999-1. Lead https://nl.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mr._Visserplein ; second https://nl.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maupoleum and OpNieuw 1996-1, 1998-3 (DC's `on/txt/`). Status: both in use (wiki, 24 Nov 2026). Caveats: the Goslerhuisje draft already mentions the Maupoleum; pitch this on the successors and the nicknames. Rank **Nice**. New place.
title: Where the Maupoleum stood: the "Colosseum" and the green glass box

heading: Sweep 6: modern and contested / Nieuwmarkt/Lastage
text: **CC-06. The tunnel under the Mr. Visserplein: a motorway that never came.** Pin 52.367950, 4.903100 (approximate, on the square; reverse-geocodes to Waterlooplein 207). The square was laid out in 1967-68 for a broad road that was to cut through the Nieuwmarktbuurt to the Central Station; the Nieuwmarkt fight stopped the road, but the car tunnel under the square was built. Its pedestrian tunnel was later bricked up; from 2003 to 2020 the tunnel held the children's play hall TunFun (bankrupt in the pandemic), and since then the VROG foundation uses it for freerunning, trampoline and urban dance. Local voice: none found yet. Lead https://nl.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mr._Visserplein ; second source needed (VROG). Status: VROG use per wiki (read 24 Nov 2026). Caveats: entrance pin to be fixed; only open for classes. Rank **Okay**. Group with CC-05 if preferred.
title: The tunnel under the Mr. Visserplein: a motorway that never came
rank_text: Rank **Okay**. Group with CC-05 if preferred.

heading: Sweep 6: modern and contested / Nieuwmarkt/Lastage
text: **CC-07. Arcam: the folded aluminium pavilion on the Oosterdok.** Pin 52.371509, 4.912474 (Prins Hendrikkade 600). Amsterdam's architecture centre sits in René van Zuuk's compact sculpture of coated aluminium folded over the roof to the ground, glass to the water. The brief was to swallow Renzo Piano's small lookout pavilion for his New Metropolis (now NEMO) and to look as modest as possible from the Scheepvaartmuseum, so it is lower on the water side. Free entry to the exhibition floor; since 2020 a "Tijdlijn Amsterdam 2000-2030" downstairs. Local voice: none found yet. Lead https://arcam.nl/over-arcam/over-het-gebouw/ (read 24 Nov 2026); second source needed (nl.wiki Arcam was rate-limited). Status: open (site, 24 Nov 2026). Caveats: the 2003 date is from memory; verify. NEMO itself is A-list; this is beside it, pitched on itself. Rank **Nice**. New place.
title: Arcam: the folded aluminium pavilion on the Oosterdok

heading: Sweep 6: modern and contested / Nieuwmarkt/Lastage
text: **CC-08. OBA Oosterdok: the free view from the library roof.** Pin 52.375824, 4.908375 (Oosterdokskade 143). The central library by Jo Coenen opened on 7 July 2007 (7/7/7) on the Oosterdokseiland, where the PTT post sorting tower (Merkelbach and Elling, 1968; Stedelijk's temporary home until 2008; demolished 2009 despite Heemschut) stood. Its top floor has a café and a terrace with one of the few free high views of the old city; it also houses IHLIA, the LGBTI heritage archive. Local voice: none found yet. Lead https://nl.wikipedia.org/wiki/Openbare_Bibliotheek_Amsterdam ; second https://nl.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oosterdokseiland . Status: open (wiki). Caveats: popular, but not on A-LIST.md; check whether the terrace is open year-round. Rank **Okay**. New place.
title: OBA Oosterdok: the free view from the library roof

heading: Sweep 7: curiosities, green and odd museums / Burgwallen-Nieuwe Zijde
text: **CC-09. Beurspassage, the "Amsterdam Oersoep".** Pin 52.374714, 4.894597 (passage between Damrak and Nieuwendijk). A dark passage left after the 1963 C&A fire was turned in 2016, when Damrak 70-79 was rebuilt, into an underwater canal: mosaic and glass ceiling by Arno Coenen and Iris Roskam full of Amsterdam things (herring, chips, tulips, bikes), chandeliers by Hans van Bentem made of bicycle parts, and a public drinking tap with a bronze fish head. Local voice: none found yet. Lead https://nl.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amsterdam_Oersoep ; second https://nl.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beurspassage . Status: open public passage (Atlas Obscura list, 24 Nov 2026). Caveats: AC and BC mention the ceiling only as a lead; it is on no shortlist. Rank **Nice**. New place.
title: Beurspassage, the "Amsterdam Oersoep"

heading: Sweep 7: curiosities, green and odd museums / Nieuwmarkt/Lastage
text: **CC-10. The plane trees of the Nieuwmarkt: a square that fought over trees.** Pin 52.372600, 4.900400 (east side of the Nieuwmarkt; reverse-geocodes to Nieuwmarkt 4). In 1991 a residents' foundation raised about 20,000 guilders to plant plane trees on the bare square; others wrote in to stop it. In 1993 the council asked for a tree plan, residents cut down the planners' version (they objected to "packing in" the Waag with ten pleached planes), and in mid-December 1995 the planes went in with a small party. Today the city's tree consultant names them as the square's shade trees among the elms of the Wallen. Local voice: "laat het leukste, spannendste en mooiste open plein van Amsterdam niet vertrutten tot de brink van Dwingeloo" (letter, OpNieuw 1991-4); the alternative from one Flesseman resident: grow ivy on the lamp posts. Lead OpNieuw 1991-4, 1993-4, 1995-3/4 (DC's `on/txt/`); second: d'Oude Binnenstad 2021-3 (Hans Kaljee walk). Status: trees standing (Kaljee, October 2021). Caveats: OpNieuw 2008-2 dates the planting to 1996; the 1995 issue announces it for 11 to 15 December 1995. Rank **Nice**. New place.
title: The plane trees of the Nieuwmarkt: a square that fought over trees

heading: Sweep 7: curiosities, green and odd museums / Nieuwmarkt/Lastage
text: **CC-11. Museumhaven Oosterdok: twenty working boats that are not a museum ship.** Pin 52.372991, 4.912696 (Oosterdok, along the Prins Hendrikkade by Arcam). The Vereniging Museumhaven Amsterdam (40 years in 2025) moors over twenty historic working vessels here, lived in and sailed, and holds the yearly Y-zeilen (32nd edition 5 Sept 2026) and a market for ship parts. Local voice: none found yet. Lead https://www.museumhavenamsterdam.nl/ (read 24 Nov 2026); second source needed (nl.wiki rate-limited). Status: active (site news March 2026). Caveats: boats are private homes, seen from the quay. Rank **Okay**. Group with CC-07 if preferred.
