heading: Sweep 6: modern and contested / De Weteringschans
text: **CE-01. Weteringschans 81-89: where the Grote Wetering squat fell, with Sinterklaas at the barricade (gone).** Pin 52.361200, 4.887130 (the 1983 building on the site, Weteringschans 81-89, on the corner of the Spiegelgracht line). A dairy cooperative's eclectic block of 1892-93 (Joseph Cuypers, son of the Rijksmuseum architect) was bought in the 1970s by the property dealer Gerard Bakker, who set out to demolish it; alderman Jan Schaefer stood for renovation, the empty part was squatted, Bakker started knocking down without a permit and was ordered by the court to restore it, and a request to list the building was refused. On 2 December 1980 the riot police cleared it in one of the hard evictions of that year; the city even sent Sinterklaas along, which backfired. The squatters were driven in a city bus to the Bijlmer prison and released at Amstel station. The new block of shops, offices and homes stood by 1983. Local voice: Ons Amsterdam "Hier gebeurde het: Weteringschans 2 december 1980" (to read in the browser). Lead: https://nl.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grote_Wetering_(Amsterdam) ; second: Ons Amsterdam article (linked from the wiki), Delpher papers of 3 Dec 1980. Status: the 1983 building stands; nothing marks the eviction. Caveats: gone thing with a strong story and an exact spot; the Peper en Zout offices (wetering-3) are the other half of the same Bakker fight: could be a paragraph there instead. **Okay**; new place or merge into "Peper en Zout, the hated offices that became monuments".
title: Weteringschans 81-89: where the Grote Wetering squat fell, with Sinterklaas at the barricade (gone)
rank_text: **Okay**; new place or merge into "Peper en Zout, the hated offices that became monuments".

heading: Sweep 6: modern and contested / De Weteringschans
text: **CE-02. The robot car park under the Vijzelgracht and its poem cabins.** Pin 52.361500, 4.891700 (the glass lift cabins on the Vijzelgracht, over the metro station; check: Location of the cabins). Over the Noord/Zuidlijn station Vijzelgracht a 120 m concrete box holds 270 cars parked by a fully automatic system: the driver leaves the car in a glass cabin on the street and a machine takes it down. The cabins, designed with the neighbourhood by Angie Abbink and Raymond Verkade, echo the weavers' houses nearby and the steel bridges, and the street paving runs on into them; city poet Marjolijn van Heemstra's lines are set in the glass (lettering by Roosje Klap) and light up when sun or headlights hit them. Opened 29 August 2023; the city took parking places off the street in return. The Vijzelgracht itself was filled in 1933, so the name is a fib. Lead: https://nl.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parkeergarage_Vijzelgracht ; second needed (gemeente project page or Benthem Crouwel). Status: open (2023). **Okay**; new place.
title: The robot car park under the Vijzelgracht and its poem cabins

heading: Sweep 6: modern and contested / De Weteringschans
text: **CE-25. Melkweg, the milk factory that became a hippie "cosmic centre".** Pin 52.364837, 4.881273 (Lijnbaansgracht 234A). A sugar refinery from 1854 (successor of the 18th-century "De Granaatappel", Spakler & Tetterode) became a dairy in 1920 and closed in 1969; in summer 1970 a youth project moved into the empty factory with a tea house, a restaurant and one hall for music, film and theatre, repeated in 1971 and 1972, and since 1973 it has been open for good: a non-profit foundation that grew from a hippie hangout into the city's pop stage (U2's first gig outside Ireland, Nirvana, Prince), with a cinema and an exhibition space. Since 2009 the Rabozaal hangs between the Melkweg and the Stadsschouwburg. Together with the drafted Paradiso, the other half of the 1970s free-space pair round the Leidseplein; Paradiso is pitched on its church past, this one on the occupation of an empty factory. Lead: https://nl.wikipedia.org/wiki/Melkweg_(Amsterdam) ; second: https://www.melkweg.nl/en/about-us/history/ (read 24 Nov 2026). Status: open. Caveats: a commercial-scale venue many visitors know; not on A-LIST.md (judge against it); the building's monument status to check. **Nice**; new place.
title: Melkweg, the milk factory that became a hippie "cosmic centre"

heading: Sweep 6: modern and contested / Weesperbuurt/Plantage
text: **CE-03. Weesperstaete, "De Doodskist".** Pin 52.361600, 4.907300 (Weesperplein, corner Sarphatistraat; Weesperplein 8 to confirm). Alexander Bodon's nine-storey office of 1969, called "the coffin" by Amsterdammers, was a dark glass box that Ids Haagsma called a copy of Mies van der Rohe's Seagram Building; Bodon wanted two more floors and a crown but the aesthetics committee refused. It stands back from the Sarphatistraat because that street, like the Weesperstraat, was to become a wide traffic artery in the 1960s "cityvorming", and a metro entrance is built into its base. Let to the university (psychology) in 1971, then a polytechnic; stripped and given opening windows in a renovation after 2003; now the city's development company. Lead: https://nl.wikipedia.org/wiki/Weesperstaete ; second: https://arcam.nl/architectuur-gids/weesperstaete/ (Arcam: "Doodskist in het centrum", the dark glass replaced by clear glass in ZZDP's 2005 renovation, done in consultation with Bodon's son, so the coffin is a little lighter now). Status: in use. Caveats: the nickname is in both sources. **Okay**; new place, or a Look for in the drafted Weesperflat / Diamantbeurs places.
title: Weesperstaete, "De Doodskist"
rank_text: **Okay**; new place, or a Look for in the drafted Weesperflat / Diamantbeurs places.

heading: Sweep 6: modern and contested / Weesperbuurt/Plantage
text: **CE-26. Professor Tulpplein: a professor who never was, and the houses on a sinking bastion.** Pin 52.360050, 4.906132 (Professor Tulpstraat 10, the even side; the square in front of the Amstel Hotel). The council named the square on 29 September 1875 after Nicolaes Tulp, Rembrandt's anatomy lecturer, who was called "professor" but never held a chair: he taught the surgeons' guild. The houses of the Professor Tulpstraat were built in 1875 on top of the demolished bastion Oosterblokhuis and in the 20th century began to subside; plans to pull them down met fierce resistance from the neighbourhood and Stadsherstel saved most of them. At no. 4 on the square the Amstel Hotel's livery stable grew into a diamond-trading building that drew diamond dealers to the street (municipal monument 2002, also as Jewish heritage). Lead: https://nl.wikipedia.org/wiki/Professor_Tulpplein ; second needed (Stadsherstel project page or the monument register for Prof. Tulpplein 4). Status: in place. Caveats: the Amstel Hotel (plantage-2) holds the square's no. 1; rename/myth item, light on things to see beyond the street. **Okay**; new place.
title: Professor Tulpplein: a professor who never was, and the houses on a sinking bastion

heading: Sweep 6: modern and contested / Weesperbuurt/Plantage
text: **CE-11. Weesperstraat, the Jewish quarter's high street turned city motorway.** Pin 52.363900, 4.906000 (Weesperstraat at the Nieuwe Prinsengracht, by Uytenhaak's block; check: Location). The narrow "Wazepergas" of the Jewish quarter (Vroom & Dreesmann opened their first shop at no. 70 in 1887) was emptied by the deportations and stripped for firewood in the hunger winter; the 1953 reconstruction plan made it a four-lane road from the IJ tunnel to the Wibautstraat, the remaining houses were pulled down in the late 1950s and early 1960s and the street was shut to all traffic 1961-65. The east side got the big 1960s blocks (Hertzberger's student flat, Arthur Staal's Metropool, now the Zoku hotel); the west side stayed bare while the first metro line was sunk in concrete caissons built on the surface (1970-77, with protests in 1975), and was rebuilt only in the 1980s and 1990s, most visibly by Rudy Uytenhaak (1992), whose concrete screens carry the rhythm of canal houses up to the traffic. Plans to narrow the road stalled for years; by 2022 part of it was cut back to two lanes. Look for the 1990s "miniature town" fronts, the canal bridges named after Jewish Amsterdammers, the Namenmonument on the green strip. Lead: https://nl.wikipedia.org/wiki/Weesperstraat_(Amsterdam) ; second: https://arcam.nl/architectuur-gids/woningen-weesperstraat/ (Arcam guide). Status: in use; narrowing ongoing. Caveats: neighbours DE-28 (embroidered wall), DE-23, AE-33 and the drafted Weesperflat; this item is pitched on the cut itself. **Nice**; new place.
title: Weesperstraat, the Jewish quarter's high street turned city motorway

heading: Sweep 6: modern and contested / Weesperbuurt/Plantage
text: **CE-12. Steven Holl's sponge on the Sarphatistraat.** Pin 52.362450, 4.916700 (the pavilion on the Singelgracht side of Sarphatistraat 410; check: Location). In 2000 the American architect Steven Holl turned the 19th-century state medicine store (Rijksmagazijn van Geneesmiddelen) into the head office of housing association Het Oosten (now Stadgenoot), keeping its columns, timber trusses and cast-iron stairs, and added a pavilion on the water wrapped in perforated copper plate over a second perforated skin, with bright colour fields that flicker through the holes ("Patterns in a chromatic field"); at night it glows. One of the few buildings in Amsterdam by a foreign star architect of that generation, and best seen from across the Singelgracht. Lead: https://arcam.nl/architectuur-gids/campus-stadgenoot/ ; second: https://www.archdaily.com/201033/flashback-sarphatistraat-offices-steven-holl-architects . Status: in use (Stadgenoot campus, extended 2012 with "The Bell", Sarphatistraat 370). Caveats: offices, outside only. **Nice**; new place.
title: Steven Holl's sponge on the Sarphatistraat

heading: Sweep 6: modern and contested / Weesperbuurt/Plantage
text: **CE-13. Roeterseiland: the bridge building with its legs cut off.** Pin 52.363300, 4.911100 (gebouw B/C over the Nieuwe Achtergracht, from the Theodore Limpergbrug; check: Location). The university's 1960s science buildings on the old tram depot were remade from 2012 for the social sciences, economics and law: AHMM removed the four lowest floors of the building that bridged the Nieuwe Achtergracht, so that the canal became the open spine of the campus instead of a culvert, with the restaurant hanging just above the water; on its roof, the highest of the complex at 46 m, the UvA planned a silent vertical wind turbine (2021). CREA, the students' cultural centre, kept the front of the 1845 diamond factory with a new inner wall against the music. Neighbours won the courtyard "Petit Versailles" from a planned teaching block (DE-31). Lead: https://arcam.nl/architectuur-gids/uva-roeterseiland/ ; second: https://nl.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roeterseiland and https://www.buurtorganisatie1018.nl/nieuws-uit-1018/2021/11/2/windturbine-op-dak-uva . Status: in use; wind turbine not confirmed as built (check). Caveats: all buildings have letters A to M, but there is no F (Wikipedia, a nice line). **Okay**; new place, or merge DE-31 into it.
title: Roeterseiland: the bridge building with its legs cut off
rank_text: **Okay**; new place, or merge DE-31 into it.

heading: Sweep 6: modern and contested / Grachtengordel-Zuid
text: **CE-21. Thorbecke, who turned his back on his square and nearly lost it to the fair.** Pin 52.365058, 4.895853 (the statue at the head of the Thorbeckeplein, OSM). Unveiled on 18 May 1876, the day after the old Reguliersplein was renamed for the statesman, the statue by Ferdinand Leenhoff looks not over "his" square but down the Reguliersgracht. Amsterdammers suspected the city of planting Rembrandt and Thorbecke on the old fairground squares on purpose to block the September kermis, which was banned that very year; in the Kermisoproer of 11 September 1876 some 300 rioters went for the mayor's windows, and their song demanded "Thorbecke van het plein". The square, a strip of nightclubs with racy shows until the 1970s, was redone in 2010-11 (statue away nine months, lent for 14 weeks to the art centre Stroom in The Hague), its bandstand went to Artis and its Sunday Modern Art Market of 25 years moved to the Rembrandtplein. Thorbecke is said to have disliked Amsterdam. Lead: https://nl.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thorbeckeplein ; second: https://nl.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kermisoproer . Status: in place; listed (rijksmonument, with its railing). Caveats: next to the A-list Rembrandtplein but a separate square; statue is theme A ground too; "disliked Amsterdam" is trivia, tell it as hearsay. **Amazing** (a start-here pick: a statue you can stand at, a riot, a renaming and a stubborn gaze); new place.
title: Thorbecke, who turned his back on his square and nearly lost it to the fair
rank_text: **Amazing** (a start-here pick: a statue you can stand at, a riot, a renaming and a stubborn gaze); new place.

heading: Sweep 6: modern and contested / Oostelijke Eilanden/Kadijken
text: **CE-14. The marechaussee's black box with 1,750 windows.** Pin 52.373600, 4.917000 (north end of the Marineterrein by the Kattenburgerstraat; check: Location). Wansleben Architekten's office for the Royal Military Police (2008) copies the exact footprint and the fortress-like courtyard of the Admiralty's sea store of 1656 (now the Scheepvaartmuseum) at the other end of the same terrain, but clad in black stone with 1,750 identical sunken windows that hide the floors and keep the staff unseen from outside; a corridor between façade and offices guarantees anonymity, while the inner court is bright with glass and coloured wooden shutters. Train passengers and cyclists off the Jan Schaeferbrug see it first. Lead: https://arcam.nl/architectuur-gids/marinekazerne-amsterdam/ ; second needed (Wansleben site). Same terrain, by the water opposite NEMO: two navy schools of 1962 raised on pilotis "by Le Corbusier's five points"; one of them (Gebouw 027E, SLA 2016) got wooden slats in the pattern of European flags over its big south windows for the Dutch EU presidency of 2016 (Arcam, https://arcam.nl/architectuur-gids/gebouw-027e-marineterrein/). Status: in use (military, closed). **Okay**; new place, or a Look for in "Marineterrein, the navy yard behind the wall" (with 027E as a second Look for).
title: The marechaussee's black box with 1,750 windows
rank_text: **Okay**; new place, or a Look for in "Marineterrein, the navy yard behind the wall" (with 027E as a second Look for).

heading: Sweep 6: modern and contested / Oostelijke Eilanden/Kadijken
text: **CE-04. Het Funen: sixteen blocks, sixteen architects, and a park that isn't one.** Pin 52.369400, 4.931000 (the central footpath of the Funenpark; check: Location). On the old Van Gend & Loos goods yard, empty and run down from the late 1970s, Frits van Dongen laid out 551 homes in sixteen free-standing blocks, each by a different office (NL Architects, Claus en Kaan, Dick van Gameren and others), in a car-free green where all paving is five-sided tiles of many sizes and greys. It was named in 2003 after the Danish island; despite the name it is a street, not a park. The archaeologists found the walls of bastion Zeeburg, now shown in Gabriel Lester's "Tussentijd" (AE-30). Amsterdammers voted the last block, "Verdana", the city's best new building of 2011, against the experts, and the scheme won the national Gouden Piramide the same year. Local voice: the fight next door: in March 2020 developer VORM wrapped the trees on the corner of the Panamalaan and Cruquiuskade in nets so birds could not nest and delay its "Fibonacci" tower, which the Funen residents opposed (1018, 25 March 2020; objections to the zoning plan ran to Jan 2019). Lead: https://nl.wikipedia.org/wiki/Funenpark ; second: https://arcam.nl/architectuur-gids/het-funen/ (Arcam: bastion Zeeburg, the last of the 26, sold for demolition in 1877; the L-shaped block with glass scales is the noise screen for the rest). Status: built 2000s, in use. **Nice**; new place (AE-30 as its Look for line).
title: Het Funen: sixteen blocks, sixteen architects, and a park that isn't one
rank_text: **Nice**; new place (AE-30 as its Look for line).

heading: Sweep 6: modern and contested / Oostelijke Eilanden/Kadijken
text: **CE-05. Mediamatic Biotoop, the art lab on the old city yard.** Pin 52.376617, 4.913154 (Dijksgracht 6). Mediamatic, a media-art foundation since 1983 (Mediamatic Magazine, the 1993 Doors of Perception conference, the "El HEMA" Arabic Hema of 2007), moved here in 2014 after Bugaboo bought the Van Gendthallen from under it, and turned the former municipal works yard into a "biotope": exhibition space in the Sluisdeurenloods, a bio lab, an aquaponics farm, allotments, a little harbour and a plant-based restaurant. The founders left in 2024 after forty years; a young team now runs it. Lead: https://nl.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mediamatic ; second: https://www.mediamatic.net/en/contact (open Mon to Fri 12:00 to 17:30, Sat 14:00 to 17:30; restaurant TestTafel Wed to Sat evenings, read 24 Nov 2026). Status: open (Nov 2026). Caveats: the Sluisdeurenloods is drafted in eilanden-1 ("Sluisdeurenloods, the wooden shed that moved for the IJ tunnel"): merge there or keep both and cross-refer; the 2020 "Serres Séparées" (diners in small greenhouses on the quay during the pandemic) is the hook the world knows: a second source is needed before using it. **Nice**; new place or merge into the Sluisdeurenloods.
title: Mediamatic Biotoop, the art lab on the old city yard
rank_text: **Nice**; new place or merge into the Sluisdeurenloods.

heading: Sweep 6: modern and contested / Oostelijke Eilanden/Kadijken
text: **CE-17. The navy's firing range, now a roof garden facing NEMO.** Pin 52.374000, 4.914450 (the former Schietbaan at the north-west tip of the Marineterrein; check: Location of the stair). A long, windowless concrete block where the navy did its shooting practice, for years left to graffiti writers, was reopened on 12 October 2023 with a new steel frame and a wide stair that is also a grandstand, leading to a roof garden with a view over the Oosterdok, NEMO and the sunset; a bread hatch of the Noord bakery Kometenbrood sits below. Everything is reused, because everything on the terrain is temporary: the steel came from an old cow shed in Brabant, the timber stood fifteen years in a Frisian sheet-pile wall. It also housed the city's first "Buitenbroedplaats" for young artists (May 2021). Local voice: the 1018 paper calls it a special place for the view and the sunset. Lead: https://www.buurtorganisatie1018.nl/nieuws-uit-1018/2023/8/28/de-schietbaan-op-het-marineterrein-is-omgevormd-tot-een-nieuwe-plek ; second: https://marineterrein.nl/experimenten/transformatie-schietbaan/ (read 24 Nov 2026). Status: open (Marineterrein site 2026). Caveats: temporary use, can change; pin approximate. **Nice**; new place.
title: The navy's firing range, now a roof garden facing NEMO

heading: Sweep 6: modern and contested / Oostelijke Eilanden/Kadijken
text: **CE-18. Wilhelmina Blombergplein: named for a woman the city thought was dead.** Pin 52.365287, 4.923156 (Wilhelmina Blombergplein 3, behind the Oranje-Nassau Kazerne). A square made in 1990 when the barracks site was turned into homes, named that year after Wilhelmina Blomberg (1908-1997), who fought for better housing in the Jordaan. The city does not name streets after living people; during the naming it simply did not know she was still alive, so she lived seven more years with a square of her own. Look for the "Stenen tapijt" (stone carpet) laid by Agnes van Genderen across the whole square, and two little elephants at the foot of the Oliphantsbrug over the Singelgracht (maker unknown). Lead: https://nl.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wilhelmina_Blombergplein ; second needed (the city's street-name register, straatnamen.amsterdam.nl, for the 1990 decision). Status: in place (Wikipedia photos). Caveats: the barracks are drafted ("Oranje-Nassau Kazerne, Napoleon's barracks where the Artis lions slept"): could be a Look for there. **Okay**; new place or Look for.
title: Wilhelmina Blombergplein: named for a woman the city thought was dead

heading: Sweep 6: modern and contested / Oostelijke Eilanden/Kadijken
text: **CE-19. Nieuwe-Hoofdhof, a hofje of the 1970s with an Aldo van Eyck sandbox.** Pin 52.370737, 4.917181 (Nieuwe-Hoofdhof 45; the sandbox in the inner square). Amsterdam has hofjes from the 14th century on; this one was made in the clearance of Kattenburg in the 1970s, when the old street plan was partly wiped out, and named only on 21 April 1993, after the bastion Nieuwe Hooft. A footpath runs through a gate on the Kattenburgerplein to the Kattenburgerkade. A relic of the first renewal years survives in it: a sandbox by Aldo van Eyck, who designed some 700 playgrounds for the city after the war, and a 1970 sculpture, the twin sister of Theo Niermeijer's "Het westen ontvangt en ontmoet 't oosten". Lead: https://nl.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nieuwe-Hoofdhof (sandbox photographed 2022) ; second needed (a Van Eyck playground inventory). Status: sandbox there in 2022. Caveats: the Kattenburg renewal and fake fronts are BE-23 and BE-24: group with them if preferred. **Okay**; new place or group with BE-23.
title: Nieuwe-Hoofdhof, a hofje of the 1970s with an Aldo van Eyck sandbox
rank_text: **Okay**; new place or group with BE-23.

heading: Sweep 7: curiosities, green corners and odd museums / De Weteringschans
text: **CE-06. Pipe Museum, the world's smokes in a 1670 canal house.** Pin 52.364126, 4.885348 (Prinsengracht 488). A private collection begun in 1969, shown on the Frederiksplein (1975-82), in Leiden (1982-95) and here since 1995; renamed from "Pijpenkabinet" in 2013. Over 30,000 objects in store and about 2,000 on show: pre-Columbian pipes, clay pipes dug up in Dutch soil, opium pipes, meerschaum carvings and the pipe makers' moulds, in period rooms; every visitor gets a personal welcome and tour. Lead: https://nl.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amsterdam_Pipe_Museum ; second: https://pipemuseum.nl/en/ (Mon to Sat 12:00 to 18:00, 15 euro, read 24 Nov 2026). Status: open (Nov 2026). Caveats: the old domain amsterdampipemuseum.nl no longer resolves (do not use); paid entry. **Nice**; new place.
title: Pipe Museum, the world's smokes in a 1670 canal house

heading: Sweep 7: curiosities, green corners and odd museums / De Weteringschans
text: **CE-07. Max Euwe Centrum, chess in the old remand prison.** Pin 52.362795, 4.883176 (Max Euweplein 26, since the move of 31 Dec 2023). A small museum of the only Dutch world chess champion (1935) and a library of about 11,000 chess books (a Ruy López of 1584 among them), set up after Euwe's death with mayor Ed van Thijn's help and since 13 December 1991 in the former Huis van Bewaring; about twenty volunteers; the city stopped its subsidy in 2016. Each summer, around 1 July, a chess festival takes over the square, where a giant board is set in the paving (check). Local voice: after 32 years the owner wanted the space back; the centre resisted, lost, and moved some 50 m to no. 26 in the same building, paid for by a donors' campaign (maxeuwe.nl, Dec 2023). Lead: https://nl.wikipedia.org/wiki/Max_Euwe_Centrum ; second: https://maxeuwe.nl/en/max-euwe-centre-mec-open-again/ (reopened Feb 2024; free entry, Tue to Sat 12:00 to 16:00, read 24 Nov 2026). Status: open (Nov 2026). Caveats: BE-08 tells the prison and Anne Frank; this item is pitched on the chess; giant board to confirm on site. **Nice**; new place, or group with BE-08.
title: Max Euwe Centrum, chess in the old remand prison
rank_text: **Nice**; new place, or group with BE-08.

heading: Sweep 7: curiosities, green corners and odd museums / De Weteringschans
text: **CE-08. De Nieuwe Schatkamer: the gold vault you can walk into.** Pin 52.359364, 4.900123 (Frederiksplein 61). After its rebuild De Nederlandsche Bank opened its basement, where the country's gold and banknotes were once stored, to anyone from March 2025: an exhibition on money and gold in the old vault ("kluis experience"), a lab for testing forged and damaged notes, the bank's money and art collections, debates; the garden and quay are open too. Lead: https://www.dnb.nl/de-nieuwe-schatkamer/ ; second: https://www.denieuweschatkamer.nl/ (current exhibition on the digital euro, June to Dec 2026). Status: open (Nov 2026). Caveats: opening hours for individual visitors to confirm. **Nice**; group with DE-44 (DNB garden) as one place: "De Nederlandsche Bank: garden, quay and gold vault open to all".
title: De Nieuwe Schatkamer: the gold vault you can walk into
rank_text: **Nice**; group with DE-44 (DNB garden) as one place: "De Nederlandsche Bank: garden, quay and gold vault open to all".

heading: Sweep 7: curiosities, green corners and odd museums / Weesperbuurt/Plantage
text: **CE-09. Sarphatistraat 66, the doll's house that stares back.** Pin 52.361241, 4.909193 (Sarphatistraat 66). A richly stuccoed neoclassical house of 1873-78 by J.H. Schmitz, built for diamond dealers who never lived in it, home to diamond workshops until the 1970s and a small hotel until about 2022; after a renovation it was for sale in 2024 for almost seven million euro, and behind the windows of the bel-étage dolls stand looking out at the street, which earned it the nicknames "poppenhuis" and "spookhuis". Lead: https://nl.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sarphatistraat_66 (photos June 2024) ; second needed. Status: dolls seen June 2024; no later evidence (check: Still there?). Caveats: private house, municipal monument; one source. **Okay**; new place.
title: Sarphatistraat 66, the doll's house that stares back

heading: Sweep 7: curiosities, green corners and odd museums / Weesperbuurt/Plantage
text: **CE-15. Artisplein: Artis for free, from a chair by the pond.** Pin 52.366469, 4.913261 (the "Watertafel" fountain on the Artisplein, corner Plantage Kerklaan / Plantage Middenlaan). In 2014 Artis pulled down its Geological Museum to open a public square (design Michael van Gessel) between the restored members' rooms (Ledenlokalen) and the Groote Museum: anyone may pull up a chair by the pond and watch the flamingos, and the long fountain at the park side runs along the "Hollandse Polder", an aviary that shows the meadow landscape before the city came, with what Arcam calls the largest collection of spoonbills in the world. A zoo that turned one corner into a city park without a ticket. Lead: https://arcam.nl/architectuur-gids/artisplein/ ; second: OSM (Watertafel, Hollandse Polder) and Artis's own site (to check opening hours of the square). Status: open (Arcam, page current 2026). Caveats: Artis is A-list; this is pitched on the free square beside it; the spoonbill claim is Arcam's alone. **Nice**; new place.
title: Artisplein: Artis for free, from a chair by the pond

heading: Sweep 7: curiosities, green corners and odd museums / Weesperbuurt/Plantage
text: **CE-22. Luther Museum in De Wittenberg, the Lutherans' old people's home.** Pin 52.365524, 4.908850 (Nieuwe Keizersgracht 570). A museum that opened on 22 June 2019 in the building the Evangelical Lutheran diaconate put up in 1772 as its home for old men and women and named after the town where Luther posted his theses; the regents' rooms, the corridor and the church hall are the main exhibits, with paintings (Breenbergh, Ruisdael), silver and furniture from the diaconate's collection. It tells a story most Amsterdammers never heard: in the 17th century about a fifth of the city was Lutheran, many of them German and Scandinavian immigrants. It runs concerts in the church hall and current exhibitions ("Vrij Denken", Luther and Erasmus, from 28 Oct 2026), and made a podcast on the churches and slavery (2021). Lead: https://luthermuseum.nl/en (read 24 Nov 2026) ; second: Buurtorganisatie 1018 news, "Luther Museum in De Wittenberg gaat op 22 juni open" (May 2019) and later concert notices (2019-2021). Status: open (Nov 2026; hours on the site, ticketed). Caveats: the 1772 building is a listed monument, check the drafts for a monument record of De Wittenberg; the Van Brants Rus hofje draft (plantage-1) already mentions Wittenberg's nurses. **Nice**; new place.
title: Luther Museum in De Wittenberg, the Lutherans' old people's home

heading: Sweep 7: curiosities, green corners and odd museums / Oostelijke Eilanden/Kadijken
text: **CE-20. The floating ball in the Oostenburgerpark, and the llamas.** Pin 52.368969, 4.925823 (the Kogelbron, OSM). After the 1980s clearance of Oostenburg the left-over open space became a park (named 18 October 1989), and the city ordered a "Kugelbrunnen" from the German artist Christian Tobin (then Christian Mayer): a red granite ball lying in a stone cup, lifted by a thin film of water so that it floats and a child can spin it by hand; placed about 1987, older sister of the one at the RAI. Since 2021 the park is also a stop on the islands' mosaic route (five mosaic sculptures, started by two residents); here it is a pair of llamas. From the park you look at the INIT building and the back of the VOC's East India warehouse. Lead: https://nl.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kogelbron_(Oostenburgerpark) ; second: https://nl.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oostenburgerpark and OSM. Status: llamas photographed May 2022; is the ball still floating? (check). **Okay**; new place.
title: The floating ball in the Oostenburgerpark, and the llamas

heading: Sweep 7: curiosities, green corners and odd museums / Oostelijke Eilanden/Kadijken
text: **CE-23. Plukbos, the food forest behind the Wittenburg blocks.** Pin 52.372253, 4.921629 (the garden on the inner terrain between Jacob Burggraafstraat, Grote Wittenburgerstraat, Tweede Wittenburgerdwarsstraat and the Kattenburgervaart; check: entrance). About 1,000 m2 of inner courtyard on Wittenburg turned by neighbours into a small urban food forest with fruit trees, herbs, a greenhouse and vegetable beds, part of the "green carpet" of Centrum; it is open day and night "for quiet neighbours and passers-by" and you may pick a fruit or cut your own tea as you walk. A tuinclub for children after school, a garden day with lunch every first Sunday, compost for the street, and each winter a "Kerst-BnB", an asylum where potted Christmas trees spend the year. It came out of the Groenplan Oostelijke Eilanden (2018-19). Lead: https://plukbos.nl/ (agenda for Nov 2026) ; second: https://vanamsterdamsebodem.nl/stadshelden/plukbos/ and https://www.buurtorganisatie1018.nl/groen-oostelijke-eilanden . Status: active (agenda Nov 2026). Caveats: gardening times are fixed, but access is said to be always open (check on site). **Nice**; new place.
title: Plukbos, the food forest behind the Wittenburg blocks

heading: Sweep 7: curiosities, green corners and odd museums / Oostelijke Eilanden/Kadijken
text: **CE-24. Dijksgracht-Oost, the railway bank where a polecat stopped the bike path.** Pin 52.375700, 4.918000 (the overgrown bank between the Dijksgracht-Oost and the railway, between the Kattenburgerstraat and the Mariniersbrug; approximate). A strip of scrub along the tracks east of the station that residents have defended for a decade: in 2015 a petition to save the "groene oase" of the Dijksgracht, in 2022 a court case over the foraging ground of common pipistrelle bats (lost), after which ecologists still halted the clearing because birds were nesting; and in February 2026 polecat droppings turned up in one of the marten boxes, so the city had to stop building its cycle path until September: the polecat is on the red list with extra protection in Noord-Holland. The city now promises brush piles and shrubs along the whole path. A curious place to look for city wildlife at dusk, between NEMO, the trains and the new towers. Lead: https://www.buurtorganisatie1018.nl/nieuws-uit-1018/2026/3/31/fietspad-dijksgracht-oost-bunzing-vertraagt-aanleg-en-omwonenden-verzetten-zich-tegen-het-nieuwe-kruispunt ; second: https://www.buurtorganisatie1018.nl/nieuws-uit-1018/2022/5/11/dijksgracht-oost-broedende-vogels-en-foerageeergebied-van-de-dwergvleermuis-voorlopig-veiliggesteld (both 1018: a second, independent source still needed, e.g. the city's project page or the Omgevingsdienst exemption). Status: works paused until Sept 2026, path not before early 2027. Caveats: a construction zone; nothing to "see" by day but the bank; pin approximate; one source family. **Okay**; new place.
title: Dijksgracht-Oost, the railway bank where a polecat stopped the bike path

heading: Sweep 7: curiosities, green corners and odd museums / Grachtengordel-Zuid
text: **CE-16. Hans Brinker Budget Hotel, proudly the worst.** Pin 52.363679, 4.888055 (Kerkstraat 136). A hostel since 1970 in a former Catholic convent (the Sint-Piusgesticht; Cuypers's chapel of 1868 is gone), with 507 bunk beds, famous far beyond Amsterdam for its anti-advertising by Erik Kessels of KesselsKramer: before-and-after photos of guests leaving in worse shape than they came, and boasts of a view of a brick wall. Arcam lists it in its architecture guide with the hotel's own claim that guests come for the atmosphere, not the architecture. Lead: https://arcam.nl/architectuur-gids/hans-brinker-budget-hotel/ ; second needed (KesselsKramer or an advertising history source). Status: open (Arcam 2026). Caveats: a commercial hostel; the story is the advertising. **Okay**; new place.
title: Hans Brinker Budget Hotel, proudly the worst

heading: Sweep 7: curiosities, green corners and odd museums / Grachtengordel-Zuid
text: **CE-10. The krullen of the canal belt: Amsterdam's open-air urinals.** Pin 52.364351, 4.889736 (the krul at Keizersgracht / Nieuwe Spiegelgracht). The curled iron urinal was the city works department's answer of about 1870 (an inventor had proposed hollow advertising columns); the first double krul went up in 1877 at the Paleis voor Volksvlijt on the Frederiksplein. The see-through top let policemen check that only one man was inside, because the krullen were also cruising spots (some 40 still used that way in 1980). In the 1960s the city wanted them gone; they stayed partly to keep drunk men from falling into the canals. In 2017 35 were left; the register lists 39 in 2026, eight of them in this zone (Amstelveld, Utrechtsestraat, Keizersgracht/Nieuwe Spiegelgracht, Lijnbaansgracht 282, Nieuwe Keizersgracht/Weesperstraat, Nieuwe Achtergracht/Roetersstraat, Plantage Kerklaan by Artis, Kadijksplein). Women still have nothing comparable, which became the "plasrecht" fight after a woman was fined in 2015. Their modern cousins are nearby: eight urilifts that rise out of the pavement in the evening and sink back in the morning, and two planted "Green Pee" urinals by the Rembrandtplein. Lead: https://nl.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plaskrul ; second: https://maps.amsterdam.nl/openbare_toiletten/ (register, 24 Nov 2026). Status: in use. Caveats: the plasrecht case needs its own source before use; a sensitive history told plainly. **Amazing** (start here: the most Amsterdam piece of street furniture, with a hidden history); new place (one pin for all; the other krullen as Look for lines).
title: The krullen of the canal belt: Amsterdam's open-air urinals
rank_text: **Amazing** (start here: the most Amsterdam piece of street furniture, with a hidden history); new place (one pin for all; the other krullen as Look for lines).

heading: Sweep 6: modern and contested / Grachtengordel-West
text: **CW-01 De Groote Keijser: the squat that became a fortress.** Pin 52.372148, 4.884450, Keizersgracht 242 to 252 (listed canal houses). The empty offices of an electrical wholesaler were squatted on 1 November 1978 and the squatters turned six canal houses into a fortress: barricades, a roof watch, stocks of fireworks and firebombs. A court ordered eviction in October 1979, but the mayor refused to send in the police; squatters occupied the council chamber in December 1979 and from January 1980 ran a pirate station, Radio de Groote Keijser (later Radio de Vrije Keyser, which still exists). The city bought the block in November 1980 for 1.8 million guilders, and the purchase split the movement into those who negotiated and those who wanted to fight on. Now social housing for groups; number 246 is "Het Suijkervat", a sugar bakery of 1666. Local voice: the radio name lives on in the Vrije Keyser, still broadcasting as the movement's own station. Lead: https://nl.wikipedia.org/wiki/Groote_Keijser . Second: https://nl.wikipedia.org/wiki/Krakersrellen and https://vrijekeyser.nl . Status: housing, facade unchanged (Wikipedia, checked 2026-11-24). Caveats: private housing, seen from the quay; no plaque known. Rank **Amazing**. New place.
title: De Groote Keijser: the squat that became a fortress

heading: Sweep 6: modern and contested / Grachtengordel-West
text: **CW-02 De Vogelstruys: three evictions and a riot.** Pin 52.369679, 4.887194, Herengracht 329 (through to Singel 370). The squat in this canal-belt block was evicted three times; the third eviction on 8 September 1980 ended in some of the heaviest street fighting of that year. It was squatted again in October 1992. Lead: IISG Staatsarchief dossier SAVRZ015 (read via Wayback, https://web.archive.org/web/2020/https://staatsarchief.nl/ ). Second: https://nl.wikipedia.org/wiki/Krakersrellen (list of riots). Status: unknown use 2026, not checked on site. Caveats: private building; dates rest on the IISG dossier, a second source for the 1992 squat is needed; Huidenstraat 19 appears in the same dossier. Rank **Okay**. New place, or a Look for line in CW-01 ("the other big canal squat").
title: De Vogelstruys: three evictions and a riot
rank_text: Rank **Okay**. New place, or a Look for line in CW-01 ("the other big canal squat").

heading: Sweep 6: modern and contested / Haarlemmerbuurt
text: **CW-03 Haarlemmer Houttuinen: the motorway that stopped at a bridge.** Pin 52.381855, 4.890108, brug 95 over the Korte Prinsengracht. A 1931 plan for a four-lane through road from the Haarlemmerweg to the Weesperstraat and Gooiseweg cost the old workers' quarter here its houses from 1969; the road opened in 1973 but was never continued, because the Nieuwmarkt fight killed the rest of the route. Brug 95 (1970 to 1972) is the high car bridge built for it and is due to be replaced by a low bridge (plan of 2018, works "in the first half of the 2020s"). Tram rails laid in 1985 were never used and wore out unridden. Hertzberger's housing (1970s) fills the gap between the road and the Haarlemmerdijk. A 1980 photo shows the fence here painted "Geen woning, geen kroning". Local voice: the Wijkkrant calls the street behind it "een weg van niks naar nergens" (see DW-13). Lead: https://nl.wikipedia.org/wiki/Haarlemmer_Houttuinen . Second: https://nl.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brug_95 . Status: bridge still standing (AW-13 mural 2023 on it, active 2026); replacement date unknown, the city project page is gone (404, 2026-11-24). Caveats: check the replacement plan before writing. Rank **Nice**. Group with AW-13 (same underpass): the road fight is the place's story, the mural its look-for; DW-13 covers the Nieuwe Houttuinen side.
title: Haarlemmer Houttuinen: the motorway that stopped at a bridge
rank_text: Rank **Nice**. Group with AW-13 (same underpass): the road fight is the place's story, the mural its look-for; DW-13 covers the Nieuwe Houttuinen side.

heading: Sweep 7: curiosities, green and odd museums / Grachtengordel-West
text: **CW-04 The double krul at the Westermarkt, and the zone's last krullen.** Pin 52.374496, 4.884908, Westermarkt by the Prinsengracht, next to the Homomonument. The green cast-iron curl urinal is an Amsterdam invention of about 1870; the standard model (1916) was see-through on purpose so a policeman could tell whether more than one man stood inside, which made krullen cruising spots (about forty were used that way around 1980). When the city wanted them gone in the 1960s the gay movement fought for them; on 24 January 1970 Dolle Mina tied krullen shut with pink ribbons to demand "plasrecht" for women; in 2017 the "Zeikwijf" protest followed a woman's fine for peeing in an alley. The city now has 39, all restored in 2008, and lets them die out: a broken krul is not replaced. The Noordermarkt krul (over a hundred years old) went to the Openluchtmuseum in Arnhem in February 2022. In this zone the city data lists seven: Westermarkt (double), Brouwersgracht by the Singel lock 52.378983, 4.894051, Herenmarkt 52.379413, 4.891667, Haarlemmerplein 52.384333, 4.883677, Lindengracht 52.379636, 4.880664, Marnixplantsoen 52.381291, 4.880182, and Marnixstraat by the Elandsgracht opposite police headquarters 52.368764, 4.877074. Local voice: in August 2026 the city tried women's urinals ("een soort krul met 2 toiletten") in the Elandsstraat and on the Elandsgracht during Pride (oudestadt.nl, 2026-08-12). Lead: https://nl.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plaskrul . Second: city toilets data https://maps.amsterdam.nl/open_geodata/geojson_lnglat.php?KAARTLAAG=OPENBARE_TOILETTEN&THEMA=openbare_toiletten (2026). Status: all seven in the city data, November 2026. Caveats: in use, smells; the Johnny Jordaanplein krul named in DW is not in the city list (probably gone). Rank **Nice**. New place (one pin, the others as a Look for list).
title: The double krul at the Westermarkt, and the zone's last krullen
rank_text: Rank **Nice**. New place (one pin, the others as a Look for list).

heading: Sweep 7: curiosities, green and odd museums / Grachtengordel-West
text: **CW-05 De Poezenboot.** Pin 52.378144, 4.893079, Singel 38G (houseboat in front of Singel 40). In 1966 a woman living on the Herengracht took in a cat and her kittens found under a tree opposite her house; by 1968 the cats had a barge, by 1971 a second, and in 1979 a purpose-built ark. It became a foundation in 1987 and is still a working shelter for strays you can visit. The stadsdeel forced the second boat away on 20 March 2006 after an eighteen-month fight; a new hull came in 2023 through crowdfunding. Local voice: the boat's own history quotes the official line in the fight as "katten zijn niet water gebonden, weg ermee!". Lead: https://www.depoezenboot.nl (history page). Second: https://nl.wikipedia.org/wiki/De_Poezenboot_(Amsterdam) . Status: open Tuesday, Friday and Saturday 13:00 to 15:00 without booking; closed 25 December 2026 to 2 January 2027 (site, read 2026-11-24). Caveats: on Atlas Obscura and in some guides, so second tier; donation asked. Rank **Nice**. New place.
title: De Poezenboot

heading: Sweep 7: curiosities, green and odd museums / Grachtengordel-West
text: **CW-06 The Fault in Our Stars bench, Leidsegracht.** Pin 52.367454, 4.886210, Leidsegracht by number 4, at the Herengracht. A plain city bench by the water became a pilgrimage spot after the film of John Green's novel (2014) put its lovers on it; young readers come to sit and cry ("I cried a week", overheard by the Binnenkrant). The bench was stolen, and the replacement draws the same visitors. Local voice: Buurtkrant Zeven, in a piece written as a neighbourhood bench, calls it "wereldberoemd" and the only famous one, "ik ben alleen in de buurt geliefd" (Zeven 151, 2024). Lead: Binnenkrant 67 (De Binnenkrant archive). Second: Zeven 151 (2024), citing Het Parool of 30 July 2024. Status: replacement bench, OSM 2026; not seen on site. Caveats: tourist-fan spot, thin on history; the theft date needs Parool. Rank **Okay**. New place.
title: The Fault in Our Stars bench, Leidsegracht

heading: Sweep 7: curiosities, green and odd museums / Jordaan
text: **CW-07 Theo Thijssen Museum.** Pin 52.375538, 4.882737, Eerste Leliedwarsstraat 16. The birthplace of the teacher, writer, union man and politician Theo Thijssen (1879 to 1943, "Kees de jongen") was due to be pulled down for new housing; after a fuss the house was rebuilt in its old form (1991 to 1995) with a small museum inside, run by a foundation since 1987. Exhibitions on school and the Jordaan of about 1890, and walks. Local voice: the Wijkkrant of 2026 reports it closed from 20 July to 2 September for its first big refit in thirty years, back with new shows, a youth trail and an audio tour of the Jordaan, plus a public programme every last Sunday of the month. Lead: https://nl.wikipedia.org/wiki/Theo_Thijssen_Museum . Second: Wijkkrant Jordaan & Gouden Reael 2026 (00000224/00000226, wcjordaan.nl). Status: open after refit, autumn 2026. Caveats: small, limited hours. Rank **Nice**. New place.
title: Theo Thijssen Museum

heading: Sweep 7: curiosities, green and odd museums / Jordaan
text: **CW-08 Noordermarkt: the markets and the fight against "vertrutting".** Pin 52.379368, 4.886774, Noordermarkt. A market square since 1616 (the Prinsenmarkt); the Monday morning market and, since 1987, the Saturday organic farmers' market with second-hand stalls. The Noordermarktfeest (1977 to 1987) began as a protest against gentrification; in 2009 regulars of café Finch ran the "Ai! Amsterdam" protest against the square's "vertrutting", and Finch, Proust and Bordewijk all closed in 2018. The square's century-old krul went to the Openluchtmuseum in Arnhem in 2022 (CW-04). The Westerstraat Monday "lapjesmarkt" (150 stalls of fabric and clothes, 52.378517, 4.884078) belongs to the same Monday. Local voice: "vertrutting" is the residents' word for what happened to the square. Lead: https://nl.wikipedia.org/wiki/Noordermarkt . Second: Amsterdamian, "Noordermarkt: Amsterdam's Beloved Organic Market" (2026-01-23). Status: both markets running 2026. Caveats: the Noorderkerk draft already names the markets as a Look for line. Rank **Nice**. Group with DW-05 (Noordermarkt small things) or new place on the market.
title: Noordermarkt: the markets and the fight against "vertrutting"
rank_text: Rank **Nice**. Group with DW-05 (Noordermarkt small things) or new place on the market.

heading: Sweep 7: curiosities, green and odd museums / Jordaan
text: **CW-09 Lindengracht: the filled canal, its market and the eel riot.** Pin 52.380038, 4.883459, Lindengracht (Saturday Lindenmarkt). The canal was filled in 1895 and became a market street in 1910; plans to dig canals open again have met resistance. Here on 25 July 1886 police broke up the "paling trekken", a banned game of pulling a live eel strung over the canal; the Palingoproer that followed left 26 dead, and the first death of the Jordaanoproer of July 1934 also fell on the Lindengracht. Today the Saturday Lindenmarkt fills the street. Lead: https://nl.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palingoproer . Second: https://nl.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lindengracht . Status: market every Saturday, 2026. Caveats: exact spot of the eel rope (by the Zaterdagse brug, gone with the canal) is approximate; no draft has the riot. Rank **Nice**. New place (check with BW: sweep 4 may want the riot).
title: Lindengracht: the filled canal, its market and the eel riot
rank_text: Rank **Nice**. New place (check with BW: sweep 4 may want the riot).

heading: Sweep 7: curiosities, green and odd museums / Haarlemmerbuurt
text: **CW-10 Westerdokseiland: the rail yard's wild flowers and the lost IJ view.** Pin 52.383948, 4.892674, Westerdoksdijk 51. An island made in 1832, a rail yard from the 1920s where over 150 wild plant species grew, seeded from the colonial trade sheds. The housing built in the 2000s ignored the old sightlines, and the Prinsengracht lost its view of the IJ; the later IJDock was built with notches to keep views open. Lead: https://nl.wikipedia.org/wiki/Westerdokseiland . Second: https://nl.wikipedia.org/wiki/Westerdok . Status: built-up 2026. Caveats: little to see of the flora story; the Goedkoop draft (Westerdoksdijk 40) already cites the article. Rank **Okay**. New place, or a Look for line in the Goedkoop draft.
title: Westerdokseiland: the rail yard's wild flowers and the lost IJ view
rank_text: Rank **Okay**. New place, or a Look for line in the Goedkoop draft.

heading: Burgwallen-Oude Zijde
text: **DC-01. "GOD ROEPT U / JESUS LOVES YOU", the neon over the station square.** Pin 52.376544, 4.899285; Prins Hendrikkade 49-51. Blue neon letters on the corner house facing Centraal Station, the first thing many arrivals read. The building, once Hotel Karsten, houses an evangelical community, a bookshop and café Dwaze Zaken; d'Oude Binnenstad says the letters were switched on by the American astronaut James Irwin. Local voice: the neighbourhood calls a coffee at Dwaze Zaken "een bakkie doen bij Jezus" (d'Oude Binnenstad 2021-4); the paper also profiled the bookshop "onder het opschrift 'God roept u'" in December 2007. Lead: d'Oude Binnenstad 2021-4 and 2007-4 (oudebinnenstad.nl/kranten). Second source: none independent yet; the Irwin story must be confirmed or attributed. Status: lit per the 2020 and 2021 issues. Caveats: religious organisation, still in use; pin on the facade. Rank **Nice**. New place.
title: "GOD ROEPT U / JESUS LOVES YOU", the neon over the station square

heading: Burgwallen-Oude Zijde
text: **DC-02. The squatter in the gable of Vredenburgh.** Pin approx 52.375136, 4.900496; corner Oudezijds Voorburgwal and Vredenburgersteeg. A stone squatter with a mohawk swinging a hammer, by Joris Baudoin, unveiled 18 September 2011 in an empty niche of the top gable; the brief was to show something from the last thirty years of the house, which was squatted in 1979 and since then holds three living groups with dance, theatre and music studios; owner Ymere co-funded it. Local voice: the buurtkrant reported it as the house's own history put on its front. Lead: d'Oude Binnenstad 2011-3 (October 2011). Second source needed (Kunstwacht, Stadscuratorium). Status: no later evidence seen. Caveat: house number to fix on site (check: Location). Rank **Nice**. New place.
title: The squatter in the gable of Vredenburgh

heading: Burgwallen-Oude Zijde
text: **DC-03. Belle and the bronze breast, Oudekerksplein.** Pin 52.374179, 4.897406 (Belle; the breast is at 52.374024, 4.897906). Belle (Els Rijerse, 2007) was billed as the first statue of a prostitute, inscribed "Respect sex workers all over the world"; a few steps away a bronze hand groping a breast is set into the paving, left in 1993 by an anonymous maker ("De Onbekende Beeldhouwer"). Local voice: What's up with Amsterdam and RLD guides tell the anonymous-sculptor story; the Wallen residents' paper followed the window closures around the square. Lead: https://www.nhnieuws.nl/nieuws/26034 (31 March 2007); OSM artwork tags; What's up with Amsterdam. Caveat: beside A-list Oude Kerk, pitched on itself; the 1993 date and anonymity rest on blogs and OSM: check. Rank **Nice**. New place (group of two).
title: Belle and the bronze breast, Oudekerksplein

heading: Burgwallen-Oude Zijde
text: **DC-04. Trompettersteeg, the narrowest alley, and its hidden coat of arms.** Pin 52.373741, 4.897706. About 90 cm wide (d'Oude Binnenstad; others say 1 m). In 2021 the street artist Dopie painted the city arms so that they only come right from one spot (anamorphic); it was blacked out in anger and restored in July 2021. Local voice: residents fought tourists queuing in the alley, and the paper covered the mural as a reclaim. Lead: d'Oude Binnenstad 2021-1; https://www.nhnieuws.nl/nieuws/289333 (23 July 2021). Status: restored 2021; no later check. Rank **Nice**. New place.
title: Trompettersteeg, the narrowest alley, and its hidden coat of arms

heading: Burgwallen-Oude Zijde
text: **DC-05. "Wandelend naar de Nieuwmarkt", the brick walkers on the Varkenssluis.** Pin 52.371837, 4.895850 (bridge over the Oudezijds Voorburgwal between Dam and Chinatown). Brick figures with granite arms by Martie van der Loo (1986), walking toward the Nieuwmarkt; vandalised, remade and set back on 12 October 2011 as four Chinese walkers, with a lion dance; a fifth once sat on the Paulusbroedersluis. Local voice: d'Oude Binnenstad called the saga "de hoop of sloop-soap". Lead: d'Oude Binnenstad 2011-4 and 2007-2. Second source needed (Kunstwacht). Status: back 2011, no later check. Rank **Okay**. New place.
title: "Wandelend naar de Nieuwmarkt", the brick walkers on the Varkenssluis

heading: Burgwallen-Oude Zijde
text: **DC-06. Majoor Bosshardt on her bench.** Pin 52.375548, 4.900026; Oudezijds Voorburgwal by the Oudezijds Armsteeg. A bronze of the Salvation Army officer who worked among prostitutes and addicts on the Wallen sits on a bench; the bridge 211 over the Achterburgwal was named after her on 7 June 2013. Local voice: AT5 (2014) "Dronken toeristen onteren beeld Majoor Bosshardt"; d'Oude Binnenstad wrote that the bench "gaf gedoe" and a cloth goes over her at night; in 2018 the Bulldog put up its own tribute ("In gedachte bent u bij ons", AT5). Lead: https://www.at5.nl/artikelen/104696 ; nl.wikipedia Majoor Bosshardtbrug. Look for: the Majoor Bosshardthuis (Salvation Army museum) next door. Rank **Nice**. New place.
title: Majoor Bosshardt on her bench

heading: Burgwallen-Nieuwe Zijde
text: **DC-07. The stamp market, Argus and the gnome, Nieuwezijds Voorburgwal.** Pin 52.371145, 4.890439 (Postzegelmarkt, by no. 280). A stamp and coin market has gathered here on Wednesday and Saturday afternoons for about a century; in June 2022 the statue Argus (Saske van der Eerden) went up for the vanished newspaper quarter of this canal, near the Kabouter (Ruchama Noorda) with its apple tree, a nod to the Kabouters of 1970. Local voice: VVAB Binnenstad followed the square's redesign. Lead: VVAB Binnenstad; nl.wikipedia Argus (beeld) and Kabouterstandbeeld. Status: market and statues present per OSM 2026. Rank **Nice**. New place.
title: The stamp market, Argus and the gnome, Nieuwezijds Voorburgwal

heading: Burgwallen-Nieuwe Zijde
text: **DC-08. Wijdesteeg, the mosaic alley.** Pin 52.371575, 4.890035. From 2014 the artist Otto Kruijssen turned a dark alley used as a toilet into a mosaic street, first chased by enforcement four or five times a day, then tolerated. Local voice: "Vroeger vonden ze dit maar een smerig straatje" (AT5, 7 Nov 2014). Lead: https://www.at5.nl/artikelen/136873 . Status unknown after 2014 (check: Still there?). Rank **Okay**. New place.
title: Wijdesteeg, the mosaic alley

heading: Nieuwmarkt/Lastage
text: **DC-09. The plaque for the Nieuwmarkt children, De Flesseman.** Pin 52.371934, 4.900814; Nieuwmarkt 77. Four boys of the neighbourhood were shot by German soldiers in 1944-45, among them Izy and Bari Baars at the corner of the Recht Boomssloot, and Alex Evers on 12 April 1945, two minutes after curfew. Former residents met in 1994, the plaque went up on 23 April 1995, and the two neighbourhood schools (Sint Antoniusschool, De Witte Olifant) adopted it: every year children lay wreaths and release balloons. Local voice: OpNieuw reports the ceremony nearly every year. Lead: OpNieuw 2006-2, 2007-1, 2012-1; d'Oude Binnenstad 2015-1. Check the 4en5mei.nl record before drafting. Rank **Nice**. New place.
title: The plaque for the Nieuwmarkt children, De Flesseman

heading: Nieuwmarkt/Lastage
text: **DC-10. Vlooienburg, the plaque that took thirty years.** Pin approx 52.367646, 4.900165 (Stopera, Amstel 1; fix on the plaque). The island quarter under today's Stopera was the heart of Jewish Amsterdam; it was emptied by deportation, decayed and was cleared for the city hall and opera. A memorial plaque for its murdered residents was unveiled in November 2022 after almost thirty years of asking; since June 2026 a maquette and finds are on show inside the Stopera. Local voice: initiator Anita Mizsahi, "het kan toch niet dat hier zomaar die Stopera op gezet i[s]" (NH). Lead: https://www.nhnieuws.nl/nieuws/311053 ; https://www.nhnieuws.nl/nieuws/360894 ; nl.wikipedia Vlooienburg; OpNieuw 2022-3 (invitation), 2026-3. Caveat: an OpNieuw letter (2023-1) dates the monument 15 November 2023, which must be a slip for 2022 (the issue is of March 2023). Rank **Nice**. New place.
title: Vlooienburg, the plaque that took thirty years

heading: Nieuwmarkt/Lastage
text: **DC-11. Spinoza at the Stopera.** Pin 52.367940, 4.899201; Zwanenburgwal. Nicolas Dings' statue of the philosopher, who was born on Vlooienburg, unveiled 24 November 2008, quoting "Het doel van de staat is de vrijheid". Local voice: OpNieuw 2008-4 and its 2018 series "Spinoza heel actueel" with a neighbourhood Spinoza expert. Lead: https://www.at5.nl/artikelen/11341 ; OpNieuw 2008-4. Rank **Nice**. New place (could merge with DC-10 if the user wants one Vlooienburg pin).
title: Spinoza at the Stopera
rank_text: Rank **Nice**. New place (could merge with DC-10 if the user wants one Vlooienburg pin).

heading: Nieuwmarkt/Lastage
text: **DC-12. The Armenian genocide stone, Krom Boomssloot.** Pin 52.371530, 4.902078; Krom Boomssloot 22. A carved cross with Armenian and Dutch text, unveiled 21 April 2018 on the front of the Armenian Apostolic church and blessed by the archbishop; about 250 people came, and it is now the place of the yearly 24 April commemoration. Local voice: "Het maakt me blij en verdrietig tegelijk" (a parishioner, OpNieuw 2018-2). The bridge in front is the Armeensebrug. Lead: OpNieuw 2018-2. Second source needed (4en5mei / church site). Rank **Okay**. New place.
title: The Armenian genocide stone, Krom Boomssloot

heading: Nieuwmarkt/Lastage
text: **DC-13. Uilenburg: the Jewish bathhouse and the teacher's house.** Pin approx 52.370682, 4.905758; Nieuwe Uilenburgerstraat 29-31. The former Jewish bathhouse held an emotional 4 May commemoration in 2019 ("Hier heeft mijn moeder gelopen", AT5); next to it the teacher's house of the Sophie Rosenthal nursery school (1887), a municipal monument, is wanted by grid operator Liander for a substation. Local voice: VVAB news 431 (2023) and 452 (2024) against the plan. Lead: https://www.at5.nl/artikelen/193782 ; VVAB news 431, 452. Outlook: Under threat. Caveat: pins and house numbers to fix. Rank **Okay**. New place.
title: Uilenburg: the Jewish bathhouse and the teacher's house

heading: Burgwallen-Oude Zijde
text: **DC-14. Bureau Warmoesstraat, the police station of Baantjer.** Pin 52.375511, 4.898238; Warmoesstraat 48. From 1903 to 2000 the station of the Wallen, notorious for corruption stories and the model for the TV series Baantjer (Appie Baantjer worked here); it closed after a homeless man died after being put out on the pavement. A small plaque went up on 26 October 2025 on the sandwich shop now in the building. Local voice: crime reporter Cees Koring, "Je vraagt ... wat hier zat en dan worden de schouders opgehaald" (NH). Lead: https://www.nhnieuws.nl/nieuws/353682 ; nl.wikipedia Warmoesstraat (Amsterdam). Rank **Okay**. New place.
title: Bureau Warmoesstraat, the police station of Baantjer

heading: Burgwallen-Nieuwe Zijde
text: **DC-15. The Dam shooting of 7 May 1945.** Pin 52.373393, 4.892800. On 7 May 1945, while the Dam celebrated liberation, German soldiers fired from the balcony of De Groote Club on the corner of the Kalverstraat: at least 32 dead. On 7 May 2016 31 name stones were unveiled in the square, a 32nd followed a year later; the older plaque is in the wall (52.372620, 4.891944). Lead: https://www.nhnieuws.nl/nieuws/184667 ; nl.wikipedia Schietpartij op de Dam op 7 mei 1945. Caveat: the Dam is A-list; this is pitched on itself. Rank **Nice**. New place.
title: The Dam shooting of 7 May 1945

heading: Burgwallen-Oude Zijde
text: **DC-16. Bet van Beeren, 't Mandje and Hartjesdag on the Zeedijk.** Pin 52.374815, 4.900983; Zeedijk 63. 't Mandje, Bet van Beeren's bar, is counted the oldest gay and lesbian bar of the city and reopened after 25 years shut (opening year and closure dates to confirm); in 2017 the Stormsteeg bridge (210) was named after her, and every third Monday of August the Zeedijk holds Hartjesdag, a drag and dressing-up street party revived here in 1997. Local voice: AT5 "Koningin van de Zeedijk krijgt eigen brug"; landlord Martin Vermaak on Hartjesdag, "Het is vooral een hoop lol" (AT5 2023, after five rainbow flags were wrecked on the street). Lead: nl.wikipedia Bet van Beerenbrug and Hartjesdag; https://www.at5.nl/artikelen/222025 ; https://www.nhnieuws.nl/nieuws/306298 (2022). Caveat: a café; see "Food and drink, borderline". Rank **Amazing**. New place.
title: Bet van Beeren, 't Mandje and Hartjesdag on the Zeedijk

heading: Burgwallen-Oude Zijde
text: **DC-17. Chet Baker's window, Hotel Prins Hendrik.** Pin 52.376525, 4.899666; Prins Hendrikkade 53-55. The trumpeter fell from a window of the hotel on 13 May 1988 and died on the stone post below. Fans first put up an illegal pole with a trumpet; the bronze plaque followed on 13 May 1999, and every night of 12 to 13 May a wake is held. Local voice: d'Oude Binnenstad 2013-1. Lead: nl.wikipedia Chet Baker (gives no. 55); d'Oude Binnenstad 2013-1; OSM plaque. Rank **Nice**. New place (neighbour of DC-01).
title: Chet Baker's window, Hotel Prins Hendrik

heading: Burgwallen-Oude Zijde
text: **DC-18. Koestraat, "Ons Dorp", the street with its own mayor.** Pin 52.372125, 4.898268; Koestraat. The residents of this short street hold a street party in the back garden where Sweelinck lived from 1590 to 1621 and install a street mayor with a chain of office ("bijzonder detail is de aan-uitknop"). At no. 5 a memorial stone of 1912 (restored 2004) marks Jan van der Heyden, inventor of the fire hose and street lighting. Local voice: d'Oude Binnenstad 2017-3 ("Koestraat, Ons Dorp"); 2007-2. Lead: d'Oude Binnenstad; VVAB Binnenstad 210. Caveat: the mayor tradition is from one 2017 report; check whether it continues. Rank **Nice**. New place.
title: Koestraat, "Ons Dorp", the street with its own mayor

heading: Burgwallen-Oude Zijde
text: **DC-19. Walenpleintje, the square behind the gate.** Pin 52.371230, 4.897710 (the Walenpoortje). A hidden court behind a gate off the Oudezijds Achterburgwal, by the Walloon church; it only got its name in 1978. Local voice: d'Oude Binnenstad 2016-4. Lead: d'Oude Binnenstad; Wanderlustingk; Amsterdam Sights. Visiting: open by day. Rank **Okay**. New place.
title: Walenpleintje, the square behind the gate

heading: Burgwallen-Oude Zijde
text: **DC-20. Oost-Indisch Huis and the dismantled VOC room.** Pin 52.370898, 4.898007; Oude Hoogstraat 24 / Kloveniersburgwal 48. The VOC's headquarters, now the UvA; the courtyard is open by day. The university took apart the VOC room (Bewindhebberszaal) without a permit and the VVAB filed an enforcement request; Folia explains why the neighbour is called the Bushuis. Local voice: VVAB news 707 (2026). Lead: nl.wikipedia Oost-Indisch Huis (Amsterdam); VVAB news 707. Caveat: second-tier sight, pitch on the contest. Rank **Nice**. New place.
title: Oost-Indisch Huis and the dismantled VOC room

heading: Burgwallen-Oude Zijde
text: **DC-21. Oudemanhuispoort, the booksellers' arcade.** Pin 52.369364, 4.895584 (Oudezijds Achterburgwal entrance). Built 1601 as an old people's home from a lottery; the shops in the passage came with a rebuild in the 18th century, sold jewels and silver first, lost trade when it became a cholera house in the 1830s, and have held booksellers for more than a century. In the garden the UvA unveiled (30 September, year to confirm from the UvA page) a memorial with 254 students and 28 staff who died in the war. Local voice: Folia "UvA-geheimen" (2020) and November 2026 on the booksellers' future. Lead: Folia; nl.wikipedia Oudemanhuispoort; UvA news. Rank **Nice**. New place.
title: Oudemanhuispoort, the booksellers' arcade

heading: Burgwallen-Oude Zijde
text: **DC-22. Two smallest houses: Oude Hoogstraat 22 and the Trips' coachman.** Pin 52.371220, 4.897664 (Oude Hoogstraat 22; Kloveniersburgwal 26 at 52.371633, 4.898905). A house about two metres wide on the Oude Hoogstraat, and the narrow house opposite the Trippenhuis that legend says the coachman of the Trips asked for, "as wide as your front door". Local voice: d'Oude Binnenstad 2014-2; OpNieuw 2019-3 ("Het Trippenhuis"); That Dam Guide. Caveat: the coachman story is legend; listed houses. Rank **Nice**. New place (group of two).
title: Two smallest houses: Oude Hoogstraat 22 and the Trips' coachman

heading: Burgwallen-Oude Zijde
text: **DC-23. Stoofbrug and the 3D-printed bridge.** Pin 52.372371, 4.897816; Oudezijds Achterburgwal at the Stoofsteeg. MX3D's printed steel bridge lay here from July 2021 to October 2023; the Vereniging filed an enforcement request because "temporary" threatened to become permanent; the old 19th-century bridge had gone missing, parts were found, and it came back with a lantern on 12 April 2024. Local voice: "Ik ben blij dat er weer een brug komt" (AT5, 16 Feb 2024). Lead: nl.wikipedia Stoofbrug; AT5 225085; VVAB news 450. Rank **Okay**. New place.
title: Stoofbrug and the 3D-printed bridge

heading: Burgwallen-Oude Zijde
text: **DC-24. Grimburgwal, the oldest lampposts in the canal.** Pin approx 52.369350, 4.895300. The only row of the city's oldest lamppost model (1847, foundry Enthoven) and 12 cast-iron balusters fell in when the quay collapsed on 1 September 2020 and were fished out at the Vereniging's request. Lead: VVAB Binnenstad 299; UvA campus page on the quay replacement (2026 onward). Status: unknown whether the posts are back. Outlook: Major change ahead (quay replacement). Rank **Okay**. New place, or a Look for line for a Huis aan de Drie Grachten place.
title: Grimburgwal, the oldest lampposts in the canal
rank_text: Rank **Okay**. New place, or a Look for line for a Huis aan de Drie Grachten place.

heading: Burgwallen-Oude Zijde
text: **DC-25. Heintje Hoekssteeg, the alley that got its gate.** Pin 52.375203, 4.899122. Named after Heyntgen Hoec, who lived here 1382 to 1410, and the source of the old nickname "Het Haantje" of the attic church on its corner; residents asked ten years for a gate against dealers and drunks and got it in March 2026 (shut 20:00 to 08:00). Local voice: "Was openbaar toilet" (AT5, 4 March 2026). Lead: https://www.at5.nl/artikelen/237136 ; nl.wikipedia Heintje Hoekssteeg. Caveat: beside A-list Ons' Lieve Heer op Solder. Rank **Okay**. New place.
title: Heintje Hoekssteeg, the alley that got its gate

heading: Burgwallen-Oude Zijde
text: **DC-26. The head of the Geldersekade: fish market, water gate and Bredero.** Pin 52.373188, 4.900783. From 1840 to the 1930s the fish hall stood here behind the Waag; the water gate under the Nieuwmarkt and two wooden landings remain. Piet Esser's statue shows Bredero's Jerolimo trying to steal a kiss from Trijntje Snaps; city papers keep calling the spot "Brederoplein". Local voice: columnist Janne, "Waar is het Brederodeplein?" (OpNieuw 2022-4). Lead: https://www.nhnieuws.nl/nieuws/356648 (1 Feb 2026); OpNieuw 2022-4. Rank **Okay**. New place.
title: The head of the Geldersekade: fish market, water gate and Bredero

heading: Nieuwmarkt/Lastage
text: **DC-27. Blauw Jan (gone), the menagerie inn.** Pin 52.369314, 4.897597; Kloveniersburgwal 87. In the 17th century an inn here showed animals from far countries; the site now carries the letters of the craft school "Maatschappij voor den werkenden stand" (1854). Lead: nl.wikipedia Blauw Jan; https://www.nhnieuws.nl/nieuws/293902 . Gone, with a building and letters to stand by. Rank **Okay**, status Gone. New place.
title: Blauw Jan (gone), the menagerie inn

heading: Nieuwmarkt/Lastage
text: **DC-28. Montelbaanstoren, "Malle Jaap".** Pin 52.372039, 4.905658; Oudeschans 2. The tower's nickname comes from bells that rang at the wrong times; OpNieuw ran "De klokken van Malle Jaap" (2018-2) and reported the tower's restoration in 2007. Lead: OpNieuw 2018-2, 2007-1; Amsterdam Sights; Wanderlustingk. Caveat: second-tier sight; nickname origin needs a firm source. Rank **Nice**. New place.
title: Montelbaanstoren, "Malle Jaap"

heading: Nieuwmarkt/Lastage
text: **DC-29. Speeltuin De Waag, a playground since 1932.** Pin 52.372236, 4.904336; Oudeschans 10d. Opened in 1932 for the tenth birthday of buurtvereniging De Waag (1922) and still on the same spot; the association keeps its banners and asks old players for memories. Lead: OpNieuw 2021-4; speeltuindewaag.nl. Visiting: public playground, opening hours. Rank **Okay**. New place.
title: Speeltuin De Waag, a playground since 1932

heading: Nieuwmarkt/Lastage
text: **DC-30. Nieuwmarkt metro station, the riot remembered underground.** Pin 52.371318, 4.900879. The station (opened 11 October 1980) was dug where houses were pulled down for the metro, the cause of the Nieuwmarkt riots of 1975; inside are works on that history, among them a wrecking ball hitting the wall and the photo collage "Groeten uit de Nieuwmarkt". In 2012 residents founded "Red de ondergrondse metrokunst" when the renovation threatened the art; 1,670 signed and the art was kept. Local voice: "Het is een symbool voor de vernieling van de oude Nieuwmarktbuurt" (AT5 2023); OpNieuw 2022-2 "Ondergrondse metrokunst gered" (the photo collage itself was lost to graffiti long ago, only frames remain). Lead: nl.wikipedia Nieuwmarkt (metrostation); https://www.nhnieuws.nl/nieuws/76163 ; https://www.at5.nl/artikelen/221229 . Rank **Amazing**. New place.
title: Nieuwmarkt metro station, the riot remembered underground

heading: Nieuwmarkt/Lastage
text: **DC-31. Auke Bijlsmabrug and Theo Boschbrug, bridges for the neighbourhood's fighters.** Pin 52.373028, 4.901956 (Auke Bijlsmabrug, Recht Boomssloot). On 31 May 2018 bridge 294 was named after Auke Bijlsma, whose lobbying helped the council reject a four-lane road through the neighbourhood by 22 votes to 21 on 5 January 1972, and bridge 230 over the Raamgracht by the Zwanenburgwal after the architect of the Pentagon, Theo Bosch. Local voice: OpNieuw headline "Eindelijk gerechtigheid!"; the neighbourhood's yearly front-garden prize carries Bijlsma's name. Lead: OpNieuw 2018-3; city decision of 5 Dec 2017 (gmb-2017-217097). Look for: Theo Boschbrug at the Zwanenburgwal end of the Raamgracht. Rank **Okay**. New place.
title: Auke Bijlsmabrug and Theo Boschbrug, bridges for the neighbourhood's fighters

heading: Nieuwmarkt/Lastage
text: **DC-32. Huis De Pinto, saved by the neighbourhood.** Pin 52.370096, 4.900857; Sint Antoniesbreestraat 69. The city bought the house in 1968 to demolish it for a planned road and the metro; squatted by the VVAB in the early 1970s and defended by Geurt Brinkgreve and the Stichting De Pinto (1971), it was restored in 1975 and housed a library branch from 1975; residents fought the branch's move in 2007. Today a cultural centre (OSM). In September 2025 a memorial for fifty years of Huis De Pinto took the last line of the poem city poet F. Starik wrote for it: "Blijf. En durf te zijn. Ga niet kwijt." Local voice: OpNieuw used the line as its motto (2025-4). Lead: OpNieuw 2025-4, 2015-4; nl.wikipedia Huis De Pinto (read 24 Nov 2026). Visiting: opening hours of the centre. Rank **Nice**. New place.
title: Huis De Pinto, saved by the neighbourhood

heading: Nieuwmarkt/Lastage
text: **DC-33. The Marionettentheater in the old smithy.** Pin 52.373443, 4.902377; Nieuwe Jonkerstraat 8. A seventy-seat puppet theatre in the former smithy where the Aktiegroep Nieuwmarkt used to meet; in March 2025 residents unveiled a squatters' map with over 200 addresses of the 1970s there. Local voice: OpNieuw 2024-4 and 2025-1. Lead: OpNieuw; second source needed for the smithy-meeting claim. Rank **Okay**. New place.
title: The Marionettentheater in the old smithy

heading: Nieuwmarkt/Lastage
text: **DC-34. Fort van Sjakoo, the bookshop from the squatters' years.** Pin 52.369111, 4.901893; Jodenbreestraat 24. Founded 1977, one of the firms OpNieuw counts among those "uit het verzet van de jaren 70 geboren". Lead: OpNieuw 2015-3; Amsterdamian. Rank **Okay**. New place.
title: Fort van Sjakoo, the bookshop from the squatters' years

heading: Burgwallen-Nieuwe Zijde
text: **DC-35. The Handelsblad complex and the Keizerrijk.** Pin 52.372200, 4.890367; Nieuwezijds Voorburgwal 234-240. The gold letters "Algemeen Handelsblad" still mark the paper's old office and printing works, squatted in 1978 and now social rented housing, "één groot complex met allemaal kruip door, sluip door routes"; a lesbian squat group lived in the street in the 1980s. Lead: https://www.at5.nl/artikelen/237135 (3 March 2026); nl.wikipedia Algemeen Handelsblad. Rank **Nice**. New place.
title: The Handelsblad complex and the Keizerrijk

heading: Burgwallen-Nieuwe Zijde
text: **DC-36. Vrankrijk.** Pin 52.371691, 4.889222; Spuistraat 216. A squat bar and political venue of the squatters' movement that has outlasted most of the Spuistraat squats. Lead: What's up with Amsterdam; nl.wikipedia Vrankrijk (to read). Status: open per OSM. Rank **Okay**. New place.
title: Vrankrijk

heading: Burgwallen-Nieuwe Zijde
text: **DC-37. Het Lieverdje.** Pin 52.368777, 4.889027; Spui. Carel Kneulman's statue was the stage of Provo's happenings in 1965-67; restored and back on 27 May 2024 ("Hij heeft al heel wat ellende gehad", AT5). Look for: the Friday book market on the Spui, squeezed by the street's renovation (NH, 11 Sep 2026). Lead: nl.wikipedia Het Lieverdje; https://www.at5.nl/artikelen/226839 . Rank **Nice**. New place.
title: Het Lieverdje

heading: Nieuwmarkt/Lastage
text: **DC-38. "De Gelderse Gaai", a bird carved from a broken paving slab.** Pin approx 52.372550, 4.900750; east side of the Nieuwmarkt, by the bench opposite café Bern. When the square was redone in 2010 a broken slab fell off a lorry outside the Waalsteeg; sculptor Klaartje Verhoeven carved it by hand into a bird and the city let her lay it back in the square in November 2010. After the last refit it came back without its bench, neck broken, and was relaid in January 2025 (now spelt "Geldersche Gaai"); the city's art department declined to take it on. Local voice: a resident and her granddaughter clean it every Monday; "Ik lig hier weer, ga niet meer weg" (the bird speaking, OpNieuw 2025-4). Lead: d'Oude Binnenstad 2015-1; OpNieuw 2025-2, 2025-4 (same author, Greetje van der Krieke). Second source independent of her needed. Rank **Nice**. New place.
title: "De Gelderse Gaai", a bird carved from a broken paving slab

heading: Nieuwmarkt/Lastage
text: **DC-39. Aprilfeesten on the Nieuwmarkt.** Pin 52.372553, 4.900089 (the square). A neighbourhood fair every April on the square, run by residents ("Heb mijn vakantie er voor omgeboekt", AT5 21 April 2026). Lead: nl.wikipedia Aprilfeesten; OpNieuw 2017-1, 2024-2. Caveat: a yearly event, not a thing to see; could be a Look for line in DC-38. Rank **Okay**. New place or Look for.
title: Aprilfeesten on the Nieuwmarkt
rank_text: Rank **Okay**. New place or Look for.

heading: Burgwallen-Oude Zijde
text: **DC-40. The plaskrul with the two watchers, Oudekerksplein.** Pin approx 52.374300, 4.897600 (by the Oude Kerk; fix on site). One of about 37 remaining cast-iron "krullen" (the city's own design, first placed about 1880); the one at the Oude Kerk has two small figures on top, and another on the Oudezijds Voorburgwal is in Amsterdam School style. The city is letting them die out. Local voice: photographer Renzo Gerritsen, "Ik vind het wel ballen hebben dat hij hier nog staat" (NH, 30 May 2024). Lead: https://www.nhnieuws.nl/nieuws/336685 ; nl.wikipedia Plaskrul. Rank **Nice**. New place.
title: The plaskrul with the two watchers, Oudekerksplein

heading: Burgwallen-Oude Zijde
text: **DC-41. He Hua temple and the Chinese Zeedijk.** Pin 52.373726, 4.900075; Zeedijk 106-118. A palace-style Buddhist temple opened by Queen Beatrix in September 2000; around it bilingual street signs, Dun Yong (the first Chinese toko on the Zeedijk) and the Vesak procession. Local voice: VVAB Binnenstad 188, "opvallende vreemdeling op de dijk". Lead: VVAB Binnenstad 188; NH 356249 (Dun Yong, Jan 2026). Rank **Nice**. New place.
title: He Hua temple and the Chinese Zeedijk

heading: Burgwallen-Oude Zijde
text:
**DC-42. Jacob Hooy & Co., the drugstore of 1743.** Pin 52.371956, 4.899184; Kloveniersburgwal 10-12. A herb and liquorice shop with its old drawers and jars; a rent rise in 2017 threatened "het einde voor eeuwenoude drogisterij" (AT5). Lead: AT5 166258; d'Oude Binnenstad ads. Status: open per OSM; check. Caveat: a shop; borderline under the shops rule. Rank **Okay**. New place.

title: Jacob Hooy & Co., the drugstore of 1743

heading: Oostelijke Eilanden/Kadijken
text: **DE-01. The floating gardens of Robert Jasper Grootveld, Wittenburgervaart.** Pin 52.370100, 4.922300 (the rafts in the Wittenburgervaart at the foot of the Ezelsbrug; approximate, on the water). Three planted rafts named Grootveld, Jasper and Robert, built with the knotting technique of the provo "anti-smoke magician" Robert Jasper Grootveld (1932-2009) and moored opposite his own tyre boat, so that the spot is, in the maker's words, one Gesamtkunstwerk by Grootveld. The city banned them in June 2021 under a 50,000 euro penalty (Waternet said the materials were unsafe), relented in October 2021, and they were handed to the neighbourhood on 19 July 2022, Grootveld's 90th birthday. Local voice: paid for by residents' vote (Centrum Begroot, 50,000 euro); the film "Drijfland" was shown in De Witte Boei on 30 Sept 2026. Lead: https://www.buurtorganisatie1018.nl/nieuws-uit-1018/2022/7/26/drijvende-tuinen-overgedragen-aan-de-buurt ; second: https://stadscuratorium.nl/en/collectie/floating-gardens/ and https://www.buurtorganisatie1018.nl/nieuws-uit-1018/2021/6/24/gemeente-verbiedt-drijvende-tuinen . Status: in place (Aug 2026). Caveats: 1018 Magazine says the permit ends Feb 2027 (Outlook: Under threat); Grootveld's own boat needs checking on site. **Amazing**; new place.
title: The floating gardens of Robert Jasper Grootveld, Wittenburgervaart

heading: Oostelijke Eilanden/Kadijken
text: **DE-02. Tug of war on the Kippebrug, Kattenburg against Wittenburg.** Pin 52.371694, 4.919498 (Kippebrug, by the Wittenburgerhoofd). A small Amsterdam School footbridge by Piet Kramer (1923), once part of a round bridgehead with a bathhouse, is the yearly battlefield of a "traditional" tug of war between the two islands, with prizes and a shared meal in De Witte Boei afterwards (2017 during the Aardappeloproer festival, 8 June 2019). Local voice: island rivalry ("eens een Eilander, altijd een Eilander", buurtboeken.nl). Lead: https://www.buurtorganisatie1018.nl/nieuws-uit-1018/2019/6/7/zaterdag-8-juni-1330-u-touwtrekken-wittenburg-tegen-kattenburg-op-de-kippebrug ; second: https://nl.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kippebrug_(Amsterdam) (bridge facts). Status: bridge standing; latest tug of war found June 2019. Caveats: whether the contest is still yearly is not confirmed after 2019 (check: Still there?); the animal bridge names of 1018 (Kippebrug, Ezelsbrug, Pelikaanbrug, Nijlpaardenbrug, Oliphantsbrug) can be a Look for line here. **Nice**; new place.
title: Tug of war on the Kippebrug, Kattenburg against Wittenburg

heading: Oostelijke Eilanden/Kadijken
text: **DE-03. Shaffy's Tuin, Dijksgracht-West.** Pin 52.376411, 4.912446 (the garden, OSM). A neighbourhood garden on the Dijksgracht-West, named after Ramses Shaffy, who lived on a houseboat here in the 1970s; ten years old on 6 Sept 2025, when its gardeners published a 5 km "green discovery walk" past twelve hidden gardens of Centrum-Oost. Local voice: a garden made and kept by residents on a forgotten strip between the railway and the water. Lead: https://www.buurtorganisatie1018.nl/nieuws-uit-1018/2025/9/18/groene-wandeling-vanaf-shaffys-tuin ; second: https://shaffystuin.nl/buiten . Status: open (Sept 2025). Caveats: the houseboat claim comes from 1018 only (verify); the new bike path on the Dijksgracht-Oost (2026) is a fight next door. **Nice**; new place.
title: Shaffy's Tuin, Dijksgracht-West

heading: Oostelijke Eilanden/Kadijken
text: **DE-04. The Sibbelwoningen, Hoogte Kadijk 112-150.** Pin 52.368758, 4.916806 (Hoogte Kadijk 130).
