A vitrine where costume designer Rien Bekkers (over 150 theatre, opera and ballet productions) shows metre-high dolls in 18th-century court dress, changed regularly. Local voice: "De onbevangen wandelaar loopt door de Herenstraat en wordt plotseling verrast door een wonderbaarlijk tafereel." Lead: Zeven 141 p3. Second: https://threadfashionandcostume.blogspot.com/2024/06/rien-bekkers.html (career only). Status: December 2023. Caveat: location and status on site (Location). Rank **Okay**. New place.
title: Rien Bekkers's costume dolls, Herenstraat

heading: Water and infrastructure
text: **G-07. The hole in the quay: a 600-year-old sluice under the Nieuwmarkt.** Pin 52.373100, 4.900450; head of the Geldersekade at the Nieuwmarkt (Burgwallen-Oude Zijde, on the border with Nieuwmarkt/Lastage). In the quay wall at the very end of the Geldersekade is a half-round opening under sandstone arches, 1.75 m wide, closed by a floating boom. It is the mouth of a 170 m culvert that runs under the Nieuwmarkt and under the Waag itself to the Kloveniersburgwal, and halfway along it sits a sluice with heavy wooden double doors that has worked for some six centuries (it is officially bridge 495 and sluice 202). It kept the salt IJ water of the Geldersekade apart from the fresh Amstel water of the Kloveniersburgwal. The odd part: it was paid for by a polder board some 40 km away, the Grootwaterschap Bijleveld between Harmelen and Montfoort, which won the right in 1413 to drain its water through Amsterdam; the sluice was rebuilt here in 1454 and the city gate that became the Waag was built right over it in the 1480s. Bijleveld handed it to the city in 1492. When the Nieuwmarkt was laid over the canals in 1614 the culvert was simply lengthened. A side branch drained the Huidenvettersloot, an open sewer with rats "the size of a beaver" until 1899. Local voice: Bijleveldsche sluis. Lead: Ons Amsterdam, "De middeleeuwse sluis onder de Waag", https://onsamsterdam.nl/artikelen/de-middeleeuwse-sluis-onder-de-waag ; second source: https://nl.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bijleveldschesluis (brug 495; culvert renewed 1988-1990 when old remains were found). Status: in use (Ons Amsterdam, undated web article; wiki current). Caveats: the Waag is A-list, but the culvert and its quay opening are not; pin estimated at the head of the Geldersekade, walk-check the opening (wiki puts the structure at 52.372619, 4.900436, under the square). Rank **Amazing**. New place.
title: The hole in the quay: a 600-year-old sluice under the Nieuwmarkt

heading: Monuments and moved fragments
text: **G-01. Leprozenpoort: the lepers' gate that walked down the street.** Pin 52.369926, 4.901111; Sint Antoniesluis 21-24 (Nieuwmarkt/Lastage). The 17th-century entrance gate of the Leprozenhuis, the lepers' house that stood where the Mr. Visserplein traffic square is now. It came from the workshop of Hendrick de Keyser (possibly cut by his English brother-in-law Nicholas Stone). In the tall fronton, under the city arms with the imperial crown, two niches hold a leper man and a leper woman with their clappers (the wooden rattles lepers had to sound). The gate was taken down for the IJ-tunnel approach, stored, and rebuilt by Stichting De Pinto in the 1970s/80s along the Sint Antoniesluis, a few hundred metres from its first spot, during the restoration of Huis De Pinto. Hans 't Mannetje restored the gate; Henri van Haaren recut the badly damaged reliefs, so what you see are copies. Local voice: also called the Lazaruspoort (the Leprozenhuis was the Lazarushuis, the lane beside it the Lazarussteeg). Lead: VVAB, De Lamp van Diogenes 104/105 (Sept 1987), via https://web.archive.org/web/2025/https://amsterdamsebinnenstad.nl/ ; second source: https://nl.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leprozenhuis_(Amsterdam) (section Leprozenpoort, citing Minne Dijkstra, "Poortjes van Amsterdam 1571-1782", 2008/2009). Status: standing (Dijkstra 2009; the drafts only mention the Leprozenhuis as a charity landowner). Caveats: not found in the RCE register under its own name; check whether it is listed with Sint Antoniesluis. Pin is from the PDOK address centroid of no. 22; walk-check which side the gate faces. Rank **Nice**. New place (could group with AC-14 Grenspaal, a few steps away and also by Hans 't Mannetje).
title: Leprozenpoort: the lepers' gate that walked down the street
rank_text: Rank **Nice**. New place (could group with AC-14 Grenspaal, a few steps away and also by Hans 't Mannetje).

heading: Monuments and moved fragments
text: **G-02. The Heerenlogement gate on the Keizersgracht.** Pin 52.368591, 4.884916; Keizersgracht 365 (Grachtengordel-West). The little entrance gate of the Oudezijds Heerenlogement, the city's grandest inn (an English merchant called it "the noblest taverne in the world" in 1653), which stood on the Grimburgwal from 1647 to 1874 and ended as the city's best-known auction house. When it was pulled down for the Binnengasthuis, the last auctioneer, J.P.A. Kilsdonk, had the gate carried to his new auction rooms here, so the name Heeren-Logement moved with it. City arms in the tympanum, the imperial crown on top, flanked by two lying lions (the lions are renewals: the originals were wrecked in a rough 1975 rebuild). The rest of the building scattered: festoons in the Rijksmuseum's fragment building, the fronton lions via the Stedelijk and the Rijkspostspaarbank to the ING office on the Haarlemmerweg, the city arms in a rock garden and then a restoration workshop, the crown still missing. Lead: Binnenstad 278 (2016), Gert Eijkelboom and Gerrit Vermeer, "De omzwerving van de leeuwen van de Grimburgwal", https://web.archive.org/web/2025/https://amsterdamsebinnenstad.nl/binnenstad/278/heerenlogement.php ; second source: RCE monument 2328, Keizersgracht 363-367 ("met hierheen overgeplaatst poortje van het Oudezijds Herenlogement (1647)"), https://monumentenregister.cultureelerfgoed.nl/monumenten/2328 . Status: in place (RCE register; article 2016). Caveats: rijksmonument; check whether the VVAB plan to reunite the fragments at the Grimburgwal ever happened. Rank **Nice**. New place.
title: The Heerenlogement gate on the Keizersgracht

heading: Monuments and moved fragments
text: **G-03. Orphan gable tops: the gables that played musical chairs.** Pin 52.364023, 4.886495; Prinsengracht 755 (Grachtengordel-Zuid), with the others as Look for. About 135 canal houses wear a gable crown taken from a demolished house elsewhere: the city stored the carved tops in its monument yard and sold them for re-use, and for more than half nobody wrote down where they came from (Theo Rouwhorst, "Bewaard voor Amsterdam. Historische geveltoppen herplaatst 1945-2015", 2016). The best chain: the neck gable of 1701 at Prinsengracht 755 carries little sea gods blowing shell horns that came from Amstelstraat 49, taken off when that house was simplified in 1938 and stored at Frankendael; Amstelstraat 49 in turn got a top in 2003 taken from Haarlemmer Houttuinen 193. VVAB called it a stoelendans (musical chairs). Look for: Bloemgracht 19 (52.374871, 4.882246), the rococo bell gable placed in 1980 as top no. 1 of the monuments office, traced to "De drie geblomde cassaes", Kalverstraat 222, demolished for Vroom & Dreesmann; Bloemgracht 73 (52.374424, 4.880249), not an 18th-century house at all but a 1976 rebuild of a house demolished in 1966, crowned with a different top bought from the city yard in Duivendrecht on 16 November 1972; Amstelstraat 49 (52.366281, 4.899977). The jordaan-5 draft already has Rozenstraat 35-43, a row of 1934 with five tops from elsewhere: merge this item with it or link the two. Leads: Binnenstad 310 (David Mulder, Prinsengracht 755), Binnenstad 306 (Bloemgracht 19), Binnenstad 308 (Bloemgracht 73), all via https://web.archive.org/web/2025/https://amsterdamsebinnenstad.nl/ ; second source: RCE monument 4398 ("een van elders overgebrachte hals met schelpblazende zeegodjes aan de vleugelstukken"), https://monumentenregister.cultureelerfgoed.nl/monumenten/4398 . Status: in place (RCE; articles 2023). The tritons are comic putti with scaly fish tails, from the workshop of Anthonie Turck (c. 1720), and the find was pure chance: a photo of Amstelstraat 49 from 1926 turned up while the writer looked for a picture of the Blauwbrug. The row of five, built in 1701 as speculation, is named after the continents: Europa (747), Asia (749), Afrika (753), Amerika (755), with 751 nameless but dated 1701; most of it is a 1959-60 rebuild. Caveats: all rijksmonumenten. Rank **Nice**. New place (one pin, the rest as Look for).
title: Orphan gable tops: the gables that played musical chairs
rank_text: Rank **Nice**. New place (one pin, the rest as Look for).

heading: Monuments and moved fragments
text: **G-04. Singel 390: the globe that was melted down and came back.** Pin 52.369374, 4.887183; Singel 390 (Grachtengordel-West). Apollo and Minerva sit on the raised cornice of this early 18th-century house, and between them sat a copper celestial globe, 1.20 m across. In 1914 it was taken down and melted for its copper. Hotel Ambassade, which owns the house, had a new globe made and hoisted it on 11 December 2002. Lead: Binnenstad 197/198 (March 2003); second source: RCE monument 5381 (cornice with Apollo and Minerva), https://monumentenregister.cultureelerfgoed.nl/monumenten/5381 . Status: globe back since 2002 (latest evidence 2003); check it is still up. Caveats: rijksmonument; hotel. Rank **Okay**. Group with G-03 (moved and replaced gable crowns), or new place.
title: Singel 390: the globe that was melted down and came back
rank_text: Rank **Okay**. Group with G-03 (moved and replaced gable crowns), or new place.

heading: Monuments and moved fragments
text: **G-05. Kalverstraat 10: the booksellers' palace above the shops.** Pin 52.372291, 4.891931; Kalverstraat 10 (Burgwallen-Nieuwe Zijde). Look up above the shop window: a raised cornice crowned by busts of Minerva and Mercury. On this plot Clement de Jonghe, Rembrandt's print publisher, kept his shop "De gekroonde konstkaert" from 1662; then came a coffee house and art shop, then Gerard Valk, the globe maker. Rudolf Wetstein, printer of Bibles in Malay and of the VOC's ship psalm book (12,700 still in stock when he died), rebuilt it in 1727 as a 35 m deep "art and book palace"; the map maker Isaac Tirion and sea-chart sellers followed, and Frederik Muller's auction house and bookshop until 1883. Wetstein's chronogram stone (capital letters adding up to 1728) went to the KOG in 1883. Lead: Binnenstad 266 (2014), Pieter Vlaardingerbroek, "Kalverstraat 10: boeken, kunst en koffie", https://web.archive.org/web/2025/https://amsterdamsebinnenstad.nl/binnenstad/266/kalverstraat-10.php ; second source: RCE monument 2138 (gable with busts, XVIIIb). Status: facade in place (RCE). Caveats: rijksmonument; nothing of the book trade left inside. Rank **Okay**. New place.
title: Kalverstraat 10: the booksellers' palace above the shops

heading: Monuments and moved fragments
text: **G-06. Koningsplein 10: the 3-metre chocolate shop that rose from the ashes.** Pin 52.367118, 4.888815; Koningsplein 10 (Grachtengordel-Zuid). Between the big stores of the Koningsplein, a house front less than three metres wide with a bay window and a little balcony in carved Art Nouveau woodwork. It was built in 1901 (architect P. van der Vliet) as a chocolaterie for J. Bruin, later held a jeweller, and burned out in 1936 (a gas heater, the papers said, after a false burglar alarm had woken the whole street months earlier). A plain modern front replaced it, which wore down to a blank white wall with a cash machine. In the 2020s architect Kees Doornenbal rebuilt the 1901 front from drawings and photos, milling ornaments and frames out of single wooden boards. Today it is only the entrance and stairwell for 22 flats above the neighbouring shops. Local voice: VVAB called it "snoepje en sieraad voor de stad". Look for: Kalverstraat 114, where Doornenbal had a Spanish sculptor recut the 17th-century neck-gable top taken off in 1937, and next door at 116-118 the copper front of 1931 by Gerard Loogman, found intact behind a 1980s glass curtain wall (Binnenstad 301/302). Lead: Binnenstad 308 (2022), "Reconstructie Koningsplein 10", https://web.archive.org/web/2025/https://amsterdamsebinnenstad.nl/binnenstad/308/reconstructie-koningsplein-10.php ; second source needed (Cuypersbulletin, or the Stadsarchief beeldbank for the 1901 front). Status: rebuilt (2022). Caveats: not listed (orde 3). Rank **Okay**. New place.
title: Koningsplein 10: the 3-metre chocolate shop that rose from the ashes

heading: Houses with a story (Hendrick de Keyser houses)
text: **G-08. De Vier Heemskinderen: four knights on one horse at the Leidsegracht corner.** Pin 52.367617, 4.886278; Herengracht 394, north corner of the Leidsegracht (Grachtengordel-West). The baker Jan Specht bought the corner plot where the 1614 and 1663 city extensions meet and in 1671 built a tall neck gable "daar de vier Heemskinderen in de gevel staan": the stone shows the four sons of Aymon from the medieval romance, Adelaart, Ritsaart, Writsaart and Reinout, all riding their magic horse Beyaert. There was a bakery here almost without a break. The stone was put on a postage stamp in 1975. Look for: the 17th-century windows in the top are unchanged; the shop front is late 19th century. Lead: Vereniging Hendrick de Keyser, https://www.hendrickdekeyser.nl/de-huizen/de-vier-heemskinderen ; second source: RCE monument 1832 (Herengracht 394). Status: standing, let as homes by the Vereniging (page read 2026-11-24). Caveats: rijksmonument, private; a different Vier Heemskinderen stone of 1899 sits in the nieuwezijde-1 draft (city register 210015), do not mix them up. Rank **Okay**. New place.
title: De Vier Heemskinderen: four knights on one horse at the Leidsegracht corner

heading: Houses with a story (Hendrick de Keyser houses)
text: **G-09. Gables that swim: Abraham Zeeman's sea fish and the dolphins of De Hond.** Pin 52.379327, 4.892490; Brouwersgracht 50 (Haarlemmerbuurt). Around 1715 Abraham Zeeman (the name means "seaman") had the claw pieces beside his neck gable carved as sea fish, a pun on his own name. It was a real tenement: a cellar flat with a little shop, a lower house and two room flats above. Hendrick de Keyser bought it worn out in 1918, one of its first houses. Look for: Herengracht 59 "De Hond" (52.377938, 4.891257), a classicist front of 1659 for the Mennonite merchant Isacq van Halmael, whose small claw pieces are dolphins. Lead: Vereniging Hendrick de Keyser, https://www.hendrickdekeyser.nl/de-huizen/brouwersgracht-50 and .../de-huizen/de-hond ; second source: RCE monuments 760 (Brouwersgracht 50) and 1529 (Herengracht 59). Status: standing, let as homes (pages read 2026-11-24). Caveats: rijksmonumenten, private. Rank **Okay**. New place.
title: Gables that swim: Abraham Zeeman's sea fish and the dolphins of De Hond

heading: Houses with a story (Hendrick de Keyser houses)
text: **G-10. Huis Serne: a century of theatre costumes, and a ceiling that ended a painter.** Pin 52.367932, 4.897140; Groenburgwal 56 (Nieuwmarkt/Lastage). A tall neck-gabled merchant's house of about 1720 near the Binnen-Amstel. The banker Willem Borski, whose fortune his widow later put into founding De Nederlandsche Bank, was born here in 1765. From 1883 it belonged to the Serne family: Arend Serne and Helena van Hoekelen, keen amateur actors, hired out stage costumes, and for more than a hundred years and four generations "A. Serne en Zoon" filled the rooms, fitting booths and attics with costumes and props for opera, operetta, student masquerades and costume balls; the front was restored to its 18th-century look for the firm's centenary in 1966. Inside hangs a clumsily painted ceiling piece: contemporaries said a "mislukt platfond" the young Hermanus Noordkerk painted for his father around 1720 made him give up painting and study law (he became a known jurist and a friend of Betje Wolff). Lead: Vereniging Hendrick de Keyser (bought 2019), https://www.hendrickdekeyser.nl/de-huizen/huis-serne ; second source: RCE monument 1273 (Groenburgwal 56). Status: owned by the Vereniging since 2019 (page read 2026-11-24). Caveats: rijksmonument; the ceiling is inside, so only the facade is public unless an open day is found; that the Groenburgwal ceiling is that very "failed" one is the Vereniging's attribution. Rank **Okay**. New place.
title: Huis Serne: a century of theatre costumes, and a ceiling that ended a painter

heading: Sweep 1: trees with a story / Burgwallen-Oude Zijde
text: **GR-01. The tallest tree in Amsterdam, in the Oudemanhuispoort courtyard.** Pin 52.369373, 4.895953 (courtyard of the Oudemanhuispoort, between Oudezijds Achterburgwal and Kloveniersburgwal). A Dutch elm planted in 1890 in the old convent garden is, at 36 m, the tallest tree of Centrum and probably of the whole city, and at 4.72 m round also the thickest elm in Amsterdam. Thousands of students walk past it every year without looking up; its base is hollow (tested 2015) but it was in good condition in August 2025. Local voice: the Bomenstichting walk calls it "de hoogste boom van Amsterdam"; artist and lawyer Jet Nijkamp drew it when the law faculty left the building. Lead: CBH advice 2024, "Hoogste boom en dikste iep van Amsterdam-Centrum" (link above); second: LRMB 1692908 and Bomenstichting walk 2021 (35 m). Status: standing, register "Kampioenboom" (download 24 Nov 2026). Caveats: courtyard open only when the UvA building is open (Mon to Fri); heights differ, 35 m (2021 walk) or 36 m (2024 advice). Rank **Amazing**. Group with the draft "Oudemanhuispoort and its book stalls" (oudezijde-1) or new place; DC-21 is the same arcade.
title: The tallest tree in Amsterdam, in the Oudemanhuispoort courtyard
rank_text: Rank **Amazing**. Group with the draft "Oudemanhuispoort and its book stalls" (oudezijde-1) or new place; DC-21 is the same arcade.

heading: Sweep 1: trees with a story / Burgwallen-Nieuwe Zijde
text: **GR-02. The last elm of the Stationsplein.** Pin 52.378304, 4.899057 (Stationsplein, in front of Centraal Station, east of the main entrance). The sole survivor of the more than 30 elms planted just after the station was built in 1889; it outlived Dutch elm disease and all the rebuilding of the square, and young elms were planted around it again in 2022. Girth over 3 m. Local voice: Bomenstichting walk: "het laatste exemplaar van de meer dan 30 iepen die geplant zijn vlak na de bouw van het Centraal Station". Lead: Bomenstichting walk 2021; second: LRMB 1694179 and city champion list (ID 339649, CBH advice 2024). OSM tags it as natural monument (node 3911893539). Status: standing, champion tree (24 Nov 2026). Rank **Nice**. New place.
title: The last elm of the Stationsplein

heading: Sweep 1: trees with a story / Grachtengordel-West
text: **GR-03. The Westermarkt elm, Amsterdam's own knobbly elm.** Pin 52.374260, 4.884137 (Keizersgracht by the Westermarkt, city tree ID 341941). An elm planted around 1900, probably from the city's own nursery at Frankendael, turned out to be an undescribed cultivar with a lumpy, burred trunk; the tree committee has provisionally named it Ulmus x hollandica 'Westermarkt', the "Amsterdamse Knobbeliep". Only five are known for sure: this veteran, the elms opposite Keizersgracht 208, 224 and 234, and the old elm at Nieuwe Herengracht 5-7 (GR-07). Local voice: CBH: "een nog niet beschreven zeldzame afwijkende cultivar". Lead: CBH advice 2024, "Veteraanbomen"; second: city register notes ("Zeldzame varieteit met veel maserknollen, voorheen altijd als Belgica benoemd") and LRMB 1697438 (warreliep). Status: standing (register 24 Nov 2026). Caveat: the name is provisional. Rank **Nice**. New place (or merge with GR-07 as one item with two pins).
title: The Westermarkt elm, Amsterdam's own knobbly elm
rank_text: Rank **Nice**. New place (or merge with GR-07 as one item with two pins).

heading: Sweep 1: trees with a story / Grachtengordel-West
text: **GR-04. The thickest tree in Centrum, a plane at Molenpad 2.** Pin 52.367241, 4.883638 (Molenpad 2, corner Prinsengracht). An oriental plane 5.75 m round, registered as 1850 but probably planted about 1860 at the new bank building of Becker & Fuld; Carl Becker was also one of the founders of the Vondelpark. Lead: CBH advice 2024, "Dikste boom"; second: LRMB 1686161 and OSM node 2722025013 (girth 5.40 m). Status: standing, champion tree (24 Nov 2026). Caveats: privately owned (register "Particulier"); check it is fully visible from the Molenpad; the two planes on the Leidsebosje in West are thicker. Rank **Nice**. Group with the draft "Molenpad, from carriages to cars, and a copied corner" (gg-west-3) or new place.

heading: Sweep 1: trees with a story / De Weteringschans
text: **GR-05. The leaning poplar of the Weteringplantsoen.** Pin 52.359040, 4.890053 (Eerste Weteringplantsoen, corner Weteringschans and Weteringcircuit). A Canada poplar 'Serotina' of about 1910, 5.55 m round, leaning hard over the plantsoen: the biggest and thickest leaning tree of Amsterdam. A leaning tree is not less stable: it grows extra heavy roots on the far side. Local voice: known locally as "de scheve populier"; CBH: "Een echte kampioen". Lead: CBH advice 2024, "Scheve en liggende bomen"; second: Bomenstichting walk 2021 and LRMB 1686110. Status: standing, champion (24 Nov 2026). Rank **Nice**. Group with DE-36 (Kruidenpluktuin in the same plantsoen) or new place.
title: The leaning poplar of the Weteringplantsoen

heading: Sweep 1: trees with a story / De Weteringschans
text: **GR-06. The pagoda trees of the Falckstraat.** Pin 52.360268, 4.896524 (Reguliersgracht corner Falckstraat). The tallest and oldest Japanese pagoda tree in Amsterdam (1900), as far as known the only one in the city with a polypody fern growing on it, with a younger partner of 1930; they flower late, in August, when insects have little else. They stand on the line of the Achtergracht, filled in about 1869. Lead: CBH advice 2024, "Japanse honingboom Falckstraat"; second: Bomenstichting walk 2021 and LRMB 1686062. Status: both champions (24 Nov 2026). Rank **Okay**. New place.
title: The pagoda trees of the Falckstraat

heading: Sweep 1: trees with a story / Nieuwmarkt/Lastage
text: **GR-07. Nieuwe Herengracht 5-7: one of the oldest elms of Amsterdam, and the hanging elm.** Pin 52.366093, 4.902225 (quay opposite Nieuwe Herengracht 5-7). An elm of 1891, nearly 3.8 m round, the only survivor of the 19th-century planting on this quay and one of the five known 'Westermarkt' elms with their burred trunks (GR-03); often cited as the oldest elm of the city, though the one in the Oudemanhuispoort is as old. Further along hangs a century-old elm far out over the water, its trunk showing the ribbed tension roots that keep it up. Lead: CBH advice 2024 ("Oudste iep", "Scheve en liggende bomen", IDs 340635 and 341861); second: LRMB 1697438 (one of the "200 kampioenbomen van Amsterdam", 2025) and the register. Status: standing (24 Nov 2026). Caveat: pin of the hanging elm not taken (ID 341861, same quay). Rank **Nice**. Group with GR-03 or new place.
title: Nieuwe Herengracht 5-7: one of the oldest elms of Amsterdam, and the hanging elm

heading: Sweep 1: trees with a story / Haarlemmerbuurt
text: **GR-08. The oldest wild fig of Amsterdam, in the quay wall at the Drieharingenbrug.** Pin 52.386686, 4.887231 (Prinseneiland, corner at the Drieharingenbrug, in the quay wall). Nobody planted it: a fig seeded itself into the sunny, sheltered quay wall around 1990, among the very first spontaneous figs in the Netherlands, and is now a small tree that bears fruit. City botanist Ton Denters, who found Amsterdam's first wild fig in 1990 and has since counted about 150, gives its GPS in his blog; an older one nearby was rooted out by residents. The tree committee put it on the city's protected list in 2024 because it "tells the story of the changing climate". Lead: CBH advice 2024, "De vijgenboom op het Prinseneiland vertelt een verhaal"; second: stadsplanten.nl, "Ode aan de Vijgenboom" (Ton Denters, 3 Jan 2021), https://www.stadsplanten.nl/2021/01/ode-aan-de-vijgenboom/ ; the register (ID N5664: "De oudste wilde vijgenboom van Amsterdam"). Status: photographed Oct 2022, in the register 24 Nov 2026. Caveat: small; best in summer with leaves and figs. Rank **Amazing**. New place (near DW-55 Palmentuin, pitched on itself).
title: The oldest wild fig of Amsterdam, in the quay wall at the Drieharingenbrug

heading: Sweep 1: trees with a story / Weesperbuurt/Plantage
text: **GR-09. The elm museum round the Hortus: lying elms and an Anne Frank seedling.** Pin 52.366166, 4.907593 (Hortusplantsoen, the horizontal elms at the water behind the Hortus). Since 2015-16 the streets round the Hortus have been planted as a small "Ulmuseum" of rare elms. Behind the Hortus two elms lay over the water from the late 1970s until elm disease killed them in 2014; early 2015 two 'Rebona' elms were deliberately planted lying down to replace them, and their trunks are now bending upwards in an arc. A few metres on, a seedling of the Anne Frank chestnut, raised on a roof terrace, was planted in the heart of the old Jewish quarter in spring 2022. Lead: CBH advice 2024 ("Liggende iepen achter de Hortus", "Ulmuseum", "Anne Frank-paardenkastanje Hortusplantsoen"); second: oost-online.nl, "Zaailing Anne Frankboom geplant op het Hortusplantsoen", https://oost-online.nl/zaailing-anne-frankboom-geplant-op-het-hortusplantsoen/ ; register IDs 348335, 348336 ("Liggende bomen"), N5663 ("Zaailing Anne Frankboom"). Status: in the register 24 Nov 2026. Caveats: the chestnut is a sapling; the Hortus itself is A-list, this is the public street side. Rank **Nice**. New place (AE-04 memorials and the Theo Thijssen draft are on the same plantsoen).
title: The elm museum round the Hortus: lying elms and an Anne Frank seedling
rank_text: Rank **Nice**. New place (AE-04 memorials and the Theo Thijssen draft are on the same plantsoen).

heading: Sweep 1: trees with a story / Weesperbuurt/Plantage
text: **GR-10. One of the oldest dawn redwoods in the Netherlands, Wertheimpark.** Pin 52.367516, 4.908730 (Wertheimpark). The dawn redwood was known only as a fossil until living trees were found in China in 1941; in 1947 the Hortus was the first in the country to receive seeds, ten of them. Eight came up; one of the survivors stands free to see in the Wertheimpark, across the road from the Hortus. Lead: CBH advice 2024, "Oudste watercipres van Nederland"; second: register ID 341851 (1947, "Vermoedelijk een van de oudste watercipressen van Nederland"). Status: champion (24 Nov 2026). Caveat: both sources are the city's; the advice cites Dendroflora 15/16 for the seed history. Rank **Nice**. Group with DE-25 (the wingnut in the same park) and the Wertheim draft (plantage-1).
title: One of the oldest dawn redwoods in the Netherlands, Wertheimpark

heading: Sweep 1: trees with a story / Weesperbuurt/Plantage
text: **GR-11. The 120-year-old wisteria of Amstel 169-171.** Pin 52.360918, 4.904579 (Amstel 169-171). A wisteria about 120 years old, its thickest stem 60 cm round, covers the front in blue every May; it was voted the Fraaiste Groene Gevel of Amsterdam in 2018 and in 2024 was put on the city's list of protected trees, because a woody climber that thick counts as a tree. Lead: CBH advice 2024, "Gevelbomen, de blauwe regen aan de Amstel"; second: register ID N5625 ("Prijswinnaar 2018 mooiste gevelgroen"). Status: photographed July 2023, register 24 Nov 2026. Caveat: on a private house, seen from the street; a May place. Rank **Okay**. New place.
title: The 120-year-old wisteria of Amstel 169-171

heading: Sweep 1: trees with a story / Oostelijke Eilanden/Kadijken
text: **GR-12. The Shaffyboom, a tree that grew through a railway fence.** Pin 52.375813, 4.919539 (Dijksgracht, opposite the former mooring of Ramses Shaffy's houseboat). For Shaffy's 75th birthday in August 2008 residents named this maple, which has grown through the railway fence, the Ramses Shaffyboom: "a strong tree that speaks of pain and the force of life; that fits Shaffy well". The fence has gone along the whole line except where the tree swallowed it, and after his death in 2009 the neighbourhood held a memorial service at the tree. Local voice: the neighbourhood calls it a "Monument voor de Levenskracht". Lead: CBH advice 2024, "De Shaffyboom, monument voor levenskracht"; second: zwartekat.nl 27 Aug 2008 and AT5 "Sfeervolle herdenking bij de Shaffy-boom" (https://www.at5.nl/artikelen/28191/sfeervolle-herdenking-bij-de-shaffy-boom). Status: standing per the 2024 advice, in the register 24 Nov 2026. Caveat: on ProRail ground. Rank **Nice**. New place (DE dropped the OSM node for lack of a source: sources now found; group with DE-03 Shaffy's Tuin also possible).
title: The Shaffyboom, a tree that grew through a railway fence

heading: Sweep 2: public and community gardens / Nieuwmarkt/Lastage
text: **GR-13. Ruijtergaard, an orchard that had to grow in crates.** Pin 52.377808, 4.906990 (De Ruijterkade, the long strip along the quay east of the station). Residents dreamed of an orchard on a stony strip by the IJ; cables and pipes in the ground made planting trees impossible, so they built raised beds from city elm wood and planted them like a food forest, which also holds rainwater. Volunteers on Wednesday and Sunday afternoons, with school classes and company groups. Lead: Shaffy's Tuin walk 2025, item 2; second: OSM way 936942270 (name only). Status: active Sept 2025. Caveats: freely open only during the work afternoons; second textual source needed. Rank **Okay**. New place.
title: Ruijtergaard, an orchard that had to grow in crates

A small residents' park since 2005 on the site of a former school and the ramp to the rubbish barges, with a view of the Montelbaanstoren. Lead: Shaffy's Tuin walk 2025, item 3. Status: Sept 2025. heading: Sweep 2: public and community gardens / Nieuwmarkt/Lastage
text: **GR-15. Coentje Gans Plantsoen, a hidden garden for all child victims of war.** Pin 52.370200, 4.910000 (approximate; Foeliestraat, 20 to 30 m from the end of the Rapenburg, garden gate on the right). Ground that drained badly in the 1960s and that residents kept from being built on became a play garden in 2007. On 3 July 2021 poet and resident Adriaan Deurlo named it after Coenraad Gans (born 3 July 1941, murdered in Sobibór 21 May 1943), the youngest of the 14 Jews taken from the building, and for all children who are victims of war and violence. The gate looks shut but is never locked. Lead: Shaffy's Tuin walk 2025, item 4 (https://shaffystuin.nl/buitengewone-buurttuinen/). Status: kept by residents at their own cost, Sept 2025. Caveats: second source needed (Joods Monument for Coenraad Gans; joodsmonument.nl search did not answer to curl); pin approximate. Rank **Nice** (Amazing if confirmed). New place.
title: Coentje Gans Plantsoen, a hidden garden for all child victims of war

heading: Sweep 2: public and community gardens / Oostelijke Eilanden/Kadijken
text: **GR-16. Plukbos, the pick-your-own wood on Wittenburg.** Pin 52.372500, 4.920000 (approximate; the block between Kattenburgervaart, Grote Wittenburgerstraat, Jacob Burggraafstraat and Tweede Wittenburgerdwarsstraat). After three shootings in the neighbourhood a resident turned an abandoned dog field into an edible garden; Mayor Halsema opened it in 2018 on the hottest day of the year. A first cherry tree grew into a food forest of about 130 crops, open day and night: "Nergens verser, noch goedkoper." Garden day with lunch every second Sunday. Lead: Shaffy's Tuin walk 2025, item 9; second: plukbos.nl ("dag en nacht geopend voor stille buurtgenoten & voorbijgangers") and buurtorganisatie1018.nl agenda 9 Feb 2025. Status: active 2025. Caveat: pin approximate. Rank **Nice**. New place (DE mentions it only in passing).

text: **GR-17. The roof garden of the Laagte Kadijk.** Pin 52.370300, 4.912600 (approximate; up the steps right after the passage under the building by Café Bloem, Laagte Kadijk). A public garden on the roof of a 1987 garage, replanted by residents from 2005, open 24 hours; you cross it and come down the other stair onto the Laagte Kadijk, then go on to the Sibbelpark. Lead: Shaffy's Tuin walk 2025, item 6. Status: Sept 2025. Caveats: pin approximate; second source needed. Rank **Okay**. Group with the Sibbelwoningen draft (extra-east) or new place.

heading: Sweep 2: public and community gardens / Oostelijke Eilanden/Kadijken
text: **GR-18. Waaigat 2, a garden with viewing windows.** Pin 52.370300, 4.922200 (approximate; Waaigat, end of the Parelstraat). A former dog-walking lawn turned into a residents' garden around 2005, reachable from the street and by boat, with framed viewing windows that each give a new view; visitors are asked to go their own way in silence. Next to it, Waaigat 1 (about 1988) has a weeping willow planted at a child's birth (not public). Lead: Shaffy's Tuin walk 2025, item 8. Status: open 24 hours, Sept 2025. Caveats: pin approximate; second source needed. Rank **Okay**. Group with DE-18 Touwbaanpark (across the Touwbrug).

heading: Sweep 2: public and community gardens / Oostelijke Eilanden/Kadijken
text: **GR-19. Buurttuin Windroosplein, the garden instead of a basketball court.** Pin 52.373185, 4.924472 (Windroosplein, OSM way 282484810). Around 1992-93 the city planned a low-maintenance basketball court here; residents proposed a garden, about twenty of them built it, and it now holds more than 150 kinds of plants. A worm hotel for kitchen waste came in 2019. The gate is always open (close it behind you). Lead: Shaffy's Tuin walk 2025, item 10; second: buurtorganisatie1018.nl, "Wormenhotel op het Windroosplein" (14 June 2019). Status: Sept 2025. Rank **Okay**. Group with the lifeboat shed draft on the Windroosplein (eilanden-1) or new place.
